wiki.1girl: An image containing one female character.
wiki.2girls: An image containing two female characters. Male characters may also be present in addition to the female characters.
wiki.3girls: An image containing three female characters. Male characters may also be present in addition to the female characters.
wiki.4girls: An image containing four female characters. Male characters may also be present in addition to the female characters.
wiki.5girls: An image containing five female characters. Male characters may also be present in addition to the female characters.
wiki.1boy: An image depicting one male character.
wiki.2boys: An image depicting two male characters.
wiki.3boys: An image depicting three male characters.
wiki.solo: An image containing a single person. No one else should be visible in the image.
wiki.multiple girls: An image depicting two or more female characters. Male characters may also be present in addition to the female characters.
wiki.very short hair: Hair that is ear or jaw length, or even shorter. Very short hairstyles include the buzz cut, crew cut, and pixie cut.
wiki.short hair: Hair less than shoulder-length, typically around neck-length or shorter.
wiki.medium hair: Hair that is approximately shoulder-length. Hair longer than shoulder-length is long hair.
wiki.long hair: Hair longer than shoulder-length, up to waist-length. Shoulder-length hair should be tagged with medium hair instead.
wiki.very long hair: Hair longer than the waist, ranging to as far down as the feet.
wiki.absurdly long hair: Hair longer than the character's height. Rule of thumb is a character is able to stand on their own hair.
wiki.bob cut: A short haircut in which a weighted area is left to fall between the ears and chin; can often include blunt ends.
wiki.pixie cut: A women's hairstyle, cut very short (around cheek length or less) on the sides and back of the head, while slightly longer on top.
wiki.ponytail: A hairstyle in which the hair is tied at the back of the head with a hair tie, scrunchie, or similar device, and allowed to hang freely from that point.
wiki.high ponytail: A ponytail that is tied high up at the back of the head. Contrast with low ponytail.
wiki.side ponytail: A ponytail that is tied at the side of the head rather than the back. Akita Neru, Flandre Scarlet and Kaga (kancolle) are noted wearers of this style.
wiki.twintails: A hair style where the hair is tied into sections forming two ponytails. The Japanese term for this type of hair style is ツインテール (twin tail).
wiki.braid: For characters with a braid or braids in their hair. A braid is an interweaving of three or more locks of hair together.
wiki.twin braids: A hairstyle that consists of two braided lengths of hair.
wiki.messy hair: Very unkempt hair, either as a deliberate hair style or because of a lack of grooming, such as when just waking up in the morning or after sex. Often contains many loose hair strands or stray flyaway hairs. Sometimes associated with disheveled characters, such as jimiko or mojyo.
wiki.hair over one eye: Hair that covers either eye. Typically associated with shy or mysterious characters. For the case where both eyes are covered, use hair over eyes. Also tag one eye covered or eyes visible through hair as appropriate.
wiki.hair between eyes: A hair bunch from the bangs that falls over the middle of the forehead, long enough to reach at least between the eyes of the person.
wiki.sidelocks: Long locks of hair growing directly in front of the ears.
wiki.blunt bangs: A hairstyle where the bangs are cut in a sharp, straight line across the entire length of the forehead. Mutually exclusive with swept bangs and asymmetrical bangs.
wiki.swept bangs: Bangs that are combed loosely to one side or the other, usually with a less distinct part than side part.
wiki.ahoge: Literally "stupid hair", an ahoge is a single long lock of hair that sticks out of a character's head.
wiki.wavy hair: A type of hair which resembles waves.
wiki.straight hair: Hair that is straight, without any curls, curves, or waves.
wiki.curly hair: Hair that is coiled to create a curly effect.
wiki.hair bun: A hairstyle in which the hair is wrapped into a round bun.
wiki.double bun: A hairstyle in which the hair is wrapped into two round hair buns.
wiki.drill hair: Hair that is curled into conical, drill-shaped ringlets. If the hair is curled but not conical and pointy, it should be tagged ringlets instead. If the hair drills are only near the tips, use low drills.
wiki.floating hair: Hair that is blowing in the wind, floating in midair, or otherwise not being held down by gravity.
wiki.hair over shoulder: Hair that is resting over the shoulder rather than hanging down the back.
wiki.hime cut: A hairstyle consisting of long straight hair, blunt bangs, and sidelocks with blunt ends.
wiki.blonde hair: Hair that is colored blonde or yellow.
wiki.aqua hair: Hair that is colored blue-green. "Aqua" also covers teal and turquoise.
wiki.two-tone hair: Multicolored hair that consists of two distinct colors.
wiki.gradient hair: Multicolored hair that blends and gradually changes from one color to another.
wiki.streaked hair: Multicolored hair or two-tone hair where the majority of the hair is one color, while only one or multiple small streaks possess a different color or colors. Don't tag streaks as a full hair color, e.g. don't tag red streaks as red hair too.
wiki.colored inner hair: Hair that is a different color on the inside than on the outside.
wiki.brown eyes: A character with brown colored eyes.
wiki.blue eyes: A character with blue colored eyes.
wiki.green eyes: A character with green colored eyes.
wiki.red eyes: A character with red colored eyes.
wiki.yellow eyes: A character with yellow colored eyes.
wiki.pink eyes: A character with pink colored eyes.
wiki.purple eyes: A character with purple colored eyes.
wiki.orange eyes: A character with orange colored eyes.
wiki.aqua eyes: A character with blue-green colored eyes.
wiki.heterochromia: Eyes with different colored irises. Also called "odd eyes".
wiki.eyelashes: When a character's eyelashes are particularly noticeable or drawn with great detail.
wiki.long eyelashes: Eyelashes that are noticeably longer than normal, usually drawn as an exaggeration.
wiki.thick eyebrows: Eyebrows that are thicker than usual, roughly the thickness of a finger.
wiki.bags under eyes: Dark circles or puffiness directly under the eyes. This can occur for a number of reasons, but is often used to indicate stress, sleepiness, exhaustion, and/or to give characters a dark appearance.
wiki.tsurime: Eyes drawn with the top eyelid slanting inwards. This usually produces a strong, piercing look and is generally given to characters with forceful personalities (naturally, exceptions exist). Also known as a positive canthal tilt or slanted eyes.
wiki.tareme: Eyes drawn with the top eyelid slanted outwards, to the point where the outer corner of the eye is much lower than the inner corner.
wiki.mole: A small dark blemish on the skin. Sometimes known as a beauty mark.
wiki.mole under eye: A mole located just below someone's eye, also known as a "tear mole". Fashionable in Japan, surpassing the Marilyn Monroe-style beauty mark popular in Western pop culture.
wiki.freckles: Small brownish spots of melanin on the skin.
wiki.blush: A rosy color in the cheeks.
wiki.makeup: Any type of makeup worn on the face. See tag group:makeup.
wiki.lipstick: A makeup product used to apply color to the lips.
wiki.eyeshadow: A type of eye makeup. A colored powder applied to the eyelids to make the eyes stand out or look more attractive.
wiki.sweat: Beads of perspiration that form on the body from physical exertion. Use this tag for light to moderate sweating (more than one drop). For heavy sweating, use very sweaty.
wiki.shiny skin: Use when skin has a sheen of specular highlights, typically from moisture. → dark skin, pale skin
wiki.wet: Covered with water or a watery liquid. May also include large amounts of bodily fluids, such as sweat.
wiki.tan: Skin darkened due to exposure to the sun.
wiki.dark skin: Skin that is darker in tone than the usual Eurasian skin tone. Characters usually have this skin tone naturally, but sometimes have dark skin due to a tan, alternate coloring, etc.
wiki.pale skin: Skin that is significantly lighter in tone than the usual Eurasian skintone, or skin which appears "bleached," lacking in color. For characters with completely white skin, use white skin.
wiki.very dark skin: Skin that is even darker than dark skin.
wiki.tanlines: A division between natural and dark skin tone due to receiving a tan while wearing clothes. Commonly in a swimsuit-like shape, but there are other types.
wiki.collarbone: The horizontal bones beneath the neck, linking the shoulders with the breast bone.
wiki.navel: The belly button is showing. Usually goes with either stomach or midriff. Contrast with covered navel.
wiki.armpits: The area of the body located underneath where the arm connects to the torso, often appearing when one or both arms are raised, especially when wearing clothes that are sleeveless, strapless, have detached sleeves, have armpit cutouts, or if the character is topless female/topless male or outright nude.
wiki.midriff: When the stomach is left partially exposed by clothing.
wiki.toned: A character who has a toned or athletic build, but is not overly muscular.
wiki.muscular: A character with a bulky, muscular physique that must have come from extensive training, body building or otherwise.
wiki.plump: Slightly chubby, but not enough to be fat. A saying that goes around for plump is "Fat in all the right places".
wiki.skinny: Having significantly less body fat percentage than the norm and/or possessing a noticeably slender body frame (e.g. visible ribs).
wiki.long legs: Noticeably longer legs than average. As a rule of thumb, legs that are longer than the upper body.
wiki.tattoo: A permanent mark or design on the body made by putting ink under the skin using a tattoo machine.
wiki.scar: A mark left on the skin where a wound, cut, burn, or other injury healed.
wiki.body blush: Blushing of body parts other than the face due to embarrassment, heat, or otherwise.
wiki.steaming body: Steam that is visibly emanating from a character, rather than an environmental source. It may be because the character is hot and sweaty, or be used to emphasize the "steaminess" of an erotic scene.
wiki.body freckles: Freckles scattered across a character's body. If the freckles are only on the character's face, just use freckles.

wiki.against glass: Pressing against a pane of glass.
wiki.arched back: When someone's back forms an inverted arch by bending backward. The opposite of bent back, which is when someone bends forward.
wiki.head tilt: When a character tilts their head to one side, which is commonly done as either an inquisitive gesture, or a cute gesture, though it can be done for any reason.
wiki.leaning back: When a character who is either standing or sitting, leans backwards at the waist. Opposite of leaning forward.
wiki.contrapposto: Standing with the body's weight on one leg, with the hip cocked out.
wiki.standing on one leg: Balancing on one leg with the other off the ground.
wiki.ojou-sama pose: When a character strikes a hand-in-front-of-mouth pose, in the manner of a wealthy aristocratic young lady (an ojou-sama). Often accompanied by a haughty "OHOHOHO!" laugh.

wiki.index fingers together: When a character is poking the tips of their index fingers together.
wiki.looking at viewer: A character looking directly at the viewer, i.e. looking at the camera or through the fourth wall.
wiki.looking back: A character turning their head, body or eyes to look behind themselves.
wiki.looking down: Looking down, with the head bent down. See downturned eyes for when the eyes are looking down but the head is not bent down.
wiki.looking up: A character looking up, with their head bent back.
wiki.looking to the side: When a character's gaze is directed to something off to their side. This is most often eyes looking 90 degrees across the shoulder, but eyes looking up to 45 degrees in either direction from the shoulder are also included.
wiki.averting eyes: A character deliberately turning their gaze away from the viewer or another character. Often done out of shyness, embarrassment, or nervousness, but applies to anger and annoyance as well. Combine with a directional looking tag where applicable.
wiki.eye contact: Two characters looking directly into each others eyes. Not for when two people simply face each other, avert their eyes, or are looking at the viewer.
wiki.looking at another: When someone is looking at someone else. Use eye contact when two people look directly into each other's eyes.

wiki.upper body: An image of the upper body of the character, approximately from the waist up. This may or may not include the head.

wiki.close-up: An image in which the subject is shown at very close range.

wiki.from below: Perspective that has the viewer looking up toward a character.
wiki.from above: Looking at something/someone from above. The perspective has you looking down at a character.
wiki.from side: The main character or subject of the image is viewed from its side. The viewer's perspective may range from directly across the subject's shoulder (or equivalent) at a 90 degree angle to up to 45 degrees to the left or right of that point.
wiki.profile: When one side of the character's face is shown.

wiki.cherry blossoms: Small flowers of the cherry tree (sakura). Usually pink and often seen falling/scattered as petals.
wiki.starry sky: An image with a focus on a sky filled with star (sky)s. If it isn't a focal point, just tag as star (sky).
wiki.indoors: A scene set inside a building or other indoor location. The majority of the picture or its subjects should be in an enclosed location.
wiki.outdoors: A scene set in an outdoor location, rather than indoors. The setting may be urban or rural.
wiki.day: An image set during daytime, when the sun is out. The sky is usually blue.
wiki.night: The time of the day when it is dark. The sky is usually black or dark blue.
wiki.evening: Later part of the afternoon where the sun begins to set but before night has fallen.
wiki.sunset: The sun setting beneath the horizon in the evening. If the sun is no longer visible, tag it dusk instead.
wiki.sunrise: The sun crossing the horizon in the morning after dawn. If no sun is visible, tag it dawn or sunlight instead. Not to be confused with rising sun flag.
wiki.dusk: The time immediately after sunset where no sun is visible, but is close enough to the horizon to light up the sky. Typical hues of this time of day are orange, red, and purple.
wiki.overcast: When the sky is completely covered by clouds.
wiki.rain: Water that falls in drops from clouds in the sky.
wiki.snow: Precipitation consisting of crystalline ice, which falls in the winter during cold temperatures.
wiki.fog: A weather condition caused by clouds forming along either ground or water surface. Results in anywhere from slight to extremely reduced visibility.
wiki.steam: The visible vapor formed by hot water vapor condensing in colder air.
wiki.dim lighting: A scene that is dimly lit, but not completely dark.
wiki.moonlight: A pale, white to bluish light cast by the moon at night.
wiki.sunlight: The light of the sun. Use this tag when sunlight is emphasized in a post. Don't use this tag just because the post takes place during the day.
wiki.backlighting: The light source appears to be behind the subject of the image.
wiki.sidelighting: When the source of lighting in a picture comes from the side.
wiki.window light: Light coming out of a window when viewed from outside.
wiki.candlelight: Settings where candles provide the majority of ambient light. This makes for dark scenes with amber-colored light radiating out from the candles themselves.
wiki.spotlight: A beam of light that shines down over somebody. This usually happens during a stage performance as a focal point for spectators.
wiki.lamp: An indoor light fixture placed on a table or floor to illuminate a room or brighten a work space. Lamps typically have a lampshade or some other covering to diffuse the light.
wiki.shadow: Darkness caused by an object blocking light. This tag is for shadows that are especially strong, noticeable, or interesting.
wiki.depth of field: An effect where part of the image appears blurry and out-of-focus. This could be the foreground, the background, or both.
wiki.bokeh: A photographic effect where circular out-of-focus points of light appear in the background of the image.
wiki.chromatic aberration: An effect where the edges of an image have a colored, blurry halo or fringe. The RGB color channels appear noticeably offset from one another.
wiki.film grain: A grainy, sand-like texture that appears in traditional film photography. Artists sometimes simulate film grain for artistic effect, especially to achieve a cinematic or retro look.
wiki.bridge: An artificial structure built to cross obstacles (natural or otherwise). They consist of a road suspended or supported in the air by different means.
wiki.river: A large natural flowing body of water.
wiki.field: A stretch of land usually cultivated with crops or flowers.
wiki.market: An outdoors area featuring market stalls where sellers sell a wide range of items, including food and other goods.
wiki.festival: An event or community gathering, usually staged by a local community, which centers on some theme, usually a unique aspect of the community.
wiki.veranda: A roofed, open gallery or porch.
wiki.wooden floor: A floor that is comprised of wooden planks laid next to each other.
wiki.stone lantern: Known as ishidōrō in Japanese, they are often seen in Japanese temples, shrines, and gardens.
wiki.koi: A type of fish. Various colorful varieties of common carp used as decoration in ponds or water gardens.
wiki.noren: Japanese rectangular split doorway curtains, often used by shops, restaurants, and food stands.
wiki.fusuma: A flat paper sliding door or panel seen in traditional Japanese architecture.
wiki.rock garden: A small field or plot of land designed to feature and emphasize a variety of rocks, stones and boulders.
wiki.park bench: A bench which is specifically situated in a park. These benches are usually made of wood, and almost always have a backrest and a continuous seat along their entire length.
wiki.tavern: A medieval bar (place); a place where people gather to drink alcohol and be served food. A common location in fantasy settings.
wiki.bamboo forest: A forest made of bamboo. Commonly shown in the Touhou series as the Bamboo Forest of the Lost, which contains the palace estate Eientei and the homes of Fujiwara no Mokou, Imaizumi Kagerou, Wriggle Nightbug, and Mystia Lorelei.
wiki.rice paddy: A rice paddy is a flooded field where rice (plant) is grown. Very common in the Japanese countryside.
wiki.arch: An arch is a vertical curved structure that spans an elevated space and may or may not support the weight above it.
wiki.stone wall: A wall which is constructed from stones (in their natural-looking form) instead of bricks or concrete.
wiki.greco-roman architecture: Buildings or structures constructed in classical Greek or Roman style, or clearly inspired by such.
wiki.tower: A tall, narrow building or structure that may stand apart from or be attached to another building or structure.
wiki.windmill: A building with a large, wind-driven wheel, traditionally used to grind grain, pump water, or operate machinery.
wiki.paper lantern: A traditional Japanese or Chinese lantern made of thin, brightly colored paper.
wiki.bamboo: A tropical plant consisting of tall, green, tubular stems. It is technically a type of grass, but its woody tissue is as strong as timber, and the tallest species can grow to a height of nearly 100 feet (30 meters).
wiki.ballroom: A type of room used for elegant banquets and dancing.
wiki.carriage: A two- or four-wheeled horse-drawn vehicle for carrying passengers. Before the advent of motor vehicles, they were a common mode of transport in cities.
wiki.greenhouse: A greenhouse is normally characterized by the following: • A building largely made up out of framing and glass panels • A building that has been made economically and with an eye for keeping costs low.
wiki.cityscape: Scenery that represents the physical aspects of a city or urban area.
wiki.skyscraper: A large, continuously habitable building with multiple floors. In modern sources, the height of a skyscraper is defined as being at least 100 meters or 150 meters, but there is no universally accepted definition.
wiki.neon lights: Tube-style light fixtures named after and commonly filled with the gas neon. Typically paired with coatings that produce brighter colors, contrasting fluorescent lamps which are almost always white.
wiki.jeans: Pants made of denim, most commonly blue or grey in color.
wiki.t-shirt: A collarless casual upper garment derived from shirts intended to be worn underneath other clothing. They are traditionally short sleeved, but various sleeve lengths are now common.
wiki.hoodie: A pullover sweatshirt with an attached hood. Often features a drawstring for the hood and a front kangaroo pocket for both hands. If it has a zipper, it's a hooded jacket.
wiki.sneakers: Shoes designed for use in sporting activity, though commonly used as general purpose footwear. Known as trainers in British English, though the more old school style of sneakers would be known as plimsolls or pumps. Known as runners in Australia and Ireland, or tennis shoes in the United States.
wiki.business suit: A suit of clothes traditionally worn by business workers, all of the same fabric and color.
wiki.chinese clothes: Any variety of Chinese clothing, including traditional clothing, contemporary clothing, and clothing worn by martial artists.
wiki.hanfu: Historical styles of clothing worn by the Han Chinese before the mid-1600s. Most styles have a “y” shape collar, but there are also styles with a rounded collar.
wiki.ruqun: A set of attire in hanfu which consists of a short jacket worn under (tucked into) a long skirt.
wiki.tangzhuang: A tangzhuang (Simplified Chinese: 唐装) is a kind of pseudo-traditional Chinese jacket, typically with a mandarin collar.
wiki.qipao: A form-fitting, Chinese dress that has side slits up (usually) both legs and a mandarin collar.
wiki.china dress: A form-fitting, Chinese dress that has side slits up (usually) both legs and a mandarin collar.
wiki.east asian architecture: Buildings and other structures constructed in traditional East Asian design.
wiki.palace: A luxurious building typically delicated to upper class people (such as royalty or nobles). Occasionally, castle can also serve as a palace.
wiki.pagoda: A pagoda is the general term in the English language for a tiered tower with multiple eaves common in China, Japan, Korea, Vietnam, and other parts of Asia.
wiki.ancient greek clothes: Clothes of the Ancient Greek people during Classical Antiquity (8th century BC to 6th century AD), or garments styled after those clothes.
wiki.toga: A loose, sleeveless outer garment styled after clothing worn in ancient Rome. Togas are usually made of a single piece of white cloth that covers the whole body, except for the right arm.
wiki.laurel crown: A head wreath made of branches or leaves of the laurel plant. Laurel crowns are frequently associated with ancient Greece.
wiki.pillar: An upright shaft or structure used as building support or as a stand-alone monument.
wiki.temple: Generally, a place of worship other than a church, mosque, Shinto shrine or synagogue.
wiki.stone floor: A floor made out of stones.
wiki.ruins: Man-made constructions that once stood tall, but have broken and degraded due to being abandoned or destroyed. This includes overgrown post-apocalyptic ruins, ruins from the ancient past, and the ruins of present-day cities or buildings.
wiki.armor: A type of clothing made to protect the wearer. Armor is usually made from a hard material, often metal, but it can also be made from simple wood or leather.
wiki.plate armor: Armor that consists of solid, metal plates.
wiki.chainmail: Armor made from small metal rings linked together into a mesh. Also known as simply "mail" or "maille."
wiki.knight: A medieval soldier who wears full plate armor and who traditionally fights as cavalry on horseback. Knights were usually of noble birth and were granted the rank of knighthood after an apprenticeship as a squire.
wiki.castle: A large medieval building, fortified with thick walls, towers, and in many cases a moat.
wiki.throne: A usually decorated and cushioned chair where a ruler or a respectable person sits.
wiki.gothic architecture: A style of architecture which flourished during the high and late medieval period. Often associated with cathedrals.
wiki.kimono: A type of traditional Japanese clothing, consisting of a long, wide-sleeved robe, closed at the front forming a "y" shape. It is held closed with a wide belt-like sash called an obi. The sleeves can be tied back with tasuki.
wiki.japanese clothes: Any variety of traditional Japanese clothing. This excludes modern Japanese fashion, such as lolita fashion (except wa lolita) and school uniforms like serafuku and gakuran.
wiki.yukata: A light summer kimono, often worn to festivals and other special occasions. In other seasons, it is typically worn after a bath in an onsen.
wiki.hakama: Traditional Japanese clothing, looking like either a pleated skirt (a hakama skirt) or baggy, pleated pants (hakama pants). A traditional hakama has seven deep pleats, five in the front and two in the rear.
wiki.obi: An obi is a wide and long embroidered sash for a kimono. Also used to tie attire (usually a robe top) closed. It may have a cord called an obijime wrapped around it to hold it in place, and it may have an ornament called an obidome in the front but off to the side.
wiki.geta: Traditional Japanese sandals with a wooden sole raised off the ground by two teeth (called ha), and held onto the foot with a fabric thong (hanao). There is also a specific style called Tengu-geta, which has only a single peg in the middle.
wiki.japanese armor: Any type of traditional Japanese armor, typically worn by samurai.
wiki.torii: A Japanese gateway or arch often seen at Shinto shrines.
wiki.shouji: A paper sliding door or panel on a wooden lattice frame seen in traditional Japanese architecture.
wiki.tatami: Straw mats typically seen in Japanese homes.
wiki.victorian: Posts that pertain to, or are inspired by, elements of England's Victorian Era (1837-1901). Preceded by the Georgian and Regency eras (and before those, the Stuart, Elizabethan, and Tudor eras), and followed by the Edwardian and the modern pre-Elizabethian eras.
wiki.corset: A form-fitting garment, worn around the waist and fastened with laces.
wiki.gown: A formal dress that is longer and more elaborate in design than a typical casual dress, reaching ankle length (or sometimes all the way to the ground) and flaring out at the sides.
wiki.top hat: A hat with an elevated cap which is worn by people of high society or stage magicians.
wiki.waistcoat: A vest with buttons on front that is commonly worn over a dress shirt with necktie or bowtie (if applicable) and below a suit jacket or coat. It is a part of most formal wear, and as the third piece of the three-piece male business suit.
wiki.frills: A trimming, as a strip of cloth or lace, gathered at one edge and left loose at the other (AKA ruffles).
wiki.mansion: A very large sprawling dwelling house.
wiki.petticoat: A women's undergarment consisting of material draped from the waist and worn under a skirt or dress.
wiki.hoop skirt: A skirt worn over a series of hoops that make it spread out.
wiki.chemise: A loose-fitting women's top with thin spaghetti straps, usually ending past the waist, typically worn as sleepwear or lingerie.
wiki.suit pants: A style of formal or semi-formal pants. They are often designed to be worn with a matching suit jacket.
wiki.dress pants: A style of formal or semi-formal pants. They are often designed to be worn with a matching suit jacket.
wiki.loincloth: Any of several ancient styles of garment designed to cover the genitals. Usually made from a folded and tied length of cloth, sometimes held in place by a belt. If it has a dangling length of cloth hanging in front and/or or behind, that part is called, for Danbooru's purposes, a pelvic curtain.
wiki.cape: A sleeveless outer garment that is fastened around or behind the neck and worn on the back.
wiki.capelet: A small cape usually covering only the shoulders. They are usually worn during the colder months, and as such are commonly seen as part of Santa costumes. Also known as a mantle.
wiki.hooded cloak: A cloak with a hood that can be pulled over the head.
wiki.tabard: An open-sided overgarment worn over clothing or armor, originating in Europe in the late Middle Ages.
wiki.shawl: A long piece of cloth, either square, rectangular, or triangular, used to drape over the upper part of the body, usually at the shoulders. May optionally be fastened together at the front with a brooch or similar item.
wiki.tailcoat: A coat with the front part cut to waist-length so it's shorter than the back which goes down to knee-length or lower. Often features lapels and worn in formal events. Some may include coattails.
wiki.uchikake: A highly formal over-kimono. Uchikake is not to be worn with an obi but is instead worn over a complete kimono outfit with obi.
wiki.mandarin collar: A short, unfolded, stand up–style high collar on a Chinese shirt, jacket, or dress.
wiki.side slit: A cutout slit along the side of the legs in a dress or skirt.
wiki.layered clothes: An outfit that consists of multiple overlapping layers of separate items of clothing. For example, a jacket worn over a cardigan.
wiki.fountain: An ornamental structure that shoots jets of water into the air.
wiki.lantern: A portable light source, designed to be carried or hung up, typically with an enclosure to protect it from the wind when used outdoors.
wiki.oil lamp: An ancient form of lighting. The most basic oil lamps are simple clay cups filled with oil into which a wick is dipped. Later oil lamps are more ornate and made of materials such as bronze or silver (think of the "magic lamp" from Arabian Nights).
wiki.torch: A rod-shaped object, bearing fire, used for illumination. Usually the end is soaked or wrapped in flammable material like pitch or oil-soaked rags to act as the fuel source, though some wooden torches are depicted as burning the wood itself (a difficult and bad idea in real life).
wiki.bonfire: An large and controlled outdoors fire made by creating a pile of flammable materials and igniting them. Associated with camping, protest, execution, and roasted sweet potato.
wiki.incense burner: A container made for burning incense. Also known as a censer. They vary greatly in size, form, and material of construction.
wiki.incense: Aromatic material (powder, stick, coil, cone, paper or rope...) that releases fragrant smoke when burned. Incense is used in therapy, meditation, religious ceremony and insectifuge...
wiki.hand fan: A tool used to move air towards oneself and cool oneself. It's commonly used when it's hot.
wiki.scroll: A long, often rolled up piece of paper typically depicted with writing on it.
wiki.calligraphy: The art of producing beautiful handwriting, using ink and a special pen or calligraphy brush. In East Asia, calligraphy is a traditional form of art.
wiki.guqin: A seven-string Chinese musical instrument of the zither family with a horizontal sounding board. It looks like a smaller koto (instrument) or guzheng, but lacks both frets and the movable bridges under the strings.
wiki.erhu: A violin-like Chinese musical instrument with two strings and a hexagonal resonator. Its bow is attached to the two strings and can never be separate from the instrument itself.
wiki.teapot: A container with a lid, spout, and handle, in which hot water is poured to steep tea leaves and from which the tea is then poured from. Often part of a tea set.
wiki.teacup: A cup traditionally used to hold tea and other hot beverages. They're typically short and made of ceramic, with a rounded base and a handle. They're often depicted alongside saucers, teapots, and tea sets.
wiki.folding screen: Furniture composed of several joined panels connected by hinges originated in China.
wiki.lotus: An aquatic plant belonging to the Nelumbonaceae family of flowering plants. The lotus has prominent blooms (of pink or white hues) rising 8-12 inches above the water, each with a flattened central seed pod structure and fully circular leaves with centrally-attached stems.
wiki.chrysanthemum: A popular plant of the daisy (flower) family, having brightly colored ornamental flowers and existing in many cultivated varieties.
wiki.willow: A tree or shrub of temperate climates that grows near water. It has long, thin branches that hang down like curtains and narrow, lance-shaped leaves sprouting along their lengths. Commonly featured in Eastern-themed settings.
wiki.pine tree: Trees in the genus Pinus in the family Pinaceae, they are evergreen trees meaning that their shrubs stay green even in winter.
wiki.silk: Strong protein fibers, sometimes coated with adhesive, produced by certain arthropods and monsters. Examples of its use in nature include insect cocoons and spider webs.
wiki.beads: A small piece of glass, stone, or similar material, typically rounded and perforated for threading with others as a necklace, bracelet or rosary, or for sewing onto fabric.
wiki.banner: A vertical flag; a piece of cloth bearing a symbol, logo, slogan, or other message that is oriented vertically instead of horizontally. Can also be used for birthday banners or other fabrics that shouldn't be called flags. Soldiers may carry a war banner.
wiki.spear: A type of polearm consisting of a sharp point or blade at the end of a long shaft, traditionally for thrusting. One of the most common polearms.
wiki.polearm: A melee weapon with the blade on the end of a long shaft.
wiki.shield: A flat and broad piece of armor carried in the hand or worn on the forearm to defend against attacks.
wiki.drum: A percussion instrument consisting of a hollow cylinder or hemisphere with a membrane stretched tightly over one or both ends, played by beating with the hands or drumsticks.
wiki.horse: A large four-legged animal, commonly used for horseback riding, racing, or as a beast of burden.
wiki.table: A piece of furniture with a flat horizontal upper surface.
wiki.fireplace: The part of a chimney that opens into a room and in which fuel is burned.
wiki.chandelier: An ornate lighting fixture that hangs from a ceiling.
wiki.candelabra: The traditional term for a set of multiple decorative candlesticks, each of which often holds a candle on each of multiple arms or branches connected to a column or pedestal. A single member of such a set is known as a candelabrum.
wiki.lamppost: Fixed, outdoor lighting intended to illuminate a street at night. Use this for gas or electric lighting.
wiki.battlefield: A field where a battle took or is taking place.
wiki.pond: A small body of standing water, smaller than a lake.
wiki.altar: An altar is a table or platform adorned, decorated with religious imagery and items for the presentation of religious offerings and rituals. It is found in places of worship like churches and temples. • For the non-Christian, miniature household version, use kamidana instead.
wiki.samurai: A feudal Japanese warrior who wears traditional Japanese armor. Often wielding traditional Japanese weaponry, like the katana, nagamaki, naginata, ootachi, tachi (weapon), tantou, wakizashi, yari, or yumi (bow).
wiki.ninja: A ninja (Chinese term) or shinobi (Japanese term) is a Japanese covert agent/mercenary specialized in underhanded fighting and espionage. A female ninja is called a kunoichi.
wiki.oiran: A traditional Japanese courtesan in Edo (present-day Tokyo), the Yoshiwara. They were a much higher-class subtype of yuujo, the iconic feudal-era Japanese prostitutes.
wiki.onmyouji: A practitioner of Onmyoudou, a traditional Japanese esoteric cosmology that is a mixture of natural science and occultism.
wiki.viking: Ancient Nordic or Scandinavian warriors who raided and pillaged across Europe from the 8th to the 11th centuries. Often associated with horned helmets, axes, and scale armor.
wiki.witch: A person, usually female, who utilizes the gift of magic.
wiki.gladiator: A warrior who fights (often unwillingly) as a form of mass entertainment, in a colosseum or other arena.
wiki.monk: A character who is a member of a religious order and lives in a monastery, usually celibate male. He usually lives his life in prayer and contemplation. The concept is ancient and can be seen in many religions like Christianity (mainly Catholicism and Orthodoxy), Buddhism, etc.. The female counterpart is nun.
wiki.priest: A person having the authority or power to administer religious rites; in particular, rites of sacrifice to, and propitiation of, a deity or deities. Their office or position is the priesthood, a term which may also apply to such persons collectively.
wiki.priestess: A female priest. Can be depicted in various ways, whether wearing the habit of male priests, as generic fantasy priest(esse)s, as nuns, etc.
wiki.blacksmith: A person who forges metal into various shapes (such as tools, furniture, nail (hardware)s, and weapons). They would typically use tools such as hammer, anvil, tongs, and forge (furnace for heating metals) as well as an apron for protection.
wiki.princess: The daughter of a king. The male equivalent is a prince.
wiki.dancer: A person wearing the attire of a dancer. A dancer is one who dances in front of a large crowd, often wearing clothing that will show off their body, and a variety of accessories, including jewelry, circlets, and veils.
wiki.butler: The title was originally entitled to the person who had the charge of the wine cellar and dispensed liquors. Today it is mostly known as a male servant to a wealthy person.
wiki.detective: A person who investigates crimes and looks into records. They are either employed by the police or by a private individual. Police detectives are commonly depicted with a police badge.
wiki.barmaid: A waitress that works in a bar (place) or tavern, usually seen carrying beer mugs, and in more medieval or fantasy settings.
wiki.grapes: A small, round, smooth-skinned edible fruit, usually purple, red, or green.
wiki.wine glass: A drinking glass with a footed stem and a wide round bowl, designed for drinking wine.
wiki.lyre: A small stringed musical instrument, similar to a harp, but handheld rather than resting on the floor. It has with strings fixed to a crossbar. They're often U-shaped, but can come in various appearances. They're often associated with ancient Greece.
wiki.statue: A lifelike free-standing sculpture usually depicting a human, animal, or deity. Statues memorializing specific historical figures are particularly common. Statues vary in scale from life-size to colossal proportions. Small-scale statues are known as statuettes.
wiki.olive: The small oval fruit of the olive tree, the olive is seen as green, black, or brown, with a red pit.
wiki.trident: A type of polearm that ends with three prongs. Typically used for fishing, but also used by aquatic or demonic beings.
wiki.pocket watch: A watch kept in one's pocket instead of being worn on one's wrist. Usually accompanied by a watch fob.
wiki.cane: A long, sometimes curved stick used as an aid to walking or as a fashion accessory, which usually runs around the length of a person's leg.
wiki.birdcage: A birdcage is a cage designed to house birds as pets. For tagging purposes this is a cage that has a flat circular bottom and a round top, usually with a hook at the top for hanging.
wiki.piano: A musical instrument played by means of a keyboard whose sound is produced by felt hammers striking metallic strings. Widely used in Classical music for solo performances.
wiki.violin: A musical instrument of the string family. Basically it consists of a formed, resonating box over which are suspended a fingerboard and four tightened strings. The player holds the larger end under the chin and the opposite end in the hand.
wiki.lace: Clothing made entirely of lace. Lace is a delicate fabric, usually colored white, containing intricate web-like patterns.
wiki.rose: A type of flower associated with romance, and it is a traditional gift given to a loved one. Each color a rose can be in has specific symbolism as well.
wiki.clock: A device that shows the time. A traditional analog clock uses rotating hands showing hours, minutes, and seconds, while a digital clock uses a numeric display.
wiki.breasts: An image where the breasts are noticeable.
wiki.hetero: Any romantic and/or sexual depiction between members of the opposite genders, regardless of if it's mutual or one-sided or if the male is a trap and the female is a reverse trap.
wiki.male pubic hair: Pubic hair on a male character.
wiki.thighs: The upper part of the legs. Use this tag when the thighs are especially noticeable or prominent.
wiki.girl on top: For any situation (not necessarily sexual) where a girl is on top of another character.
wiki.tongue: When the tongue is decently visible, well defined, or particularly prominent.
wiki.bare shoulders: When the shoulders are exposed, as part of clothing design, pulling/falling down, or other. Bare shoulders are especially prominent in clothes that are sleeveless, strapless, or worn off shoulder.

wiki.on bed: Sitting or lying on a bed or futon.
wiki.ass: The buttocks, the round fleshy part of the human body at the back of the hips, on which a person sits.
wiki.sky: When the sky is a focal point, the main subject, or used as a background.
wiki.teeth: Small, whitish structures found inside one's jaw. Teeth are used to bite, to break down food before they are swallowed, and many other functions including self-defense.
wiki.female pubic hair: Pubic hair on a female character.
wiki.closed mouth: The lips held together and not showing any interior portion of the mouth.
wiki.pillow: A pillow is used to sleep on and support the head/neck or other parts of the body while sleeping, lying down or sitting.
wiki.closed eyes: When a character has both eyes closed. If one eye is open, use one eye closed.
wiki.single hair bun: A hairstyle where the hair is wrapped into a single round hair bun.
wiki.water: A clear, colorless, tasteless liquid with chemical formula H₂O, vital to most life on Earth.
wiki.long sleeves: Sleeves that cover the arms to at least the wrists.
wiki.oral: Any kind of stimulation of a persons' genitals with the tongue or mouth.
wiki.parted bangs: Bangs that are parted in the middle or to one side.
wiki.saliva: A liquid produced in the mouth of most animals.
wiki.curtains: Sheets of cloth used for privacy and to block light, usually hung over windows.
wiki.curtain: Sheets of cloth used for privacy and to block light, usually hung over windows.
wiki.clothed male nude female: A picture where the male is wearing clothing, but the female is nude.
wiki.pregnant: The state of having a baby growing in the uterus.
wiki.group sex: Any sex act involving more than two participants at the same time. This can be a single person with multiple partners (as in a threesome or gangbang), or multiple couples having sex together (as in an orgy).
wiki.ring: Jewelry consisting of a circlet designed to be worn on the finger. Often made of precious metals such as gold or silver and set with gems, but can be any material and style.
wiki.tree: A large plant with a tall wooden trunk dividing into small branches ending in leaves.
wiki.tears: The fluid produced by the eyes, oftentimes (though not always) when crying or laughing.
wiki.squatting cowgirl position: A variation of cowgirl position where the person on top rides their partner while squatting with their feet on the ground, rather than kneeling as in normal cowgirl position. wiki.threesome: A form of group sex involving exactly three people at the same time.
wiki.mixed-sex bathing: People of different genders sharing a bath or shower, innocently or otherwise.
wiki.pink nails: Fingernails and/or toenails that are colored pink.
wiki.sex toy: A toy or device used for personal sexual purposes. Sex toys are usually designed for masturbation, but they may also be used with a partner.
wiki.sex toys: A toy or device used for personal sexual purposes. Sex toys are usually designed for masturbation, but they may also be used with a partner.
wiki.clothed female nude male: An image where the female is wearing clothes, but the male is nude. This is sometimes used to imply dominance.
wiki.candle: An object made of wax with a string running from top to bottom which is set alight. Its most common shape is cylindrical.
wiki.clitoris: A female sexual organ, the primary female erogenous zone. Usually refers specifically to the clitoral glans, a little pink button on top of the vulva.
wiki.wedding ring: A ring on the ring finger of the left hand, or a ring that is otherwise obviously a wedding ring, e.g. one used for a marriage proposal.
wiki.bed sheet: A sheet of cloth put on the bed that you can either sleep on or under.
wiki.collared shirt: A shirt with a folded collar. This includes dress shirts and other less formal kinds of shirts.
wiki.blue shirt: Any style of shirt that's colored blue.

wiki.feet out of frame: Like full body, except both of the character's feet are outside of the image. Part of the character's shins may be cropped out as well, but their knees should be within the image. Compare with cowboy shot.
wiki.looking ahead: A character looking directly in front of themselves, and not at the viewer. Looking ahead is relative to the character's front, not the viewer's perspective. If they are looking at viewer, use that instead.
wiki.sideways glance: Looking out of the corner of the eye, usually looking to the side or looking back.
wiki.looking at breasts: Looking at someone's breasts or flat chest, usually out of envy or awe.
wiki.frown: A facial expression used to indicate a variety of negative emotions, including displeasure, disapproval, annoyance, or general unhappiness.
wiki.light smile: A gentle or subtle smile, similar to that of the Mona Lisa. This tag is considered distinct from smile to help distinguish the two.
wiki.expressionless: When a character's face lacks any emotion or expression. Different from serious, where there is a reason for anger or determination, such as a battle or a death. Here, the character is stoic for no apparent reason.
wiki.pout: The protruding of the lips to one side to show displeasure.
wiki.angry: A person who is mad or upset. Especially evident when an anger vein is present, or when the character is glaring.
wiki.sad: To be affected with or expressive of grief or unhappiness.
wiki.crying: The act of shedding tears. Typically due to the subject experiencing emotional event, especially sadness.
wiki.drooling: When saliva leaks from the mouth.
wiki.saliva drip: When saliva leaks from the mouth.
wiki.moaning: A long, low sound expressing physical or mental suffering or sexual pleasure. Tagged when it appears someone is moaning (aided by sound effects in the art, or even hearing it audibly).
wiki.clenched teeth: Teeth that are tightly pressed together.
wiki.sparkling eyes: When a character's eyes contain star-shaped sparkles in them, adjacent to the pupil. Usually indicates excitement.
wiki.empty eyes: Eyes with no glint or light spots, or that are colored with solid, dull shading.
wiki.sleepy: Feeling the need to sleep, either at the end of the day or when waking up in the morning.
wiki.serious: A character with a serious or solemn demeanor or expression. Usually appears less relaxed than expressionless, or provided with context such as an impending battle or someone's death.
wiki.happy: Feeling or showing joy, contentment, or pleasure. Usually, this effect is achieved by laughter or a wide, open-mouth smile.
wiki.surprised: Feeling or showing surprise because something unexpected happened.
wiki.scared: A character who is in an emotional state of fear.
wiki.smug: Exhibiting great satisfaction with oneself or with one's situation. This may be to the point of being overly confident or cocky, much to the annoyance of others (until, that is, one's cockiness backfires and results in failure).
wiki.nervous: Appearing or acting unsteady, erratic, or irregular. Usually the character is trembling, blushing, or sweating because they have something to say to someone they like.
wiki.upright straddle: Straddling another person face-to-face while that person is sitting upright. May involve a leg lock. In the Kama Sutra, this position is known as the Lotus Blossom position.
wiki.reverse upright straddle: A sex position in which the receiving partner sits on the penetrating partner's lap while facing away, getting penetrated from behind.
wiki.reverse suspended congress: A sex position in which a person is held in midair while being penetrated from behind.
wiki.piledriver (sex): A sex position where the receiving partner is placed on their shoulders with their legs folded back and their hips lifted vertically in the air, while their partner squats and penetrates them from above.
wiki.boy on top: When a male is on top of someone else, which doesn't always have to be sexual.
wiki.thigh sex: A sex act in which a person rubs their penis in between their partner's closed thighs. Also known as intercrural or interfemoral sex, or sometimes by the Japanese term 'sumata' (すまた).
wiki.frottage: Rubbing the genitals against another person's body, while nude or clothed.
wiki.reverse spitroast: An act of group sex similar to spitroast, except that instead of one man (at least) at each end of a woman, there is one woman (at least) at each end of a third partner. Not to be confused with male spitroast.
wiki.bathing: The act of washing the body in a bath, usually in a bathtub, bathroom, or onsen, with the body partially submerged in some fluid.
wiki.showering: The act of taking a shower. Usually within a shower room, but may also be used for characters caught in a rainstorm.
wiki.swimming: Movement through water using one's arms and legs.
wiki.wading: Standing or walking in water less than waist deep.
wiki.floating: Moving or hovering in midair, seemingly without the help of an outside propulsion system (i.e wings).
wiki.partially submerged: Standing in water more than waist deep, or lying, sitting, or kneeling in shallow water.
wiki.washing hair: The act of cleaning hair with soap or shampoo. A character can wash their own hair, or another character might wash it for them. A child will often be depicted wearing a shampoo hat while having their hair washed.
wiki.splashing: When a liquid (usually water) is splashed around. Often comes from one's hands or feet, from something falling into a liquid and from naturally-occurring waves.
wiki.after bathing: Character has just left bathing in a shower, a bathtub, onsen or the like. Drying, using towel, wearing a bathrobe or being in various states of undress are common.
wiki.shared bathing: People sharing a bath or shower, innocently or otherwise.
wiki.bathhouse: A communal bathing space, typically known in Japan as 銭湯 (sentou).
wiki.ofuro: A traditional wooden Japanese bath with steep square sides. Sometimes freestanding, but not always.
wiki.bubble bath: A bath containing many bubbles, most likely caused by some sort of soap or a bath bomb.
wiki.shower head: A handheld or fixed device used to spray water for showering.
wiki.soap bubbles: Soap that has been foamed and slathered over the body during bathing.
wiki.towel: A large piece of absorbent fabric used for wiping or drying the body. Often features in bath, onsen, and beach scenes.
wiki.innertube: A type of recreational swim ring used to float in the water, especially by young children and people who cannot swim. So called because it resembles (and in earlier times, usually was) the inner tube of a car tire.
wiki.drinking: Consuming any type of drink or beverage.
wiki.reading: Reading a book, scroll, manga (object), magazine (object), newspaper, or other printed material.
wiki.cooking: The act of preparing food by preparing ingredients, then using different heating methods to cook it into a huge variety of different meals and dishes. Failure may result in bad food.
wiki.shopping: Going to a shop and browsing around for desired items to purchase, sometimes with a shopping cart, shopping basket or shopping bag in hand.
wiki.singing: The act of producing musical sounds with the voice.
wiki.karaoke: A form of entertainment done by amateur singers who sing along to pre-recorded instrumental versions of popular songs with the lyrics displayed on a video screen and timed by moving animation. Maracas and Tambourines are often used.
wiki.playing games: A person playing any type of game.
wiki.playing video games: A character playing a video game.
wiki.playing sports: A sport being played by someone.
wiki.studying: The act of researching information or doing school homework in order to expand one's knowledge.
wiki.writing: Using a pen, pencil, or other implement to mark words on a surface, typically paper.
wiki.drawing (action): A character actively creating a picture with a pencil, pen, crayons, markers, or other similar implement.
wiki.painting (action): When a character is engaged in the activity of painting.
wiki.stretching: Stretching one's limbs or body, usually to loosen muscles or to alleviate cramps. Often performed before or after exercising, or while yawning after waking up.
wiki.yoga: A commonly known generic term for physical, mental, and spiritual disciplines which originated in ancient India.
wiki.exercising: Any kind of activity that involves moving the body around in order to stay fit and/or lose weight.
wiki.exercise: Any kind of activity that involves moving the body around in order to stay fit and/or lose weight.
wiki.training: When character is seen practicing something to improve either their strength, reflexes, or certain skills such as combat, entertainment, or magic.
wiki.fishing: As a verb, it is the act of catching fish. As a noun, fishing refers to the recreational sport. Most examples of fishing on Danbooru are of the type performed with a fishing rod and baited hook, but methods of fishing vary widely, from fishing with nets to fishing with solar guns and harpoons (spearfishing) to the use…
wiki.camping: A recreational activity where people set up tents in outdoors locations and go out to enjoy nature or the scenery. The evenings typically comprise of cooking (e.g. grilling) food and socializing around a campfire.
wiki.picnic: A leisurely activity mainly composed of eating outdoors, ideally within a beautiful landscape.
wiki.hiking: A long, vigorous walk done in the outdoors as a recreational activity, usually on trails or foot paths in nature.
wiki.sunbathing: To sit or lie in the sun, especially to tan the skin.
wiki.smoking: Burning a substance like tobacco and either inhaling or tasting the smoke it emits. This can be done with cigarettes, cigars, pipes, hookah, bong and kiseru. Illegal recreational drugs like marijuana, cocaine and methamphetamine can be smoked as well.
wiki.cleaning: The act of making something clean.
wiki.talking on phone: Someone using a phone to converse with another person on the other end of the line.
wiki.selfie: Using a camera or cellphone to take a picture or video of oneself.
wiki.taking picture: Taking a photograph of something, whether with a camera or a cellphone.
wiki.driving: When a character is in control of a vehicle or a ride that doesn't include pushing or pulling it, such as steering a car, piloting a mecha, or holding the reins of the horse pulling their cart.
wiki.horseback riding: Riding a horse or horse-like creature. This includes unicorns, pegasuses, centaurs, hippogriffs, donkeys, mechanical horses on carousels, and people pretending to be horses.
wiki.riding bicycle: Riding a bicycle while it is moving.
wiki.tennis: A racket sport played between two players (singles) or between two teams of two players each (doubles). Each player uses a tennis racket to strike a tennis ball over a net into his opponent's court.
wiki.soccer: A team sport played between two teams of eleven players using a soccer ball. The object of the game is to score by driving the ball into the opposing goal.
wiki.badminton: A racket sport played by volleying a shuttlecock back and forth over a high narrow net with a long-handled badminton racket.
wiki.table tennis: Table tennis, also known as ping-pong, is a sport in which two or four players hit a table tennis ball (also known as a ping-pong ball) back and forth across a table using table tennis paddles. A common feature seen in ryokan (traditional Japanese inns).
wiki.boxing: The sport of boxing, in which fighters punch each other to either achieve a knockout or win by referee decision.
wiki.track and field: A category of sports that involves various running, jumping and throwing competitions, such as short- or long-distance running, pole vaulting, shotput, discus throwing, high jumping and others. There are also mixed events where participants compete in different events and accumulate points based on their performance.
wiki.golf: A game played on a large open-air course, in which a small hard ball is struck with a club into a series of small holes in the ground, the object being to use the fewest possible strokes to complete the course.
wiki.archery: The practice of shooting an arrow (projectile) using a bow (weapon). Either as a form of combat or as a recreational sport.
wiki.nurse: A health care professional who assists doctors and other health care professionals in the treatment of sick and injured people.
wiki.doctor: A licensed medical physician who cares for the sick and injured at a hospital, working alongside nurses. Other duties include performing physical examinations, performing surgeries, giving x-rays, and prescribing medication.
wiki.teacher: A person who teaches students in a school.
wiki.waitress: A person wearing a waitress uniform, regardless of gender.
wiki.barista: A person who serves behind the counter in a cafe.
wiki.salaryman: A Japanese businessman or male office worker.
wiki.policewoman: Someone wearing a female police uniform, regardless of gender. May feature female service cap, pencil skirt, handcuffs and a handgun.
wiki.flight attendant: A crew member who provides services for passengers aboard aircraft. Also known as cabin crew, steward/stewardess, or air host/air hostess.
wiki.idol: A young entertainer who performs through a combination of singing and dancing, usually while wearing very showy or frilly idol clothes.
wiki.nurse cap: A hat worn by female nurses, sometimes adorned with a cross. The cap's original purpose was to keep the nurse's hair neatly in place and present a modest appearance. It all but disappeared by the late 1980s with the near universal adoption of medical scrubs.
wiki.idol clothes: Clothes worn by idols for performances, particularly common in j-pop. These are usually frilly dresses for female idols and dapper suits with accessories for male idols, and are often impractical for being worn outside of performance events.
wiki.blazer: A type of jacket resembling a suit jacket, but cut more casually, usually worn as part of a school uniform. Oftentimes features lapels.
wiki.sportswear: Clothes that characters wear to play sports.
wiki.helmet: A protective piece of armor designed to protect the head from damage. The design and shape can vary because of the time-period, setting, and what the helmet is to protect the head from.
wiki.stethoscope: A medical device used to listen to the internal sounds of the body, especially the lungs and heart (organ). It is also used to listen to the stomach and intestines and blood flow in arteries and veins. In combination with a blood pressure monitor, it can be used for measurements of blood pressure.
wiki.clipboard: A small board with a clip on the top to fasten a bunch of papers together. It is a practical way to do writing on the go for professionals such as researchers, doctors and restaurant servers.
wiki.condom: A (usually) latex sheath worn over the penis during sex to prevent pregnancy or the spread of sexually transmitted diseases.
wiki.used condom: A condom that has been used and usually left filled with cum. Many times left tied.
wiki.condom in mouth: A person holding a condom in their mouth, either still in the wrapper or already used. Usually a precursor or invitation towards sexual activity. Occasionally the condom is applied via fellatio.
wiki.condom wrapper: Sealed package containing a condom. Can also apply to an opened package.
wiki.dildo: An artificial replica of a penis used as a sex toy for masturbation. Some can also serve as a vibrator, or be attached to a strap-on.
wiki.gangbang: A group of three or more people having sex with a single person.
wiki.netorare: A fetish in which someone close to the protagonist is either willingly or unwillingly seduced and stolen away. This isn't necessarily limited to one's lover, but may also include friends, unrequited love interests, or even relatives.
wiki.cheating (relationship): Having sex or a romantic relationship with someone other than one's regular partner in a monogamous relationship. When this happens among married people, this is known as adultery. This can also apply to meeting another without the regular partner knowing.
wiki.groping: Touching or fondling another person in a sexual way, usually the breasts or ass.

wiki.voyeurism: Watching some else have sex or engage in other intimate activities such as undressing, showering, masturbating, or going to the bathroom.
wiki.recording: Video recording taking place in the picture. Commonly demonstrated by framing the picture in a viewfinder, or by putting ●REC or アナログ (analog) in the top left or right corners.
wiki.object insertion: An inanimate object inserted into the vagina, anus, or even urethra.
wiki.breastfeeding: The act of suckling milk from a breast.
wiki.afterglow: As in "basking in the afterglow" - the warm, glowing feeling of bliss that lingers following orgasm after engaging in happy sex.
wiki.carrying: Supporting something or someone, usually with one's arms. Carrying something should require more effort than simply holding it in one's hand.
wiki.against window: A character is pressing against any part of the window. This includes the window frame and windowsill.
wiki.trembling: A reflex motion caused by cold, fear, nervousness, or excitement. It can also denote instability.
wiki.looking around: The act of someone turning their face from side to side to look around, be alert, or check what is on either side of them. It is often accompanied by afterimage or motion lines because the turning of the face from side to side must be specifically described.
wiki.furrowed brow: When the skin on the forehead (the brow) becomes creased due to concentration or anxiety.
wiki.dazed: When a character is stunned or dizzy, unable to think clearly and their vision is sometimes blurred due to the impact.
wiki.size difference: An image that focuses heavily on the size difference between two or more people; often minigirl, miniboy, giantess, and giant male pictures fall into this category.
wiki.fitness gym: An indoor facility with exercise machines where people go to exercise, lift weights, or otherwise work out. Commonly known by names such as health club, fitness center, and weight room.
wiki.school gym: An indoor facility with a large open sports court where sports are played, such as basketball (sport), indoor volleyball (sport), or wrestling. Physical education classes are held here in schools, and if equipped with a stage or bleachers also school assemblies.
wiki.hospital: A facility where doctors and nurses provide treatment for sick or injured people.
wiki.locker: A type of storage compartment with a lock that is usually used to store clothing, equipment, or books.
wiki.mirror: A polished surface used to view reflections.
wiki.full-length mirror: A mirror tall enough that it shows the user's entire reflection from head to feet. A full-length mirror may be free-standing with a base that holds it upright, or it may be affixed to a wall as is usual with smaller mirrors.
wiki.tissue box: A box with a hollow in the top that has a plastic cover with a slit through the center. Tissues are folded and placed in the box so that they can be pulled out one by one through the slit.
wiki.airplane interior: A scene set inside an aircraft. This could be in the passenger area or the cockpit.
wiki.airport: A location where aircraft such as airplanes, helicopters, or dirigibles takeoff and land.
wiki.cockpit: A cockpit (also called flight deck in big airplanes) is the area, usually near the front of a vehicle, from which its pilot controls it.
wiki.bus interior: A scene set inside a bus.
wiki.movie theater: A place that works like a theater, except visitors watch movies instead of live performances.
wiki.amusement park: A large park with a variety of thrill rides, games, and other attractions. They generally cater to a much wider age group than children's playgrounds. There is some overlap between the attractions at amusement parks and those found at festivals and traveling carnivals, but amusement parks tend to be permanent installat…
wiki.ferris wheel: An amusement park or fairground ride consisting of a giant vertical revolving wheel with passenger cars suspended on its outer edge.
wiki.zoo: A facility where wild animals are kept and exhibited to the public.
wiki.convenience store: A retail shop that carries a limited selection of basic items, as packaged foods and drugstore items, and is open long hours for the convenience of shoppers.
wiki.supermarket: A large self-service retail shop that sells food and household goods.
wiki.internet cafe: A cafe that charges a fee for internet, computer usage, or both. Also known as a cybercafe.
wiki.prison: An institution that incarcerates lawbreakers for a specific time as deemed by the justice system. The intention is to remove them from society and have them learn from their mistakes before being released. Serious offenders serve longer sentences for the purpose of making the public safer.
wiki.construction site: The location where construction workers do their job of building a facility from the ground up.
wiki.casino: An institution designed for gambling. Employees are hired to deal in various games of chance such as poker, blackjack (game) or roulette.
wiki.nightclub: An entertainment facility open during nighttime hours. They usually serve food and alcohol, and provide music and space for dancing floor shows.
wiki.laboratory: An institution where scientists and researchers work on experiments and long-term studies. Different branches of science thus have different types of laboratories.
wiki.church: The Christian place of worship. Can also apply for its interior.
wiki.farm: An area of land that is devoted primarily to agricultural processes with the primary objective of producing food and other crops.
wiki.barn: A type of building found on farms used to store agricultural equipment, animals, and fodder. Often painted red.
wiki.parking lot: A public location where people park their cars. Parking lots are common in cities, especially outside of shops, shopping malls, sports stadiums, and other large venues.
wiki.mountain: A large natural elevation of the earth's surface rising abruptly from the surrounding level; larger and steeper than a hill.
wiki.waterfall: A cascade of water flowing over a steep or vertical drop.
wiki.stadium: A venue for playing sports, holding concerts, or other events primarily held outdoors, consisting of a partially or fully enclosed field or stage in a tiered structure designed to allow spectators to stand or sit and watch the event.
wiki.golf course: A golf course is a venue where the game of golf is played. It consists of a series of holes, each consisting of a teeing ground, a fairway, grass and other hazards, and a green with a flagstick and hole. A standard round of golf consists of eighteen holes.
wiki.izakaya: A Japanese bar (place). Comes in a variety of styles, but the most well-known has the patrons sitting or standing near the bar (place), with wooden menu boards on the walls. Bottles of sake can be on the countertop, while the customers are served with plates of food and likely beer.
wiki.ryokan: A type of traditional Japanese inn.
wiki.tent: A collapsible shelter of fabric (such as nylon or canvas) stretched and sustained by poles, used for camping outdoors or as a temporary building. Frequently associated with camping and the circus.
wiki.campfire: A campfire is a fire at a campsite that provides light and warmth, and heat for cooking.
wiki.karaoke box: A karaoke establishment consisting of rooms containing karaoke equipment, usually rented out for a period of time.
wiki.market stall: A makeshift or temporary structure where merchants sell their wares. A common sight at festivals and open-air markets.
wiki.apartment: A residence within a larger building containing multiple other apartments. Apartment buildings or complexes can range in size from only a few apartments to dozens or hundreds.
wiki.basketball court: A basketball court is the playing surface for basketball (sport), consisting of a rectangular floor, with hoops at each end. Indoor basketball courts are almost always made of polished wood, usually maple.
wiki.tennis court: The field where tennis is played, divided into half by a tennis net.
wiki.soccer field: Also known as a football pitch, it is the playing surface for the game of association, soccer (known as football in Europe.)
wiki.baseball stadium: A stadium specifically built for baseball (sport).
wiki.bowling alley: A facility designed for the sport of bowling. It is divided into a number of slickened alleys, each with a section at the end where the bowling pins are mechanically assembled.
wiki.boxing ring: A raised platform surrounded by four posts at the corners and four parallel rows of ropes, used for the sport of boxing.
wiki.running track: A paved track for running on. Often features multiple lanes for races.
wiki.sports court: A 'multi-sport court', most commonly associated with basketball (sport), tennis, volleyball (sport), and up to a dozen more court sports and activities. Also known as a 'game court', 'gamecourt', or 'combination court', they aren't the same size as a dedicated regulation tennis court or basketball court, and are typica…
wiki.bunk bed: A type of bed frame in which multiple beds are stacked on top of each other, allowing a higher density of sleeping persons per floor space. Commonly seen in children's rooms, dorms, ships, and jails.
wiki.basketball (object): The type of ball used in basketball (sport).
wiki.soccer ball: A ball used in the sport of soccer/football, it is popularly known for having a black and white truncated icosahedron pattern. ⚽
wiki.tennis ball: A bright green rubber ball with a thin layer of fabric, designed for use with tennis.
wiki.volleyball (object): The type of ball used in volleyball (sport).
wiki.baseball (object): The ball used in the game of baseball (sport).
wiki.bowling ball: The slightly heavy ball used in bowling. It has three closely-spaced holes through which the thumb, middle, and ring fingers are inserted for grip and aid of release.
wiki.golf ball: A small dimpled ball used in the game of golf.
wiki.tennis racket: A type of racket used in tennis to bat a tennis ball back and forth in the court.
wiki.baseball bat: A smooth wooden or metal club used in the game of baseball (sport) to hit the baseball (object) after the ball is thrown by the pitcher.
wiki.golf club: A long wooden or metal stick that has a heavy head on a slender shaft, used to hit the ball in golf.
wiki.badminton racket: A racket used for playing badminton.
wiki.baseball mitt: A glove that is used especially to catch a baseball (sport) in said game, in case the batter misses the ball.
wiki.bow (weapon): A weapon that shoots arrow (projectile)s. The weapon is used for hunting, sport shooting, and war.
wiki.shuttlecock: A shuttlecock (also called a birdie or shuttle) is a high-drag projectile used in the sport of badminton. It has an open conical shape formed by feathers or plastic embedded into a rounded cork (or rubber) base.
wiki.arrow (projectile): The projectile launched by a bow (weapon) or crossbow. It has sharp, weighty point and fletchings on the rear to stabilize its flight.
wiki.bicycle: A human-powered, pedal-driven vehicle with two wheels, one behind the other.
wiki.guitar: A plucked six-stringed musical instrument, either electric or acoustic, with a long neck.
wiki.book: A collection of sheets of paper bound together to hinge at one edge, containing printed or written material, pictures, etc.
wiki.pen: A writing instrument for writing or drawing (action) on paper with ink.
wiki.cellphone: A small handheld electronic mobile phone.
wiki.cigarette: A rolled or stuffed paper-wrapped cylinder containing tobacco which is ignited for smoking. Highly addictive and hazardous to your health, increasing the risk of cancer, tuberculosis, asthma, heart disease, and many more.
wiki.frying pan: A flat-bottomed utensil used for frying or cooking foods.
wiki.shopping bag: A bag usually made of paper or plastic used for carrying purchased goods.
wiki.broom: An object consisting of a long stick with a brush made out of stiff fibres at one end. It can be used for either sweeping the floor or transportation by flight.
wiki.fishing rod: A tool used to catch fish with a line and hook.
wiki.game controller: A device used to provide input to a computer or video game. Normally this refers to a controller that is separate from the main machine, connected by wire or wirelessly, as opposed to the controls built into a handheld game console such as a Game Boy or Nintendo DS.
wiki.gamepad: A device used to provide input to a computer or video game. Normally this refers to a controller that is separate from the main machine, connected by wire or wirelessly, as opposed to the controls built into a handheld game console such as a Game Boy or Nintendo DS.
wiki.paintbrush: An umbrella tag for the following types of brushes: • art brush • calligraphy brush • trim brush
wiki.kiseru: A long, thin-stemmed Japanese smoking pipe with a small bowl. Traditionally used for smoking kizami (刻み), or finely shredded tobacco, it went out of style after World War II.
wiki.smoking pipe: A tube with a small bowl at one end used for smoking tobacco.
wiki.cigar: A tightly rolled bundle of dry and fermented tobacco. The cylinder is predominantly brown in color and larger than a cigarette. The top half is wrapped with a brand stamp.
wiki.calligraphy brush: A round-tipped brush used for writing calligraphy, ink painting, and occasionally other forms of art. Usually broader than an art brush.
wiki.quill: A pen made from a bird's feathers.
wiki.pencil: A writing or drawing (action) device consisting of a thin stick of pigment (usually graphite), usually encased in a thin wood cylinder.
wiki.newspaper: A scheduled publication containing news of current events, informative articles, diverse features, editorials, and advertising. It usually is printed on relatively inexpensive, low-grade paper such as newsprint.
wiki.mop: A wooden pole with a sponge or absorbent fibers at the end, used to clean floors.
wiki.bucket: A cylindrical container with an open top and a flat bottom, often including a carrying handle. Can be made of almost any material, most common are metal, plastic and wood. Buckets are typically used to carry liquid.
wiki.ladle: A long-handled utensil used to scoop, transfer, and/or serve liquids, often soups and stews.
wiki.firefighter: A firefighter is a rescuer extensively trained in firefighting, primarily to extinguish fire.
wiki.scientist: A person who conducts scientific research and experimentation, often in a laboratory. Scientists stereotypically wear long white lab coats.
wiki.farmer: A person who works in a farm, engaged in farming, raising living organisms for food or raw materials.
wiki.construction worker: Someone who is involved with constructing a building. Frequently seen wearing hard hats, high-visibility clothing, and work boots.
wiki.janitor: A professional who takes care of buildings such as hospitals, schools, and office buildings. Their primary responsibility is as a cleaner and in some cases they will also carry out maintenance and security duties.
wiki.race queen: A model usually present at auto racing events. They are typically seen wearing skimpy outfits bearing the logos of the racing team or its sponsors. Their official job is to hold a parasol over the driver to shield them from sunlight while their car is being worked on. Also known as a grid girl or umbrella girl.
wiki.soldier: A member of a professional army, trained, equipped, and armed to fight in a war. They usually wear military uniforms, often with combat helmets and body armor.
wiki.jogging: Running at a slow or leisurely pace, but still moving faster than walking. Often done for exercise.
wiki.skiing: The sport of sliding down from a high place on the snow-covered slopes or snow mountain with two skis and two ski poles. Especially refers to using two boards, choose snowboarding for using only one board.
wiki.diving: The practice of either diving into the water or swimming underwater, either with a breathing apparatus (scuba diving, snorkeling, or surface supplied diving) or by breath-holding (freediving).
wiki.weightlifting: A type of exercise, mostly done at the fitness gym, where the person lifts heavy weights, such as dumbbells and barbells.
wiki.rape: Forced penetration and other sexual acts on an unwilling participant. The unwilling participant is often visibly unhappy, in pain, distressed, crying, or scared. If no penetration, use molestation.
wiki.after rape: The aftermath of rape. The subject who was raped should look distraught or otherwise should be clear that they were thoroughly unwilling.
wiki.rough sex: Sexual activity which is visibly very intense and energetic, and in which one or more of the participants may even appear to be in distress (though this does not necessarily mean that rape is occurring).
wiki.angry sex: Having sex while feeling angry towards one's partner. Sometimes also called "hatefucking" (or "hatemance" for the actions leading up to it). Should not be confused with rape, as "angry sex" implies that all parties involved are consenting.

wiki.harbor: A sheltered body of water that is suitable to moor a boat or a ship. Can also be used for an artificial platform used to dock a watercraft to unload the cargo or passengers.
wiki.bus stop: A point on a fixed bus route for on-loading and off-loading passengers. Marked by a visible bus stop sign or road sign.
wiki.playground: An area designed for children's social and recreational activities, usually in outdoor settings such as parks or school grounds. Typical playground installations include benches, swings, slides, sandboxes, and jungle gyms.
wiki.highway: A paved road, typically multi-lane, designed for high-speed or long distance motor vehicle traffic, often between cities. They're main public roads serving as high-speed thoroughfares.
wiki.taxi: A taxi (also known as a cab) is a car designed to carry passengers to a destination for a fee.
