wiki.toddlersex: Sexually explicit or sexually suggestive artwork of even younger children (younger than loli and shota) or babies. This is considered a extreme form of lolicon or shotacon.
wiki.mother and child: A mother and her own child.
wiki.father and child: A father and his own child.
wiki.kindergarten uniform: A school uniform for preschool children (5 or under), typically consisting of a simple long-sleeved blue shirt or blouse and a yellow school hat. Boys often wear shorts while girls wear a pleated skirt. Common accessories include a kindergarten bag, a school hat and a name tag. Sometimes called a smock in Japanese.
wiki.tomoeda elementary school uniform: The school uniform worn by students at Tomoeda Elementary School (友枝小学校) in Cardcaptor Sakura.
wiki.child carry: When a person, usually a child or baby, is carried by sitting upright in a person's arms.
wiki.child: A young person between infancy and puberty. This may be the character's actual age, or they may be aged down by the artist.
wiki.anime coloring: A style of coloring used in 2D anime, consisting of hard-edged highlights and shadows, as opposed to the soft, smooth shadows used in fully rendered art. Also known as cel-shading, it is the art style seen in most anime screenshots.
wiki.flat color: An image that is colored in solid blocks of color, without shadows, highlights, or gradients. The image is "flat" in that there are little to no indications of depth.
wiki.watercolor (medium): Traditional art created using watercolor paints.
wiki.screentones: A technique for applying texture or shading to a drawing by using dots in a grid pattern, used as an alternative to hatching (texture).
wiki.lineart: Art consisting mostly of solid lines, with no coloring or shading.
wiki.monochrome: An image drawn in shades of a single color. It doesn't have to be just black and white; it could be another color such as sepia, red, blue, green, etc.
wiki.thick outlines: Thick outlines are present when a character or item's outer lineart is thicker or denser than what is common.
wiki.1990s (style): Anime or manga drawn in a style that was popular in the 1990s. This includes both works originally made in the 1990s, and modern works drawn in a faux retro artstyle.
wiki.2000s (style): Anime or manga drawn in a style that was popular in the 2000s. This includes both works originally made in the 2000s in this style, and modern works drawn in a faux retro artstyle. This tag should not be used for images created in the 2000s that do not fall into this specific art style.
wiki.retro artstyle: Art drawn in the style of a prior decade, whether it be art actually from the time period or newer art imitating it with a faux retro artstyle.
wiki.drop shadow: A shadow-like visual effect consisting of a character-shaped area of color offset from the character. The shape of a drop shadow is exactly the shape of the character; if it's angled or distorted, use shadow instead.
wiki.absurdres: An image at least 3200 pixels wide or 2400 pixels tall. Approximately equivalent to mpixels:>=7.7.
wiki.highres: An image at least 1600 pixels wide or 1200 pixels tall. Approximately equivalent to mpixels:>=1.9.
wiki.simple background: An image with an empty or featureless background. Commonly, a background that is solid white, transparent, or another color.
wiki.white background: A background that is completely or predominantly white in color. Can also apply to gradient background in conjunction with another background color.
wiki.black background: A background that is solid or predominantly black. Can also apply to gradient background in conjunction with another background color.
wiki.grey background: Backgrounds with a solid or predominantly grey color. Can also apply to gradient background in conjunction with another background color.
wiki.blue background: Backgrounds with a solid or predominantly blue color. Used for shades of ultramarine, navy or sky blue. For aquamarine or turquoise, use aqua background. Can also apply to gradient background in conjunction with another background color.
wiki.pink background: Backgrounds with a solid or predominantly pink color. Can also apply to gradient background in conjunction with another background color.
wiki.yellow background: A background that is solid or predominantly yellow. Can also apply to gradient background in conjunction with another background color.
wiki.red background: Backgrounds with a solid or predominantly red color. Can also apply to gradient background in conjunction with another background color.
wiki.two-tone background: A background that consists of only two colors. May or may not involve a gradient transition between them.
wiki.polka dot background: A completely or predominantly polka dot background.
wiki.striped background: A completely or predominantly striped background.
wiki.floral background: A background consisting of flowers. The flowers can be a simple pattern or real.
wiki.halftone background: A completely or predominantly halftone background.
wiki.sparkle background: A background consisting of sparkles, whether they're drawn really large and easy to see, or the background is flooded with glints of glitter.
wiki.abstract background: A background consisting of abstract shapes, colors, or patterns, usually with no identifiable objects or setting.
wiki.blurry background: When the background of an image is out-of-focus.
wiki.pixel art: An image drawn with a pixelated art style, typically with large individual pixels and a limited color palette.
wiki.ukiyo-e: Traditional Japanese woodblock prints, parodies thereof, or other art based on that style.
wiki.chibi: A chibi (Japanese for "small") is a super deformed character, whose proportions are exaggerated for a cute effect.
wiki.greyscale: A completely colorless, black-and-white image. The image is composed exclusively of shades of black, white, and grey. It is very common for comics and doujinshi to be in greyscale.
wiki.spot color: A mostly-monochrome, muted and/or dark picture, with a few colors employed to 'pop out' and draw the viewer's attention.
wiki.partially colored: Some parts of a picture are colored, while others remain uncolored, left as a sketch or lineart. This is either because the image is unfinished, or as way to draw attention to a subject.
wiki.pastel colors: An image colored primarily with pale shades and hues, achieved by using low contrast and high saturation.
wiki.muted colors: An image that is barely in color, due to colors being washed out, usually by mixing with grey. Muted colors are very low in saturation.
wiki.muted color: An image that is barely in color, due to colors being washed out, usually by mixing with grey. Muted colors are very low in saturation.
wiki.limited palette: An image that uses a small number of distinct colors. Images fitting this tag use more than one color besides black and in more of the image than what would be considered spot coloring. Likely to also be considered partially colored.
wiki.colorful: An image filled with bold, bright colors that stand out. Colorful images are very high in saturation.
wiki.high contrast: A picture that features sharp divisions between very dark colors and light colors. More commonly seen in greyscale works, but it can also be seen of colorful ones too.
wiki.sepia: An image primarily colored or tinted in sepia, a brownish or yellowish color tone commonly seen in old photographs. This may be used to impart a vintage or antique quality, or to indicate something happened in the past, such as a flashback.
wiki.light rays: Visible beams of light that emanate from the sky or from a light source, often traveling through clouds or gaps in between objects. Also known as light shafts, god rays, or crepuscular rays.
wiki.sunbeam: Visible light rays that stream through gaps in clouds or between other objects during the day.
wiki.dappled sunlight: The effect of sunlight filtering through trees or leaves, creating a pattern of light and shadows.
wiki.silhouette: A view of an object or scene consisting of an outline and a featureless interior. It is usually black and often confused with shadow.
wiki.light particles: Very small bright particles that float in the air. Often seen with light rays coming through a window and illuminating the dust particles in the air.
wiki.sparkle: A bright shimmer of reflected light, generally several diamond_(shape)-, astroid, or star (symbol)-shaped lines radiating from a point. They can be used to indicate an object is bright and shiny, but more often in anime they appear in a character's eyes, next to their head, or as an sparkling aura around a character to…
wiki.petals: Petals that are detached from a flower.
wiki.falling petals: Petals falling or blowing in the wind.
wiki.bubble: Usually refers to a soap bubble, which is a very thin film of soapy water that forms a sphere with an iridescent surface. However, this term can also applied to any type of bubble, including chewing gum and air bubbles underwater.
wiki.confetti: A multitude of colored paper, usually thrown at celebrations. Not to be confused with petals.
wiki.lens flare: An optical artifact caused by sufficiently intense light entering a lens. This light reflects and scatters in a way that leads to it "leaking" into the image, appearing as bright patches of various shapes and sizes in the image.
wiki.bloom: When bright lights blur into surrounding areas.
wiki.motion blur: When a part of the image is blurry to imply fast movement.
wiki.speed lines: A type of motion lines that indicate fast speed. Usually drawn as a large number of lines surrounding the character, or encompassing the entire background.
wiki.emphasis lines: Lines drawn in a burst pattern, radiating outward from a part of the image to which the artist wants to draw attention. They cause the area surrounded by the lines to stand out more in the viewer's eye.
wiki.very wide shot: An image where the subject is fully visible but takes up a vanishingly small portion of the frame, even less so than in wide shot. If none of the individual characters are noticeable from the image thumbnail, consider using this tag.
wiki.foreshortening: A technique in which an object is depicted at an angle, making it appear shorter than its actual size. This captures the distortion seen when viewing an object at an unusual angle.
wiki.bird's eye view: A viewpoint looking down at a scene at a very steep angle from above. The camera is positioned above the subject as if the viewer is a bird in the sky. The opposite of worm's eye view.
wiki.worm's eye view: A viewpoint looking up at a scene from a very steep angle from below. The subject generally towers over the viewer as if the viewer is a worm on the ground, often with a high degree of foreshortening present.
wiki.no humans: No human or human-like characters are visible in the picture.
wiki.scenery: An image that pays special attention to the scene or landscape of its composition, usually favoring it over any characters present.
wiki.solo focus: An image containing multiple people, but focused on only a single person. The other characters are either unidentifiable or only a small part of the picture.
wiki.people: Unnamed background characters that are not part of an image's focus, usually to bring life to a scene and make spaces look less empty. They may be drawn at considerable distance from the viewer, or established as an insignificant part of the image.
wiki.audience: People who come to watch a concert, performance, or other event that is usually on a stage in the middle of a stadium.
wiki.crowded: Where a large abundance of people are in an area with little space between them.
wiki.wrestling ring: A square-shaped, raised platform covered in canvas and surrounded on each side by three taut ropes, in which professional wrestling matches are staged. Distinguished from a boxing ring in that most boxing rings have four ropes instead of three.
wiki.arena: A typically enclosed area surrounded by seats for spectators, in which sports, entertainments, and other public events are held.
wiki.pom pom (cheerleading): Large, fluffy ball of soft material usually waved about by cheerleaders.
wiki.wrestling: A martial art that involves grappling with an opponent in order to pin or press them to the ground.
wiki.suplex: A professional wrestling move involving one person lifting an opponent over one's body and then driving that opponent onto the mat.
wiki.german suplex: A suplex where one lifts the opponent from behind and slams them on their shoulders.
wiki.submission hold: A submission hold specifically refers to types of professional wrestling style moves used to immobilize an opponent causing them to surrender/submit.
wiki.armlock: Restraining another person by holding them from beneath the armpits, similar to a full nelson, but without placing the hands on the back of the neck.
wiki.scissorhold: Wrapping one's thighs around another person's head or neck and squeezing. Like a headlock, but using the legs instead of the arms. Originally a wrestling move, on Danbooru this usually refers to a femdom practice.
wiki.choke hold: A choke hold, or stranglehold, is any type of unarmed strangulation technique used to submit an opponent or incapacitate a foe by restricting their airway (choking) or blood flow (strangulation). Choke holds are common in martial arts such as judo, Brazilian jiu-jitsu and sambo.
wiki.triangle choke: A type of figure-four choke hold that strangles the opponent by encircling their neck with the legs in a configuration similar to the shape of a triangle.
wiki.piledriver (wrestling): A wrestling move that is performed by holding the opponent upside down with their head close to the waist and effectively sitting down with their head meeting the ground in between the opponent's thighs.
wiki.pinned: Held firmly to a surface by someone, generally with the intent of restricting movement or keeping the other in one spot.
wiki.catfight: A fight between two girls. Might involve cat-like scratching (hence the term). Usually unarmed.
wiki.arm wrestling: A contest of strength typically involving two participants holding each other's hand of the same side, with their elbow placed on a flat surface (usually a table) as a "lever" and attempt to force the opponent's hand down onto the table top to win.
wiki.sumo: A Japanese competitive wrestling sport where a wrestler attempts to force another wrestler either down to the ground or out of a circular ring. It is considered the national sport of Japan.
wiki.mixed martial arts: Mixed martial arts (MMA), sometimes referred to as cage fighting, is a full-contact combat sport based on striking, grappling and ground fighting, incorporating techniques from various combat sports from around the world.
wiki.martial arts: Ambiguous tag for various unknown combat arts, especially unarmed combat arts. If a specific martial art can be identified, please use its tag instead. → karate, taekwondo, aikidou, jeet kune do, judo, kung fu, boxing, capoeira
wiki.cheering: The act of supporting someone during an event by yelling positive messages in order to boost morale.
wiki.victory pose: A victory pose is a pose assumed by a person to celebrate victory, particularly by athletes and other sportspeople. Victory poses often involve raising the arms in the air.
wiki.bearhug: When a character is forcefully constricted from the waist.
wiki.head between thighs: For when only a person's head is held or situated between another person's thighs. May also be considered a scissorhold if the one person is using their thighs to deliberately asphyxiate or squeeze the other person.
wiki.sexual harassment: Sexual abuse or unwanted sexual attention that is milder than rape or molestation.
wiki.pulling another's clothes: Pulling down someone else's clothing, usually to expose their private parts. Do not use for clothing that is being lifted up, pulled to the side, or grabbed to get their attention.
wiki.defeat: When someone has been beaten in battle or has lost a game. The opposite to victory.
wiki.public masturbation: Masturbating in public. A form of public indecency. If other people are nearby, it may also be a form of exhibitionism or stealth masturbation.
wiki.masturbating while watching: Masturbating while watching other people having sex. This may be an act of voyeurism or during group sex.
wiki.public bondage: Purposeful physical restraint of a person, as with ropes, cords, or cuffs, for sexual purposes in public.
wiki.wrestling outfit: A post in which one or more characters are wearing clothing designed to be used while wrestling. This can be anything as realistic as a singlet and pads, or it can be akin to the more stylized outfits found in professional wrestling.
wiki.singlet: A one-piece, tight-fitting, colored uniform, usually made of spandex or nylon, often used in amateur wrestling.
wiki.referee: An official who observes a sports game to enforce the rules of the game.
wiki.wrestling mask: A fabric-based mask that some professional wrestlers wear as part of their in-ring persona or gimmick.
wiki.championship belt: A wide decorative trophy belt at least wielded by a boxing, mixed martial arts, or professional wrestling champion, usually having a large golden centerpiece denoting the official title name and logo.
wiki.elbow pads: Protective gear worn around the elbows to protect them against impact injury from falling to the ground or hitting an obstacle.
wiki.martial arts belt: A belt worn with martial arts outfits like dougi.
wiki.desi: South Asian people and costumes, associated with the countries of India, Sri Lanka, Pakistan, and Bangladesh.
wiki.indian clothes: See asian indian clothes or native american clothes.
wiki.middle eastern architecture: A collective term for buildings (and their interiors) which have architectural influence historically or currently associated with the Middle East region after Classical Antiquity. This includes Arabic, Iranian (Persian), Islamic, Ottoman (Turkish) architecture and more.
wiki.mixed-sex combat: A fight between men and women. Mixed-sex combat arts usually involves ryona/reverse ryona and femdom elements as a part of a fetish, and humiliation is a recurring occurence.
wiki.gagged: Having the mouth restrained to prevent speech or mouth movement, either with a purpose-built gag, such as a ball gag, or by an improvised gag, such as tape over the mouth. Commonly associated with bondage.
wiki.improvised gag: A gag made of unconventional materials, such as cloth, articles of clothing, or tape.
wiki.cleave gag: A cloth gag that goes between the subject's teeth, holding their mouth open.
wiki.gag harness: A gag secured in place using more elaborate sets of straps than the normal two side straps.
wiki.shibari over clothes: Wearing shibari-style bondage over the clothes.
wiki.bound arms: Both arms bound together with some sort of restraint.
wiki.bound legs: Both legs bound together with some sort of restraint.
wiki.bound torso: The upper body of a character is bound.
wiki.captured: When someone is being held in custody by others, often while being restrained.
wiki.tied to chair: A character is restrained to a chair by any means.
wiki.chained: When a character is tied up in one way or another using a chain(s).
wiki.prisoner: Someone who is in prison. Usually seen wearing prison clothes, consisting of either an orange jumpsuit or black-and-white striped clothes.
wiki.small penis humiliation: Humiliation scenario that occurs when a character makes fun of someone's actually or purportedly small penis (often as a part of a femdom act). Typical indicators include a character making a pinching gesture with their fingers, stifled laughter and other embarrassing references to another character's penis.
wiki.chastity cage: A device that can be locked onto a person's penis to prevent the wearer from engaging in sexual contact. In many cases, it also makes erections uncomfortable or impossible. Also known as a penis cage.
wiki.instant loss: A trope where a character is almost instantly defeated, despite their cocky attitude beforehand. Often a sexual scenario where a character ends up mating pressed despite their protests that they'll never lose to the dick, although it can also apply to non-sexual scenarios.
wiki.forced to watch: A situation where a character is being forced by someone else into watching something they don't want to see. This includes mirrors to look at themselves and video recordings.
wiki.cage: A structure of bars or wires in which birds or other animals are confined.
wiki.shimaidon: Group sex with two (or more) sisters.
wiki.shimaidon (sex): Group sex with two (or more) sisters.
wiki.oyakodon (sex): A threesome with a mother and daughter simultaneously. The term is derived from the literal translation of oyakodon (food), a "parent-and-child donburi" that contains chicken and egg as key ingredients of the dish.
wiki.group incest: More than two relatives engaged in an act of incest.
wiki.sexual coaching: A character coaching, helping or encouraging another during group sex, often without directly participating. This tag applies to any sexual act.
wiki.measuring: Using a tool marked with standard dimensions in order to figure out the size, amount or degree of something. On Danbooru, it's popular for one character to figure out another character's bust, waist and hip measurements.
wiki.penis measuring: Measuring a penis, a phallic object, or the depth of a possible penetration.
wiki.ruler: An instrument used in mathematics and engineering to measure distances or to draw perfectly straight lines.
wiki.tape measure: A long and thin strip of plastic or metal, etched with scales. The plastic tape measure is usually short (around 150 cm, although really long ones can reach hundreds of meters) and used by a tailor to take body measurements for clothes-making.
wiki.notebook: A book of blank pages, used for writing, drawing (action), or taking notes. They are available in a variety of sizes and bindings, with spiral binding being especially common. Many notebooks feature perforated pages that are easier to tear out.
wiki.sketchbook: A book filled with blank pages, which an artist can sketch drawing (object)s on.
wiki.eraser: An object, typically a piece of soft rubber or plastic, used to rub out writing.
wiki.notepad: A small pad of blank pages used for taking notes.
wiki.sticky note: A small piece of paper with a strip of glue on its back, made for temporarily attaching notes to documents and other surfaces. Usually colored yellow due to the ubiquity of 3M's Post-It brand.
wiki.envelope: A common packaging item for mailing letters and documents, either through a mailing service or from a sender directly to a receiver.
wiki.letter: A longish note commonly written on folded paper.
wiki.love letter: A letter given to confess one's love for the recipient. Almost always an envelope sealed shut with a heart-shaped sticker.
wiki.map: A picture or diagram representation of a location, often augmented with street, city, or landmark information. May be written on paper or in a book as a guide or atlas, or imprinted on a globe.
wiki.map (object): A map is present somewhere in the image as an object.
wiki.origami: Origami (折り紙, from ori meaning "folding", and kami meaning "paper") is the traditional Japanese art of paper folding.
wiki.paper airplane: A toy airplane made of paper. One of the many basic origami patterns.
wiki.wallet: A small flat case that can hold small personal items such as paper currency, credit cards identification documents, photographs, commuter passes, business cards, and other paper or laminated cards.
wiki.coin: A round metal disk used as money.
wiki.money: Any form of currency, including banknotes (paper currency), coins, or even money bags.
wiki.dice: Dice are small, throwable objects used to generate random values in a wide variety of games.
wiki.chess piece: Any of the various pieces or "men" used to play chess.
wiki.gift box: A small box that may be wrapped with colorful paper and tied together with a bow on the outside. The inside will contain a gift for one person to give to another as a surprise.
wiki.trophy: A reward recognizing someone's achievements that the recipient can display on a shelf. They're typically seen at sports events or associated with film-making.
wiki.padlock: A portable lock with a shackle that may be passed through an opening, such as a chain or hasp, to secure an object.
wiki.wand: A short, thin, hand-held stick made of wood, stone, ivory, or metal, with ceremonial or magical significance.
wiki.hourglass: A timing device made with two bulbous pieces of glass connected together, where sand or similar material inside the glass can trickle through one bulb to the other to measure a certain amount of time, whether it is in minutes or an hour.
wiki.magnifying glass: A convex lens that is used to produce a magnified image of an object. The lens is usually mounted in a frame with a handle.
wiki.binoculars: A type of optics. A pair of telescopes mounted side-by-side.
wiki.telescope: A device used to observe a subject that is far away, often celestial bodies in the far reaches of space.
wiki.megaphone: A funnel (cone) shaped device held to the mouth, and used for amplifying or directing sound.
wiki.briefcase: A case used for carrying documents, such as papers or files or books. Mostly used by business people or students.
wiki.calendar (object): When a post contains a calendar, but the actual post is not a page of a calendar.
wiki.watering can: A portable can with a long open spout extending from one side and a handle on the top, designed for manually watering flowers and plants.
wiki.hammer: A tool or weapon meant to deliver an impact to an object. The most common uses are for driving nail (hardware)s in construction, fitting parts, forging metal, and breaking up objects. A large hammer, such as sledgehammer, can be used as a deadly bludgeoning weapon.
wiki.wrench: A tool used to apply leverage to tighten and loosen nut (hardware)s or bolt (hardware)s. Also called a spanner.
wiki.screwdriver: A tool with a flattened, cross-shaped, or star-shaped tip that fits into the head of a screw to turn it.
wiki.saw: A tool consisting of a hard blade, wire, or chain with a toothed edge. It is used to cut through relatively hard material, most often wood. The cut is made by placing the toothed edge against the material and moving it forcefully back and forth.
wiki.axe: An implement consisting of a wedge-shaped blade head attached to long handle.
wiki.sewing needle: A needle with a small hollow on the non-pointed end to allow for thread to pass through. Then the prepared needle is run through fabric to sew clothing.
wiki.thread: A long, thin strand of cotton, nylon, or other fibers used in sewing, stitching, embroidery, or weaving.
wiki.yarn: Twisted strands of fiber, usually stored wrapped in a yarn ball, used for knitting. Also used as a common toy for cats.
wiki.yarn ball: A bunch of yarn rolled up into a ball for storage.
wiki.comb: A small hairdressing tool made out of numerous teeth lined in a row. They help brush hair and manage the scalp, and some are made to help remove nits.
wiki.hair brush: A stick brush with rigid or soft bristles used in hair care for smoothing, styling, and detangling human hair, or for grooming an animal's fur.
wiki.hair dryer: A handheld electric appliance used for drying and styling hair.
wiki.toothbrush: A small stick with firm bristles used for brushing teeth to remove plaque and keep teeth clean.
wiki.makeup brush: A cosmetic brush used to put on makeup, particularly on the cheeks or eyelids.
wiki.perfume bottle: A small spritz bottle or vial containing perfume, meant to be sprayed on a person or object to give it a pleasant scent.
wiki.tissue: A thin lightweight paper used for a variety of cleaning, cushioning, and wrapping purposes.
wiki.thermometer: A device for measuring temperature. Often used in a medical context.
wiki.first aid kit: An emergency kit containing basic medical supplies for fast treatment of an injury.
wiki.test tube: A piece of laboratory glassware composed of a finger-like length of glass tubing, open at the top, with a rounded U-shaped bottom.
wiki.remote control: A small, handheld controller that operates some sort of electronic device from a distance, such as a television, DVD player, CD player, air conditioner, etc.
wiki.tablet pc: A tablet computer, commonly just called a tablet, is a portable computer housed within the casing of a handheld touchscreen display. They appear like a larger version of the modern smartphone.
wiki.computer keyboard: A peripheral device used to type and enter characters into a computer. It is a separate component of many desktop computers and an integrated one on laptops.
wiki.keyboard (computer): A peripheral device used to type and enter characters into a computer. It is a separate component of many desktop computers and an integrated one on laptops.
wiki.computer mouse: A device used to control an on-screen pointer by detecting two-dimensional motion. Often goes on a mousepad (object).
wiki.mouse (computer): A device used to control an on-screen pointer by detecting two-dimensional motion. Often goes on a mousepad (object).
wiki.bento: A Japanese packed lunch. A traditional bento consists of rice, fish or meat (or tako-san wiener), tamagoyaki, and one or more pickled or cooked vegetables, usually in a box-shaped container, and sometimes wrapped in a cloth known as a furoshiki or stacked together.
wiki.water bottle: A bottle that looks like it contains water. Use plastic bottle for bottles not containing water.
wiki.thermos: A container or vessel designed to keep liquids hot or cold for long periods of time. This is accomplished by the container being composed of two flasks, one within the other, and joined at the neck.
wiki.black rose: A flower that does not exist in nature but have been genetically engineered. It mainly serves as a plot device in fiction to represent negative concepts such as death, tragic, romances, hatred and farewells.
wiki.blue rose: For the character from Tiger & Bunny, see Blue Rose (Tiger & Bunny).
wiki.orange flower: A flower that is orange in colour.
wiki.pink rose: One of the most popular, naturally-occurring flowers across the world, representing gentleness, refinement and femininity.
wiki.purple flower: Any kind of flower that's colored purple. They can either be real kind of flowers or fictional.
wiki.purple rose: While dark purple and indigo roses do not exist due to the lack of blue pigmentation, light lilac roses do and can represent enchantment, desire and caution.
wiki.red rose: One of the most popular color of natural roses across the world, and often represents love and romance.
wiki.white rose: One of the most popular color of roses across the world, representing purity and innocence.
wiki.yellow flower: Any type of flower, whether real or fictional, that is colored yellow.
wiki.yellow rose: A color of rose that occurs naturally, and is often associated with joy and friendship.
wiki.camellia: A flower growing in evergreen shrubs native to Asia, especially in Japan, China, and Korea.
wiki.daisy (flower): Daisy and aster are blanket names for many similar looking flowers in the expansive Asteraceae family. Asters are practically indistinguishable from daisies for tagging purposes.
wiki.tulip: A perennial plant that grows from a bulb, has lance-shaped leaves, and produces a large, showy flower. Tulips come in a wide range of colors.
wiki.white lily: A lily that has white blossoms. Check lily for more information.
wiki.wisteria: A woody vine whose flowers hang down in pendulous, elongated clusters. The blossoms are colored either white, violet, pink, or purple.
wiki.bare tree: A tree with no leaves or flowers, whether due to shedding in autumn, or because the tree is dead.
wiki.branch: A piece of wood that grows from a tree or bush. Compared to a stick, a branch is usually bigger and may have leaves or flowers attached to it.
wiki.lily pad: A round leaf of the Nymphaeaceae family (water lilies).
wiki.palm leaf: A leaf from a palm tree or from any similar plant.
wiki.tree stump: The base of tree that remains in the ground after most of the stem or trunk has been removed.
wiki.vines: Any plant that has a growth habit of trailing or scandenting (i.e., climbing) stems, lianas, or runners. The term vine may also refer to the stems or runners themselves, such as when used in wickerwork, for example.
wiki.bird: A class of animals characterized by their feathered wings.
wiki.butterfly: A butterfly is any of several groups of mainly day-flying insects of the order Lepidoptera, the butterflies and moths. Like other holometabolous insects, butterflies' life cycle consists of four parts, egg, larva, pupa and adult.
wiki.cat: A domesticated feline mammal. This tag can also be used for cat-related things like stuffed cats, cat demons/monsters, and bodiless cat heads.
wiki.dog: A canine mammal. May be feral or domesticated.
wiki.fish: An aquatic animal usually having scales and breathing through gills.
wiki.school desk: A desk used by students in a school classroom.
wiki.school chair: A chair used by students in a school classroom. Usually armless, with a metal frame and a wooden seat.
wiki.chalkboard: A board to be written on with chalk, typically used in school classrooms as a visual aid.
wiki.book stack: A vertical grouping of books placed on top of one another to form a small tower.
wiki.cabinet: Boxy pieces of furniture with doors and drawers for storing miscellaneous items. Some cabinets can be freestanding, while others are mounted on a wall or attached like a medicine cabinet.
wiki.drawer: Open-top boxes that slide in and out of cabinets, used to store clothing and other items.
wiki.flower pot: A container in which flowers and other plants are cultivated and displayed, indoors or outdoors.
wiki.picture frame: A rigid structure that surrounds or encloses a photo (object), painting (object), or drawing (object).
wiki.potted plant: A plant that is grown indoors within a flower pot or container of any size or shape.
wiki.rug: A movable floor covering of thick woven material or animal skin, typically not extending over the entire floor. Contrast with carpet, which is not movable and covers the floor wall to wall.
wiki.shelf: A flat, rigid structure that is fixed at right angles to a wall or forms part of a cabinet, desk, etc. and is used to support, store, or display objects.
wiki.tablecloth: A thin cloth that is larger in size than the top of a table, designed to be draped over the table.
wiki.wooden table: A table made out of wood.
wiki.window blinds: A window covering composed of long slats used to block light from coming through the window.
wiki.barrel: A large wooden container used for maturation, fermentation, and/or storage of alcohol and spirits. It is often made of slats of wood bound by metal rings.
wiki.candlestand: A device that holds one or more candles in place, also known as a candlestick or candleholder. A candlestand for several candles is called a candelabra. They can be simple or highly ornate, and they can be made of various materials, from wood to brass to silver.
wiki.gohei: A wooden wand traditionally decorated with shide (zigzag paper streamers), though in the past it was made with rectangular strips of paper. It is used for Shinto rituals to cleanse negative energy or bless.
wiki.shimenawa: Braided rice straw rope, often worn as a sash, used for ritual purification in the Shinto religion, often seen festooned with shide.
wiki.vase: A tall ceramic or glass jar designed for holding cut flowers and water in it.
wiki.wind chime: A decorative object suspended in midair that makes noise when blown by the wind.
wiki.treasure chest: A box or chest containing treasure, often gold coins or gems. Coveted by fantasy adventurers and pirates. May sometimes be a trap containing a mimic instead.
wiki.cardboard box: A box generally used for transporting things, for hiding, for sneaking around, or for building a robot.
wiki.doll: A small toy representation of a person, designed for interactive play and display. Dolls can be crafted from a variety of materials, including both hard substances like plastic and wood, and soft materials such as cloth and rubber.
wiki.gift: A gift box, bag, or container wrapped in plain or patterned paper and decorated with ribbons. Gifts are often given on birthdays, Christmas, or Valentine's Day.
wiki.ceiling: The upper interior surface of a room or other similar compartment. Most commonly visible in upward-facing perspectives.
wiki.checkered floor: Alternating colored squares adjacent to each other, patterned into the floor.
wiki.door: A hinged, sliding, or revolving barrier at the entrance to a building, room, or vehicle, or in the framework of a cupboard.
wiki.doorway: The space in a wall where a door opens, or a covered area just outside a door. Or a door frame, even if no door is visible.
wiki.gate: A door placed on certain fortifications or an arched structure with opening at the center.
wiki.ladder: A structure consisting of a series of bars or steps between two upright lengths of wood, metal, or rope, used for climbing up or down something.
wiki.open door: A door that has already been opened.
wiki.open window: A window that has been opened to allow air from the outside to flow inside.
wiki.pole: A tall, cylindrical structure that stands up straight in the ground. Also gives a stripper something to dance around.
wiki.reflective floor: A floor that creates a reflection.
wiki.sliding doors: Doors that are designed to slide open and closed, rather than being controlled by a doorknob.
wiki.tile floor: An indoor floor made of square tiles, typically made of stone, glass, ceramic, or clay. Often also reflective floor.
wiki.floor tiles: An indoor floor made of square tiles, typically made of stone, glass, ceramic, or clay. Often also reflective floor.
wiki.tile wall: A wall made of square tiles, typically made of stone, glass, ceramic, or clay. Commonly found in bathrooms and kitchens.
wiki.tombstone: A stone marker placed near a grave. Also known as a headstone.
wiki.wooden wall: A wall that is comprised of wooden planks placed next to each other.
wiki.spider web: A net-like construct of sticky silk thread used by spiders to catch prey.
wiki.pavement: Stones arranged to form the surface of a street, footpath, etc.
wiki.road sign: A sign erected at the side of a road to provide information to drivers.
wiki.poster (object): A large printed picture, usually pasted or hung on a wall.
wiki.trash can: A container where waste is put.
wiki.trash bin: A container where waste is put.
wiki.air conditioner: A machine that circulates cold air in a building to keep the premises cool during hot days.
wiki.alarm clock: A clock that has an alarm that one can program to go off at a particular time in order to wake them up the following morning. Traditional alarm clocks use bells, while modern ones use beepers, buzzers, or music.
wiki.electric fan: An electrical device with revolving vanes used for ventilation and general comfort. If the subject is visibly making strange sounds/dialogue by speaking into the fan then fan speaking may apply.
wiki.light bulb: A light bulb is a device that produces light from electricity when turned on. Light bulbs are often used to bring light to a space or to indicate when an electronic device is on.
wiki.refrigerator: A storage appliance that keeps food cold. Also known as fridge in British English.
wiki.television: A device that receives television signals and produces them on a screen.
wiki.faucet: Fixed device found in kitchens and bathrooms used for drawing water. Often paired with a sink or bathtub. May be installed outdoors for use with a hose.
wiki.toilet: A plumbing fixture found in bathrooms used for defecation and urination.
wiki.cooking pot: A steel, ceramic or glass vessel used for different cooking applications such as boiling, braising and stewing.
wiki.drinking glass: Any type of glass cup made for drinking cold beverages. Using one to drink a hot beverage is not recommended as it could break, unless the glass is thick.
wiki.kettle: A container for boiling water. Stovetop kettles are normally metal and have a lid, spout, and handle. The handle is generally placed at the top so that the kettle can be hung over an open fire.
wiki.crystal: A crystal consists of matter that is formed from an ordered arrangement of atoms, molecules, or ions. At the macroscopic scale crystals have well defined shapes with flat faces. Examples of crystals are snowflakes, diamonds, and quartz.
wiki.seashell: Generic term for the empty shells of various marine mollusks, often adapted for decorative use. Common varieties include the shells of scallops, conches, clams, and cowries.
wiki.shallow water: Water that isn't particularly deep, where the bottom is usually visible.
wiki.starfish: Also called a "Sea star". They are star-shaped sea creatures from the class Asteroidea.
wiki.waves: A disturbance on the surface of the ocean caused by wind blowing over the water.
wiki.rubber duck: A toy, resembling a small yellow duck, used on playtime during one's bath.
wiki.aircraft: Any sort of flying machine, realistic or fictional.
wiki.fighter jet: A jet-powered military aircraft. Fighting in conflicts as close support for ground troops, and maintaining air superiority in a dogfight. These crafts can travel at supersonic speeds of Mach 1, 2, and 3; armed with an array of guided and unguided penetration bombs, missiles, and vulcan cannons.
wiki.flight deck: The flat surface on an aircraft carrier where aircraft takeoff and land.
wiki.military vehicle: A vehicle that is used primarily for military (combat) purposes.
wiki.motor vehicle: Any motorized, self-propelled ground vehicle that does not operate on railroad tracks. Commonly wheeled or sometimes has caterpillar tracks.
wiki.motorcycle: A two-wheeled motor vehicle with a step-over frame.
wiki.sports car: A type of car designed around dynamic performance and highlighting the fun of driving.
wiki.truck: A truck is a motor vehicle designed to transport cargo, carry specialized payloads, or perform other utilitarian work.
wiki.smokestack: An upright exhaust pipe for discharging smoke from a locomotive, ship, factory, and such, and helping to induce a draft.
wiki.watercraft: A marine vehicle, including ships, boats, hovercraft and submarines.
wiki.warship: A type of ship specifically made for military combat uses. Typically operated by the navy.
wiki.glowing weapon: Any type of weapon that is glowing.
wiki.happy halloween: The message "Happy Halloween" written somewhere, in English or any other language.
wiki.happy valentine: When the message "Happy Valentine's Day" (or some variation thereof) is written somewhere, in English or any other language.
wiki.year of the rabbit: The Year of the Rabbit is fourth in the Chinese Zodiac. These are Rabbit years: 1939, 1951, 1963, 1975, 1987, 1999, 2011, 2023.
wiki.year of the tiger: The Tiger ranks the third of the animals in the Chinese zodiac. Years of birth include 1914, 1926, 1938, 1950, 1962, 1974, 1986, 1998, 2010, 2022.
wiki.wreath: A ring made of flowers, leaves, fruits, twigs, or other natural materials. It can be used as an ornament, hung on a wall or door, or worn on the head as a head wreath.
wiki.setsubun: Setsubun (節分, lit. "seasonal division") is the last day of winter in the Japanese calendar. It usually corresponds to February 3rd in the Gregorian calendar.
wiki.tanabata: A Japanese festival celebrated on July 7 that "celebrates the meeting of the deities Orihime (tanabata) and Hikoboshi (represented by the stars Vega and Altair respectively)". One observed custom during the festival is to write wishes on small slips of paper called tanzaku and hang them on bamboos.
wiki.spring (season): Use this tag for images that clearly take place during spring. Telltale signs include lots of flowers (especially cherry blossoms) and fairy heralds. → flower, cherry blossoms, lily white, Summer, Autumn, Winter, hay fever
wiki.autumn: The third season, also known as "fall", is marked by shorter daylight hours and cooler weather along with the end of the growing season and the year's final harvest. Generally identified by the presence of autumn leaves and the return of warmer clothing such as scarves and sweaters.
wiki.snowman: A handmade sculpture made out of compacted snow. Usually it consists of two or three large snowballs stacked on top of each other, then adding decorations like a hat or bucket, coal or rock for the eyes and buttons, a carrot for the nose, a scarf, and twigs for arms.
wiki.folding chair: A light, portable chair that folds flat, and can be stored in a stack, row, or on a cart.
wiki.lounge chair: A type of outdoor chair that allows a sunbather to recline in a relaxed position. Often found at a beach or at poolside, possibly in conjunction with a parasol. Also known as a sun lounger, chaise lounge (US), or deck chair (UK).
wiki.on bench: Someone is on a bench, regardless if they're sitting, squatting, standing, lying and such.
wiki.on floor: Sitting, lying, or kneeling on the floor of a room or other indoors environment.
wiki.on ground: Sitting, lying, or kneeling on the ground in an outdoors environment, whether that be grass, dirt, sand, snow, pavement, etc. A character on a beach towel or blanket may be considered to be on the ground.
wiki.on swing: When someone or something is on a swing.
wiki.on table: Standing, sitting, lying, or similar atop a table.
wiki.gym storeroom: An indoor storage room used to store equipment used by physical education classes, such as vaulting horses and basketball (object)s. Often found near the school gym.
wiki.morning: The part of the day that generally most people start to wake up and the sun starts to rise. Comes after night and before noon. Includes dawn and the sunrise.
wiki.grey sky: A sky which is grey. Often caused by rain or clouds.
wiki.gray sky: A sky which is grey. Often caused by rain or clouds.
wiki.constellation: A group of star (sky)s that appear to form a pattern in the sky.
wiki.contrail: A vapor or condensation trail caused by airplanes.
wiki.red moon: Any image depicting the moon with a distinct red tint or glow. Also called a "blood moon." This is often considered an evil omen.
wiki.breath: Visible steam exhaled in puffs, usually in cold or winter weather.
wiki.glint: Spikes of light reflecting off a shiny object, commonly a polished or metal object such as jewelry or a sword.
wiki.light trail: A moving source of light leaving behind a trail.
wiki.sunburst: A sunburst consists of rays of light radiating out from a central point.
wiki.musical note: A symbol that represents a sound, indicating both its pitch (how high or low the sound is) and its duration (how long it should be played).
wiki.notice lines: Lines appearing around a character's head like to indicate that they notice something. Can also be used around objects to point them out.
wiki.puff of air: A cartoon puff of air: 💨. Usually comes from a character's head to indicate anger, annoyance, exhaustion, smugness, or simply a sigh.
wiki.spoken musical note: When a musical note is either inside a speech bubble or follows a simple line from a character who has their mouth open. It can express joy or singing.
wiki.squiggle: A round scribble denoting a character as grumbling, annoyed, unamused, embarrassed, frustrated, or otherwise vaguely dissatisfied. If used inside a speech bubble, tag also as spoken squiggle.
wiki.zzz: A sound effect generally used to portray sleeping, snoring or the soft, quiet breathing during sleep.
wiki.diagonal-striped background: A striped background where the stripes are arranged diagonally.
wiki.plaid background: A completely or predominantly plaid background.
wiki.sunburst background: A sunburst background radiating outward from the center behind the subject.
wiki.vertical-striped background: A striped background where the stripes are arranged vertically.
wiki.3d background: Hand-drawn artwork with a 3D-rendered background. Compare with mixed media.
wiki.black border: An image with a black border along all four sides.
wiki.outside border: When a character or object appears either on top of or outside a border, letterbox or pillarbox surrounding the rest of an image or panel. Do not use with out-of-border text of any kind.
wiki.white border: An image that has a white border surrounding its edges. The character's body may be drawn outside the border.
wiki.against tree: A character is against a tree, usually with their back, while standing or sitting.
wiki.in tree: A character located in the leafy area of a tree (the area where most of the branches are located) via sitting, hanging, etc.
wiki.sitting in tree: Sitting on the branches of a tree.
wiki.standing on liquid: When a character is standing on the surface of a liquid, most often water.
wiki.opening door: A door that is currently in the process of being opened in the image.
wiki.cold: When a character is affected by cold temperatures.
wiki.hot: When a character is affected by hot temperatures.
wiki.headlamp: A type of small flashlight (or other similar illuminating device) worn on the head to provide light while leaving the hands free.
wiki.cloud print: An article of clothing or anything made out of fabric that has the printed motif of clouds.
wiki.starry sky print: Clothing with a print that features star (sky)s, either as viewed from a starry sky or from outer space.
wiki.neon trim: High in contrast and usually luminescent, neon trim are generally be depicted as brightly-glowing or pulsing lines over the surface of an object, clothing or person.
wiki.red skirt: A skirt or miniskirt that is colored red.
wiki.green skirt: A skirt or miniskirt that is colored green.
wiki.grey skirt: A skirt or miniskirt that is colored grey.
wiki.pink skirt: A skirt or miniskirt that is colored pink.
wiki.purple skirt: A skirt or miniskirt that is colored purple. This can range from deep indigo to bright violet.
wiki.layered skirt: A skirt that consists of multiple layers of fabric.
wiki.white pants: Any style of pants that are colored white.
wiki.grey pants: Any style of pants that are colored grey.
wiki.white shorts: Any style of shorts that are colored white.
wiki.black kimono: A kimono that is colored black. This includes other kimono-styled tops such as yukatas and furisodes.
wiki.red kimono: A kimono that is colored red. This includes other kimono-styled tops such as yukatas and furisodes.
wiki.pink kimono: A kimono that is colored pink. This includes other kimono-styled tops such as yukatas and furisodes.
wiki.red hakama: A hakama that is colored red. Traditionally worn by mikos.
wiki.obijime: Obijime is a small decorative string tied around the obi, used only in women's kimono.
wiki.tasuki: A lightweight ribbon or cord used to tie back the sleeves on a yukata or kimono in order to keep them out of the way during cleaning or recreational activities.
wiki.full armor: A full set of armor that covers the head, body, arms, and legs. This tag also applies for an armor set that's on a stand, or if a helmet is unworn but still visible.
wiki.greaves: Piece of medieval armor worn over the shin.
wiki.vambraces: Long armored cuffs worn on the forearm, often with gauntlets. For tagging purposes, use this if the cuff is present but the character is not wearing gauntlets.
wiki.checkered clothes: Clothing with a checkered pattern, which is a series of uniform, repeating squares that alternate between two colors in a diagonal arrangement. The most popular pairing is black and white, but many other combinations exist.
wiki.argyle clothes: Clothing with an argyle pattern - i.e., having repeating diamonds.
wiki.cross-laced clothes: Any type of clothing which has crisscrossing laces, strings, or ribbons.
wiki.asymmetrical clothes: Clothing that differs significantly from one side of the body to the other, either by design, or by way of wearing (style).
wiki.taut clothes: Clothing that is so tight that the fabric ripples, usually between the breasts.
wiki.unbuttoned: An article of clothing with buttons that have been left unfastened, leaving the clothes open.
wiki.raglan sleeves: Raglan sleeves are sleeves attached to a garment via a diagonal seam from the armpit to the neckline (rather than a simple circular seam at the edge of the shoulder). They are often made in a different color than the torso of the garment and are constructed from one piece of material.
wiki.wing collar: A collar with folded-down corners, which form the "wings".
wiki.double-breasted: A type of buttoning usually found on outerwear with two columns of buttons and flaps that overlap rather than meeting at the middle.
wiki.flip-flops: A type of casual sandal, consisting of a flat sole held loosely on the foot by a Y-shaped strap known as a toe thong that passes between the first and second toes and around both sides of the foot.
wiki.pumps: Low-cut, dressy high heels that leave the top of the foot and ankle bare, without any lacing besides a potential ankle strap.
wiki.thighband pantyhose: Pantyhose with a darker band around the thighs.
wiki.black socks: Socks or kneehighs that are black.
wiki.striped thighhighs: Thighhighs or over-kneehighs that are striped.
wiki.brown thighhighs: Thighhighs or over-kneehighs that are brown.
wiki.red thighhighs: Thighhighs or over-kneehighs that are red.
wiki.asymmetrical legwear: Thighhighs, socks, or pantyhose that are different in length, color, or design.
wiki.leg warmers: Thick baggy coverings worn on the lower legs, on top of the socks and shoes, to keep the legs warm. Leg warmers are footless and typically cover the leg from the ankles to the knees.
wiki.naked cape: A cape worn without any other clothing beneath it.
wiki.naked sheet: When a character is nude but partially covered by a sheet or blanket.
wiki.nude cover: A nude person covering their privates with an object, such as a pillow, blanket, bed sheet, or towel.
wiki.partially undressed: When a character is partially undressed relative to what they are wearing.
wiki.bare hips: Clothes that leaves the hips bare. Whether it be a leotard, a swimsuit, a garment that has a side slit or a hip vent or any garment that exposes the hips.
wiki.no shirt: Wearing everything but a shirt. That is, wearing a bra or bikini top with pants (or other bottoms), but without a shirt.
wiki.no pants: Wearing a top and underwear, but no bottoms. For example, wearing a shirt and panties, but no pants or skirt. See bottomless for when a character isn't wearing bottoms or underwear (they're completely naked from the waist down).
wiki.unworn panties: Panties that are visible but not being worn.
wiki.unworn bra: A bra that is not being worn.
wiki.heart pasties: Pasties in the shape of a heart.
wiki.collared dress: A dress with a folded collar.
wiki.long dress: A dress that is beyond knee-length, typically mid-calf-length or beyond.
wiki.pleated dress: A dress with vertical folds of fabric.
wiki.halter dress: A dress held in place with a halterneck.
wiki.layered dress: A dress that consists of multiple layers of fabric.
wiki.strapless leotard: A leotard that is strapless, without any shoulder straps to keep it in place on the upper body.
wiki.black one-piece swimsuit: A one-piece swimsuit that is colored black.
wiki.highleg one-piece swimsuit: A one-piece swimsuit with a much higher legline than usual, showing off more of the wearer's hips.
wiki.naval uniform: A military uniform worn by members of a navy. Typically these will be either white or khaki in summer or tropical regions, and black or very dark blue in winter or cold regions.
wiki.white jacket: A jacket that is colored white.
wiki.brown jacket: A jacket that is colored brown.
wiki.grey jacket: A jacket that is colored grey.
wiki.black coat: A coat that is colored black.
wiki.hooded coat: A coat with a hood attached to it.
wiki.black vest: A vest that is colored black.
wiki.jacket on shoulders: A jacket draped over the shoulders, rather than worn with the arms in the sleeves.
wiki.red cape: A red cape, often worn by superheroes.
wiki.grey shirt: Any style of shirt that's colored grey.
wiki.yellow shirt: Any style of shirt that's colored yellow.
wiki.brown shirt: Any style of shirt that's colored brown.
wiki.cropped shirt: A shirt that is cut short, with its bottom hem lying above the waist, often revealing the wearer's midriff.
wiki.polo shirt: A pullover collared shirt with a placket neckline that normally features three buttons. These shirts are traditionally short sleeved, but long sleeved versions are also available. Some of these shirts may feature a breast pocket.
wiki.undershirt: A light typically collarless shirt or top made to be worn underneath other clothing, such as dress shirts. They're frequently plain and white.
wiki.tied shirt: A shirt tied together at the bottom, usually so that the midriff is exposed.
wiki.black sweater: A sweater that is colored black.
wiki.black camisole: A camisole that is mainly black.
wiki.pink panties: Panties that are predominately pink in color.
wiki.polka dot panties: Panties that have a polka dot pattern on them.
wiki.lace panties: Panties made completely from lace, unlike lace-trimmed panties, which only have lace around the outside.
wiki.thong panties: Panties with a thong back. A thong is a thin strip between the buttocks that leaves most of the butt cheeks bare.
wiki.bow bra: A bra that features a bow as a decoration, or less commonly a front-tie bra that ties together with a bow. Usually the bow is between the breast cups.
wiki.lace-trimmed bra: A bra with lace trim around the edges.
wiki.red bra: A bra or similar upper body lingerie that is colored red.
wiki.single earring: When a character is wearing only one earring on one of their ears.
wiki.bangle: A large stiff ring worn as jewelry around the wrist.
wiki.goggles on head: Goggles worn on the top of the head, instead of on the eyes.
wiki.straw hat: A hat entirely made of straw, the dry stalks of cereal plants after the grain and chaff have been removed.
wiki.mini crown: A crown that is much smaller than a regular sized one.
wiki.headpiece: A decorative type of headwear that is fitted around one's head (usually being fitted near/on the forehead) and doesn't fit the traditional definition of a crown, tiara, hairband, etc.
wiki.bandana: A bandana is a cloth (or strip of cloth) one wears around the head, face or neck for either protective or decorative purposes. It is also worn by high school students for self-motivation.
wiki.wristwatch: A watch worn on the wrist.
wiki.hair tie: A small elastic band used for tying hair into ponytails or other styles. They are made in a wide variety of colors and patterns.
wiki.earmuffs: A winter accessory designed to protect the ears from cold environments, thus preventing frostbite. They often resemble headphones.
wiki.faceless female: A female character who is faceless; her facial features (mainly the eyes) don't appear, either because they're hidden, covered by hair, in shadow, or not drawn at all.
wiki.buzz cut: An all-rounded very short haircut typically done with electric clippers. Stereotypical of high school Japanese baseball players and military recruits.
wiki.bowl cut: A simple short haircut that is the same length all the way around the head, forming the shape of an upside-down bowl.
wiki.inverted bob: A type of bob cut that features a short back and long front. The hair must gradually increase in length as it goes to the front.
wiki.front ponytail: Hair wrapped and tied beneath the chin. Kagiyama Hina is the most popular example of this hairstyle.
wiki.high side ponytail: A side ponytail that is tied high up, close to the top of the head.
wiki.wide ponytail: A ponytail that fans out in the back so that it remains thick despite being tied.
wiki.side braids: Braids hanging on the side of the face, anywhere other than in front of the ears.
wiki.nape braid: A braid wrapped around the nape area, if the braid runs on the sides of the head use half up braid or half up half down braid instead.
wiki.low-braided long hair: Long hair that is braided down low, at the bottom or middle, but not at the top.
wiki.single side bun: A single hair bun at the side of the head rather than the back.
wiki.side up bun: A single hair bun or double buns on the side of the head, with the rest of the hair hanging normally. The hair bun equivalent of one side up and two side up.
wiki.long sidelocks: Sidelocks that are shoulder-length or longer. If they are waist-length, use very long sidelocks. If they are body-length, use absurdly long sidelocks.
wiki.red streaks: Streaked hair where the streaks are red.
wiki.blue streaks: Streaked hair where the streaks are blue.
wiki.black streaks: Streaked hair where the streaks are black.
wiki.pink streaks: Streaked hair where the streaks are pink.
wiki.fiery hair: Hair that is, or appear to be, made of fire. Can also apply to tails and creatures.
wiki.colored sclera: When the sclera - the white part of the eye - is a color other than white.
wiki.symbol in eye: When any kind of symbol is part of a character's eyes, but is not related to the symbol-shaped pupils. For instance, a person may have blue eyes, normal pupils, and the glint seen from reflected light, but has the addition of a pink flower symbol somewhere in the blue portion.
wiki.solid circle eyes: Eyes drawn as solid black circles, or a solid circle of another color with or without an outline. Usually seen in chibi characters.
wiki.thick eyelashes: Eyelashes that are much thicker and more pronounced than usual. It tends on the artist's style, but the lashes can be so large that they can be seen even in a thumbnail, or they can be noticeably clumped together.
wiki.horizontal pupils: Pupils that are horizontal or rectangular in shape instead of circular. Horizontal pupils are common in animals such as sheep, goats, horses, octopodes, reptiles and amphibians.
wiki.star in eye: A star (symbol) shape inside someone's eyes.
wiki.red sclera: When the normally white part of the eyes are red.
wiki.yellow pupils: A character with yellow pupils. Not to be confused with yellow eyes, for when the iris (part surrounding the pupil) as yellow, or yellow sclera for when the normally white sclera are colored yellow.
wiki.x-shaped pupils: When a character's pupils are shaped like an X. Not to be confused with + + or x x.
wiki.whisker markings: Facial marks on the cheeks resembling whiskers.
wiki.body markings: Markings on the skin that are unnatural (not moles, freckles, birthmarks, etc.), and are either a natural trait of the character (possibly shared by others of their clan, race or species), or of an ambiguous nature. It may be unclear whether the markings are tattoos, makeup, bodypaint, tanlines, or something else.
wiki.star facial mark: A facial mark/facial tattoo shaped like a star.
wiki.birthmark: A birthmark is a congenital, benign irregularity on the skin which is present at birth or appears shortly after birth, usually in the first month.
wiki.scar on stomach: A scar located on a person's stomach.
wiki.scar on chest: A scar on a character's chest.
wiki.scar on arm: A scar located on a person's arms.
wiki.flower tattoo: A tattoo shaped like any kind of flower, whether it'd be realistic or abstract in design.
wiki.shoulder tattoo: A tattoo located on the shoulder or upper arm area.
wiki.chest tattoo: A tattoo located on the upper chest. For men, this can be anywhere on the abs. For women, it is on the upper chest area above the breasts.
wiki.one-piece tan: Tanlines created by a one-piece swimsuit, leotard, or other similar garment.
wiki.bikini tan: Tanlines created by any type of bikini or by a bra, sports bra, or other underwear, including both a top and bottom tans.
wiki.cracked skin: Skin that is cracked, as if the person is composed of brittle material such as stone.
wiki.wrinkled skin: Lines and creases that form on the skin as a person ages. Can be caused by age, sun exposure, smoking, pollution, etc.
wiki.very sweaty: Heavy sweating. Typically illustrated with numerous sweat drops, rivulets of sweat, along with other signs of exertion such as heavy breathing or a steaming body.
wiki.turn pale: When the color is washed out of a character's face because they are shocked, horrified, disgusted, scared, depressed, or otherwise drained of emotion. Can also show that the character is sick or is comedically giving up the ghost.
wiki.dirty: Dirt, filth, or mud on someone or something.
wiki.dirty face: Mud, dirt, or other grime on a person's face.
wiki.ear blush: A blush that covers the ears. May indicate extreme embarrassment.
wiki.purple nails: Fingernails and/or toenails that are colored purple.
wiki.green nails: Fingernails and/or toenails that are colored green.
wiki.aqua nails: Fingernails and/or toenails that are colored aqua.
wiki.yellow nails: Fingernails and/or toenails that are colored yellow.
wiki.orange nails: Fingernails and/or toenails that are colored orange.
wiki.white nails: Fingernails and/or toenails that are colored white.
wiki.multicolored nails: When a character has fingernails and/or toenails featuring a variety of colors, typically (but not exclusively) as a result of selective application of nail polish. Each nail may have different colors, or the nails can have multiple colors on each one, such as a ladybug or rainbow pattern.

wiki.viera: A race of mostly female rabbit-like humanoids from the Ivalice realm of the Final Fantasy series.

wiki.hand over own mouth: When a character uses their hand(s) to cover their own mouth.
wiki.partially underwater shot: When the image is divided into two by the water's surface; in other words, the "camera" is partially submerged.
wiki.pov across table: When the viewer is assumed to be sitting across the table from a character. It may also be used with table-like surfaces such as counters and desks.
wiki.aiming at viewer: A character aiming a gun or any type of weapon at the viewer. Sometimes used for other objects pointed at the viewer, like a camera or a hose.
wiki.female pov: A first-person point of view from a female character's perspective.
wiki.facing to the side: A character facing to their side with closed or covered eyes.

wiki.pillarboxed: A technique where vertical bars are displayed on the left and right sides of a picture. The opposite of letterboxed.

wiki.wiping tears: The act of removing tears from one's face, typically by hand, sleeve, or tissue.

wiki.crescent facial mark: A facial mark or facial tattoo shaped like a crescent.

wiki.hand on own stomach: Placing a single hand on one's own stomach.

wiki.dot mouth: A character's mouth is portrayed as only a small dot beneath their nose.
wiki.blank stare: A facial expression characterized by a lack of emotion, understanding, or focus. Suggests confusion, disinterest or even that a character isn't thinking about anything.
