wiki.no eyebrows: When a character has no eyebrows at all. Should not be used if the eyebrows are simply covered by a hat or hair.
wiki.blunt tresses: Hair that has been separated from the rest into sidelocks, ringlets, etc., and then been freshly cut flat. Typically tied with a tress ribbon or bunched together to create a tassel-like appearance. Akashi from Kancolle is a prominent example of someone with these.
wiki.long sideburns: Sideburns that go past the ears reaching down to the jaw, sometimes projecting towards the cheek. Usually with goatee or stubble on the chin. Use together with the beard tag if the beard is formed of stubble and long sideburns.
wiki.split ponytail: A ponytail that splits at the base into two or more tails.
wiki.prehensile hair: Hair that is capable of movements by thought, commonly (though not exclusively) by shaping itself like a hand or tentacle.
wiki.hair spread out: When someone's hair spreads out over a surface due to gravity. Usually found on girls with long hair lying on their back or absurdly long hair that reaches beyond the floor.
wiki.multiple braids: A hairstyle that consists of three or more braided lengths of hair.
wiki.updo: A women's hairstyle where the hair is tied up and held high at the back of the head, usually in a more elaborate style than a simple hair bun or ponytail. The hair may be held in place by braids, hairclips, hair sticks, or hair ties.
wiki.loose hair strand: Single strands of hair that are drawn out of place, separated from the rest of the hair.
wiki.low-tied sidelocks: Sidelocks that have been tied at the middle or the bottom of the locks.
wiki.hair flowing over: Long, flowing hair that is draped over an object, item, or irregular surface in such a way that demonstrates proper observation of hair physics and/or gravity.
wiki.broken horn: A character with a single broken horn. If both of the horns are broken, use broken horns instead.
wiki.dog tail: A character with a dog-like tail.
wiki.mouse tail: A tail of a mouse (animal), which is usually wiry and lacking fur, as compared to other tails.
wiki.raccoon tail: Use this tag if a character has a tail resembling a raccoon's or a tanuki's. → tail, raccoon, tanuki, raccoon ears
wiki.tiger tail: A long striped tiger-like tail seen on tiger girls and tiger boys.
wiki.shark tail: A character with a shark-like tail, with vertical fins. See cetacean tail for tails with horizontal fins.
wiki.squirrel tail: Use this tag when a character has a tail of a squirrel. → tail, squirrel, squirrel ears
wiki.lion tail: Use this tag when a character has a tail reminiscent of a lion's tail. → tail, lion, lion ears
wiki.monkey tail: A tail from a monkey. Very long, flexible, and strong enough to wrap around tree branches for monkeys to hang off of.
wiki.bird tail: A tail shaped like a bird's.
wiki.ghost tail: A wispy tail making up someone's bottom half in place of legs. Commonly seen on ghosts and genies.
wiki.snake tail: A character is depicted as having a snake's tail. Not for when a character is depicted as having the lower body of a snake, such posts should be tagged with lamia instead.
wiki.spiked tail: A tail with spikes on it.
wiki.heart tail: A tail or multiple tails bent in the shape of a heart. A common visual gag used for Valentine's Day-themed pictures or as a general sign of affection.
wiki.cow tail: Use this tag when a character has a cow-like tail. → cow, tail, cow girl, cow ears, cow horns
wiki.mini wings: Wings on the back that are smaller than usual.
wiki.multicolored wings: A pair of wings that have at least two or more colors present, either as a gradient or otherwise.
wiki.purple wings: A pair of wings that are colored purple.
wiki.spread wings: Wings that are spread wide open.
wiki.sharp teeth: When a character has sharp, pointed teeth. Differs from fangs in that all of the character's teeth are sharp.
wiki.fangs: A character with multiple prominent canine teeth, such as with vampires or various animals.
wiki.fang out: When a character shows a single fang outside a closed mouth.
wiki.round teeth: A wide, open-mouthed smile where the front upper teeth are drawn as a single round semicircle.
wiki.buck teeth: When the two upper front teeth project forward to such a degree, that they are very prominent and obvious.
wiki.lower teeth only: When only the lower teeth are drawn in the mouth.
wiki.long tongue: A tongue that reaches past the chin when extended.
wiki.forked tongue: A tongue that splits part way down, usually close to the end. Occurs naturally on many reptilians. The negative assocations with reptiles and snakes has led to demons also having forked tongues.
wiki.colored tongue: A tongue having an uncommon color.
wiki.blue tongue: A tongue that is colored blue. If a character has their mouth open and the rest of the mouth is also blue, that can count under this tag.
wiki.tail raised: A tail that is lifted up rather than hanging naturally.
wiki.prehensile tail: A tail capable of holding or grabbing.
wiki.bandaid on hand: A bandaid on a person's hand.
wiki.facial tattoo: A tattoo located on the face.
wiki.back tattoo: A tattoo located on the back.
wiki.breast tattoo: A tattoo located on the breast.
wiki.stomach tattoo: A tattoo on the stomach, but not above the pubic area like a pubic tattoo.
wiki.star tattoo: A tattoo of a star (symbol) symbol.
wiki.hand tattoo: A tattoo located on the hand.
wiki.barcode tattoo: A tattoo of a barcode. One notable example is Agent 47 of the Hitman (Game) franchise, who has a very obvious one on the back of his head.
wiki.mole on thigh: A mole located on someone's thigh.
wiki.mole on neck: A mole that is located on a person's neck.
wiki.mole above mouth: A mole placed just above the mouth, but not on the cheek.
wiki.scar on nose: A scar on a character's nose.
wiki.riding pokemon: Someone is riding a Pokémon. This tag should not be used for someone having sex with a Pokémon.
wiki.imminent kiss: The moment just before when two characters are about to kiss.
wiki.after kiss: The moment after a kiss. Often accompanied by a saliva trail, leftover lipstick marks, or implied by wiping one's mouth.
wiki.pocky kiss: When two people bite a piece of pocky at both ends and, as they eat more of the pocky, grow closer to each other until there's no more pocky left and they kiss.
wiki.untying: Undoing a ribbon or string-tied garment. Examples include bowties or ribbons on many school uniforms, side-tie bikini bottoms or side-tie panties, and hair ribbons.
wiki.poking: The act of jabbing the index finger or a blunt object against a soft object, popularly used on fleshy parts of the skin such as the cheek and the breast.
wiki.confession: A character making or reacting to a confession of love.
wiki.comforting: A character trying to ease another's sadness.
wiki.knees apart feet together: Someone with knees apart, feet together. In contrast with knees together feet apart.
wiki.hand on own leg: When a character's hand is on their leg.
wiki.elbow rest: Resting one or both elbows on something, such as a surface, object, or one's own body.
wiki.spread fingers: When a character's fingers are spread or splayed wide, with each digit well apart from the others.
wiki.bowlegged pose: Standing while squatting slightly with knees pointed outward, contracting the glutes to emphasize the crotch by pushing it forward. Often accompanied by arms behind head and leaning back.
wiki.heel up: Standing with both feet on the ground and one heel raised up.
wiki.on shoulder: An animal, creature, or person resting or sitting on someone's shoulder.
wiki.cheek bulge: Something pushing against the inside of a character's mouth, making their cheek bulge out. For things pushing against the outside of a character's face, use cheek poking.
wiki.uvula: A small, fleshy, finger-like flap of tissue that hangs from the back of the throat and is an extension of the soft palate.
wiki.spitting: The act of expelling saliva and/or phlegm from the mouth.
wiki.pain: A symptom of some physical injury or bodily suffering. The usual expression of pain is wincing and tears. In more comical images pain can be indicated by "pain-lines", a lightning bolt that hovers over the injured area, a giant bandaid, or a character cowering in front of their attacker or holding their head.
wiki.xd: A facial expression that combines > < eyes with a wide open smile (:D). A happy expression; often indicates that the character is laughing.
wiki.o3o: The emoticon of loose or puckered lips, shaped like the number 3.
wiki.u u: A facial expression similar to ^ ^, except the eyes curve downwards in a 'U' shape. Commonly used when a character's eyes are closed while relaxing or thinking.
wiki.weapon over shoulder: Holding or carrying a weapon over the shoulder.
wiki.weapon on back: A weapon worn on the back. Use the applicable weapon tag (often sword or rifle) together with this tag.
wiki.sword over shoulder: A sword held or carried over the shoulder.
wiki.sword on back: A sword worn on a person's back.
wiki.reverse grip: A knife grip in which the knife is held with the blade pointing down, from the bottom of the fist, rather than the top ("natural" or "hammer" grip) of the closed fist. This grip makes stabbing downwards easier.
wiki.hand on hilt: When a character's hand is idly touching or resting upon the hilt of their own sword, usually unsheathed and planted in the ground.
wiki.finger on trigger: Holding a gun with the finger on the trigger or inside the trigger guard, especially when not prepared to safely fire it. The opposite of trigger discipline.
wiki.drawing sword: Pulling a sword out of something. In most cases this something will be a sheath and the unsheathing tag should be used as well. Exceptions to this include images where the sheath itself isn't visible, or where the sword is being drawn from something else entirely.
wiki.holstered: When a weapon (usually a handgun) is placed on a holster. The weapon must be visible to the viewer.
wiki.hand on another's ass: When someone has a hand on someone else's ass, such as to lift them up or pull them closer.
wiki.twirling hair: Fidgeting with one's hair by twirling it around one's finger, usually a sign of nervousness.
wiki.hair twirling: Fidgeting with one's hair by twirling it around one's finger, usually a sign of nervousness.
wiki.finger to cheek: A character distinctly placing their finger, often the index finger, on their cheek.
wiki.finger to own chin: A character placing one of their fingers upon their own chin. Usually indicates pensiveness or puzzlement, occasionally amusement or smugness.
wiki.licking finger: Licking of fingers. Sometimes done for suggestive purposes.
wiki.pocky in mouth: A stick of pocky held in the mouth. The character may be eating it or it may be a prelude to a pocky kiss.
wiki.teasing: Provocative behavior intended to raise a particular emotion. Can be done for romantic, sexual, friendly, or bullying related reasons.
wiki.arm around another's waist: A character wrapping their arm around another character's waist.
wiki.hand on another's hip: When a character's hand is on another character's hip.
wiki.kissing forehead: A kiss on the forehead. Generally used as a term of endearment.
wiki.sexually suggestive: A sexual innuendo; doing something that hints at sex or that appears sexual when technically it's not. For example, making a penetration gesture, being covered in a suggestive fluid, or sucking on a popsicle suggestively.
wiki.yellow theme: An image where yellow is the dominant color. For example, a monochrome image that is yellow, or an image with an overall yellow color theme.
wiki.horror (theme): An image that provokes fear, uneasiness or dread from the viewer. If a character seems to feel this way but the image as a whole is not creepy to the viewer, then use horrified instead.
wiki.orange theme: An image where orange is the dominant color. For example, a monochrome image that is orange, or an image with an overall orange color theme.
wiki.black theme: An image where black is the dominant color.
wiki.white theme: An image where white is the dominant color.
wiki.brown theme: An image where brown is the dominant color. For example, a monochrome image that is brown, or an image with an overall brown color theme.
wiki.reference sheet: An image depicting the details of a design. A reference sheet usually consists of multiple views of the same subject from different angles, with notes pointing out the details of the design, and sometimes with details such as clothing or accessories drawn separately for characters.
wiki.turnaround: A character, often full body, shown from multiple views about their vertical axis while usually keeping the same pose and outfit. A technique commonly used on reference sheets to demonstrate a character's entire design.
wiki.column lineup: A group of characters (generally more than two) arranged in distinct columns or rows, with separating lines between them.
wiki.collage: A collection of several images in one, usually of screencaps or characters drawn by different artists.
wiki.clone: Two or more instances of the same character in the same scene. The instances should be completely identical and wearing the same outfit; if they're not identical, it may be multiple persona instead.
wiki.animalization: When a character who is not normally an animal is portrayed as an animal or creature.
wiki.romper: A one-piece garment combining a shirt and shorts. In the early 1900s they were primarily worn by children as playwear, but were also popular in the 50s, 70s, and 2000s as women's fashion.
wiki.cupless bra: A bra without cups; also called a open-cup bra. Designs vary, but in general the bra consists of only straps or strings that encircle the breasts, with no cups to cover the breasts or nipples.
wiki.cheek pinching: Pinching one's own or someone else's cheeks. Often used on oneself to check if they're dreaming, or used on children as a painful alternative to a headpat.
wiki.covered penis: When the shape of someone's penis is visible beneath their clothing, commonly seen with skin tight clothes or as a form of censoring.
wiki.oral invitation: Blatantly offering to receive an ejaculation in one's open mouth.
wiki.futa on male: A futanari being the dominant sexual partner over a male. This typically means that the futa is the one penetrating.
wiki.yor briar: One of the three main characters of Spy x Family. She is an assassin under the code name "Thorn Princess".
wiki.twilight (spy x family): One of the three main characters of Spy x Family. He is a spy with his real name unrevealed; he uses "Twilight" as his code name. Also known by his cover civilian name Loid Forger.
wiki.yuri briar: Character from Spy x Family. Yuri Briar is the younger brother of Yor Briar. While officially a civil servant for the Ostanian Ministry for Foreign Affairs, in truth, he is a member of the State Security Service (SSS), the Ostanian Secret Police, a Stasi-like organization that aims to maintain order in Ostania by surve…
wiki.fiona frost: A deuteragonist from Spy x Family.
wiki.kochou shinobu: Shinobu Kocho is a major supporting character of Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba.
wiki.kanroji mitsuri: A character in Kimetsu no Yaiba.
wiki.rengoku kyoujurou: Supporting character in Kimetsu no Yaiba.
wiki.tomioka giyuu: Supporting character in Kimetsu no Yaiba.
wiki.iguro obanai: Supporting character in Kimetsu no Yaiba. Has a white snake pet called Kaburamaru, usually wrapped around his neck.
wiki.uzui tengen: Supporting character in Kimetsu no Yaiba. Has three wives: Makio (kimetsu no yaiba), Hinatsuru (kimetsu no yaiba), and Suma (kimetsu no yaiba).
wiki.douma (kimetsu no yaiba): Kimetsu No Yaiba character. A emotionless demon and Upper Rank 2 of the Twelve Kizuki. He is a pale, young-looking man with rainbow eyes and multicolored hair -- primarily blonde, with a black and red pattern resembling a stain on the top of his head.
wiki.levi (shingeki no kyojin): Corporal Levi (リヴァイ) is a character from Shingeki no Kyojin, has short black hair and black eyes, usually dual wielding two swords.
wiki.hange zoe: A character from Shingeki no Kyojin.
wiki.erwin smith: Chracter in Shingeki No Kyojin. Voiced by Ono Daisuke.
wiki.petra ral: A character in Shingeki no Kyojin. A member of the Scout Regiment. .
wiki.pieck finger: Shingeki no Kyojin character. Voiced by Numakura Manami.
wiki.mizuhara chizuru: A character in Kanojo Okarishimasu. She is a 19-year-old (later 20-year-old) college student at Nerima University. She works part-time as a rental girlfriend. Her real name is Ichinose Chizuru.
wiki.arsene lupin iii: The protagonist of Lupin III. The grandson of Maurice Leblanc's Arsène Lupin, he's a gentlemen thief with a goofy personality, who seems to enjoy the act of stealing than the item itself. Wears an iconic open suit jacket and necktie of varying colors depending on the series or movie. Notable user of the Walther P38.
wiki.jigen daisuke: A Lupin III character. The partner-in-crime of Arsene Lupin Iii. He wears a suit with a fedora that usually covers his eyes.
wiki.mine fujiko: The only female member of Arsene Lupin III's posse, Fujiko is a classic femme fatale who has no problem betraying Lupin so she can steal something valuable. She is excellent with espionage and flirting with her enemies to get what she wants, but she tends to get captured often.
wiki.ishikawa goemon xiii: A character in Lupin III. He is a samurai descended from the legendary Ishikawa Goemon. He is part of Lupin's posse.
wiki.ghislaine dedoldia: Ghislaine Dedoldia from Mushoku Tensei is a former member of the party Fangs of the Black Wolf, a group that once included Paul Greyrat and Elinalise Dragonroad. She previously served as a bodyguard for the Boreas family and holds a King rank in the Sword God Style, having trained under the Sword God, Gal Farion.
wiki.eris greyrat (adult): Grown up version of Eris Greyrat from Mushoku Tensei, who first appears in Volume of the light novel.
wiki.gojo satoru: One of the main characters of Jujutsu Kaisen.
wiki.gojou satoru: One of the main characters of Jujutsu Kaisen.
wiki.nanami kento: Kento Nanami is a supporting character in Jujutsu Kaisen.
wiki.fushiguro toji: Recurring character in Jujutsu Kaisen. Fushiguro Megumi's father.
wiki.mahito (jujutsu kaisen): A special-grade cursed spirit_(jujutsu_kaisen) in Jujutsu Kaisen. Usually appears as a young male with blue hair, brown and blue heterochromic eyes and stitches on his skin.
wiki.mei mei (jujutsu kaisen): Jujutsu Kaisen character. Ui Ui (Jujutsu Kaisen)'s elder sister. She has white hair with multiple braids: braided bangs over one eye and a braided ponytail. She wears a dark purple turtleneck jumpsuit with juliet sleeves and brown knee boots.
wiki.ubel (sousou no frieren): Sousou no Frieren character. Voiced by Hasegawa Ikumi. Her name means "nasty" in German.
wiki.himmel (sousou no frieren): Himmel is the Hero of the Hero Party in Sousou no Frieren, which consisted of Priest Heiter, Mage Frieren, and Warrior Eisen (sousou no frieren). His name means "sky" in German.
wiki.eisen (sousou no frieren): Eisen is a Dwarf and the Warrior of the Hero Party, alongside Priest Heiter, Mage Frieren, and Hero Himmel.
wiki.heiter: Heiter was the alcohol-loving priest of the Hero Party, which consisted of Hero Himmel, Mage Frieren, and Warrior Eisen. Heiter is known as a drunkard, which is why Frieren calls him a "Corrupt Priest".
wiki.hisoka morow: A character from Hunter x Hunter, serving as one of the main antagonists of the series.
wiki.chrollo lucilfer: Character from Hunter x Hunter and the main antagonist of the Yorknew City arc.
wiki.illumi zoldyck: A character from the Hunter x Hunter series.
wiki.leorio paladiknight: One of the four main characters of Hunter x Hunter.
wiki.shion (tensei shitara slime datta ken): Tensei Shitara Slime Datta Ken character. A well endowed female ogre who is also a terrible cook. One of the six survivors of the ogre village.
wiki.mirko: A character from Boku no Hero Academia. A professional Japanese hero with "rabbit" quirk, granting her various rabbit-like abilities such as immensely strong legs, capable of jumping at a great height, and superhuman hearing ability. Her civilian name is Usagiyama Rumi.
wiki.endeavor (boku no hero academia): Pro hero from Boku no Hero Academia. He married Todoroki Rei and became the father of Todoroki Shoto, Todoroki Fuyumi, Todoroki Natsuo and Todoroki Touya. He has red hair and blue eyes. His beard and clothing appear to be on fire.
wiki.hawks (boku no hero academia): Character from Boku no Hero Academia. He has blonde, short hair, yellow eyes, forked eyebrows and red, feathered wings. He may often be seen wearing a fur-trimmed jacket with long, fur-trimmed sleeves. There may be goatee stubble on his face.
wiki.eraser head (boku no hero academia): The pro hero Eraser Head from Boku no Hero Academia, although he is very obscure outside of U.A. since he dislikes media attention. He is the homeroom teacher of Class 1-A.
wiki.all might: Character from Boku no Hero Academia. The #1 superhero and a symbol of strength and the eighth hero of the "One For All" linage. He was mentored by Shimura Nana and in turn mentors Midoriya Izuku.
wiki.shigaraki tomura: Main antagonist of Boku no Hero Academia. He is a powerful villain who has messy grey hair and numerous hands that cover his upper body and his face.
wiki.dabi (boku no hero academia): Character from Boku no Hero Academia.
wiki.yagi toshinori: The civillian identity of All Might. For tagging purposes, the name will be kept to his true, frailer form as well as his younger self rather than tagging both versions as Yagi.
wiki.mount lady: A neophyte Pro Hero from Boku no Hero Academia with the power to become a giantess. Her real name is Takeyama Yuu.
wiki.bakugou mitsuki: Character in Boku no Hero Academia. Mother of Bakugou Katsuki and wife to Bakugou Masaru.
wiki.lady nagant: Character from Boku No Hero Academia, introduced as an antagonist during the Dark Hero Arc. She is a mature female with purple and pink hair, and wears a medium-length sleeveless purple dress.
wiki.echidna (re:zero): A character from Re:Zero Kara Hajimeru Isekai Seikatsu. She is the Witch of Greed.
wiki.tatsumaki: A character from One-Punch Man. Her full hero name is Senritsu no Tatsumaki (戦慄のタツマキ, Tornado of Terror), Terrible Tornado in the official translation, and she is the 2nd place ranked S-class hero in the Heroes Association. She is Fubuki (one-punch_man)'s older sister and a powerful telekinetic/psychic.
wiki.fubuki (one-punch man): A character from One-Punch Man. Her full hero name is Jigoku no Fubuki (地獄のフブキ, lit. Blizzard of Hell, Hellish Blizzard in the official translation), and she is the 1st place ranked B-class hero of the Heroes Association. She is Tatsumaki's younger sister and a powerful telekinetic/psychic.
wiki.saitama (one-punch man): The main protagonist character from the One-Punch Man series.
wiki.genos: A superhero character from One-punch Man. The 16th rank S-class hero, aka "Demon Cyborg".
wiki.onsoku no sonic: A character from One-punch Man. Aka Speed-o'-Sound Sonic. A master ninja assassin who uses his eponymous superhuman speed to confuse his enemies. Also, a dude.
wiki.nami (one piece): One Piece character. The navigator of the Straw Hat Pirates. She has an adopted sister named Nojiko (one piece). Her goal is to create a map of the entire world.
wiki.nico robin: One of the main characters of the manga and anime One Piece. She is the archaeologist of the Straw Hat Pirates.
wiki.roronoa zoro: "Pirate Hunter" Roronoa Zoro is of the main characters of the manga and anime One Piece. He is one of the main fighters of the Straw Hat Pirates, surpassed only by his captain.
wiki.sanji (one piece): "Black Leg" Vinsmoke Sanji is one of the main characters of the manga and anime One Piece. He is a member of the Straw Hat Pirates, serving as cook and fighter. Sanji's life goal is finding the All Blue, a legendary sea where all oceans of the One Piece world meet, giving a cook the opportunity to make a truly global a…
wiki.trafalgar law: One Piece character. One of the Eleven Supernova and captain and doctor of the Heart Pirates. He became one of the Shichibukai, but his position was revoked for allying with Luffy.
wiki.yamato (one piece): One Piece character. Daughter of Kaidou (one piece), though she identifies herself as a man and refers to herself as "Oden" .
wiki.boa hancock: One Piece character. She is the captain of the 4th Kuja Pirates and the current empress of Amazon Lily. Also known as the "Snake Princess" and "Pirate Empress", titles reflecting her status as the strongest on the island and being the world's most beautiful woman and one of the youngest Shichibukai.
wiki.portgas d. ace: One Piece character. Luffy and Sabo (One Piece)'s adoptive brother. 2nd division commander in the Whitebeard Pirates.
wiki.perona: One Piece character. One of the "mysterious four", "Ghost Princess" Perona commanded the Wild and Surprise zombies aboard Thriller Bark. Commonly seen with her pet zombie/stuffed toy Kumacy.
wiki.uta (one piece): Character from One Piece Film: RED. She's voiced by Nazuka Kaori, while her singing voice is provided by Ado (utaite). She is the adopted daughter of Shanks (one piece).
wiki.donquixote doflamingo: One Piece character. The captain of the Donquixote Pirates. King of Dressrosa and one of the Shichibukai.
wiki.crocodile (one piece): One Piece character, first introduced as one of the Shichibukai and the leader of the criminal organization Baroque Works under the codename Mr. 0. He later on co-founded Cross Guild with Dracule Mihawk and served as one of the de-facto leaders.
wiki.franky (one piece): One Piece character. Born as Cutty Flam, Franky is the cyborg shipwright of the Straw Hat Pirates. His life goal is to build a ship to explore the whole world.
wiki.brook (one piece): "Soul King" Brook is one of the main characters of the manga and anime One Piece. He was invited into the Straw Hat pirate crew by their captain, and joined as the crew's musician and second sword fighter (he usually uses a sword hidden in his cane).
wiki.sabo (one piece): A major One Piece character. He is the adoptive brother of Monkey D. Luffy and Portgas D. Ace and chief of staff in Monkey D. Dragon's Revolutionary Army.
wiki.dracule mihawk: One Piece character. First introduced as one of the Shichibukai and later become the de-facto co-leader of Cross Guild along with Crocodile (one piece).
wiki.donquixote rocinante: One Piece character. He is the second son Donquixote Homing and the younger brother of Donquixote Doflamingo. The former Corazon of the Donquixote Pirates,
wiki.shanks (one piece): A character of One Piece. Captain of the "Red-hair Pirates", he used to be a crew member of "Pirate King" Gol D. Roger. He was the one who gave Monkey D. Luffy his signature straw hat and inspired him to become a pirate after he lost his left arm in a fight against a Sea King to protect young Luffy.
wiki.eustass kid: One Piece character. One of the Eleven Supernova and captain of the Kid Pirates. He is a rival of the fellow Supernovas Monkey D. Luffy and Trafalgar Law. During the timeskip, he challenged the Emperor Shanks (one piece) and ended up losing his left arm after the battle with his first mate Benn Beckman.
wiki.jinbe (one piece): One Piece character. Took over as Captain of the Sun Pirates after Fisher Tiger died, formerly one of the Shichibukai. Later becomes the helmsman of the Straw Hat Pirates. His goal is to see humans and fish-men coexist peacefully.
wiki.kaidou (one piece): One Piece character, and the main antagonist of the Wano arc. He is the captain of the Beast Pirates, the tyrannical ruler of the Wano nation, and father of Yamato (one piece).
wiki.law-chan: A genderswaped version of Trafalgar Law from One Piece.
wiki.buggy the clown: One Piece character. Captain of a circus-themed pirate ship and Luffy's rival. Formerly one of the Shichibukai, and later on the leader of the Cross Guild
wiki.marco (one piece): One Piece character. Marco the Phoenix is the 1st division commander of the Whitebeard Pirates.
wiki.tashigi: One Piece character. A Marine ensign under the command of Smoker. She bears an uncanny resemblance to Shimotsuki Kuina, which makes Roronoa Zoro uncomfortable.
wiki.tsunade (naruto): A supporting character in the anime/manga Naruto (series). She is the best healer in the ninja world and one of the legendary Sannin, together with Jiraiya (naruto) and Orochimaru (naruto).
wiki.hatake kakashi: A supporting character in Naruto (series). An elite ninja who trained Uzumaki Naruto, Uchiha Sasuke and Haruno Sakura as the leader of Team 7 (naruto). Later became the Sixth Hokage.
wiki.konan (naruto): A villain from the Naruto (series) manga and anime series, appearing in Naruto Shippuuden. Member of the Akatsuki group of criminals. She is the only woman in the group.
wiki.namikaze minato: Naruto (series) character also known by his nickname of The Yellow Flash (黄色い閃光, kiiroi senkou).
wiki.deidara (naruto): A villain from the Naruto_(series) manga and anime series. Member of the Akatsuki group of criminals. On the first official character poll where he appeared, he came third.
wiki.mitarashi anko: A kunoichi from the Naruto (series) franchise. She is a special jonin and proctor of the Chuunin exams. The legendary sannin Orochimaru (naruto) was her sensei before he defected from Konoha, and Anko hates him to the present, but she uses many of the techniques she learned from him.
wiki.android 18: Character from the Dragon Ball series. The twin sister of Android 17, wife of Kuririn and mother of Marron (dragon ball).
wiki.vegeta: A major character in the Dragon Ball franchise, first introduced in Dragon Ball Z. Vegeta made his appearance in chapter #204 "Sayonara, Son Goku", published in Weekly Shounen Jump magazine on January 7, 1989, seeking the wish-granting Dragon Balls to achieve immortality.
wiki.android 21: A female android introduced in Dragon Ball FighterZ.
wiki.piccolo: Character from the Dragon Ball franchise. He is a Namekian and the reincarnation of Piccolo Daimaou, later on fused with Nail (dragon ball) and Kami-sama (dragon ball). Introduced as Piccolo Jr.
wiki.majin android 21: The initial playable form of Android 21 in Dragon Ball FighterZ. After transforming, Android 21 has the appearance of a female Majin - white hair, pink skin, red eyes with black sclera and pointy ears, as well as a tail. In battle, she is capable of copying her opponent's abilities, as well as turning them into food.
wiki.gogeta: The fused form of Goku and Vegeta after performing the Fusion Dance properly. Originally an anime-only character that never appeared in the manga, appearing only in Dragon Ball Z Movie 12, Fusion Reborn, in the Super Saiyan form, and in the Dragon Ball GT anime, in the Super Saiyan 4 form.
wiki.broly (dragon ball super): The main antagonist of Dragon Ball Movie 20, Dragon Ball Super Broly, alongside his father Paragus (dragon ball super), serving under Frieza. Originally an anime-only character, only designed by Toriyama, now under his supervision for this movie.
wiki.frieza: Frieza is one of the main antagonists of the Dragon Ball franchise, first introduced in Dragon Ball Z as the titular main antagonist of the Frieza Saga.
wiki.vegetto: The fused form of Goku and Vegeta while they're both wearing Potara earrings, first appearing during Dragon Ball Z, fighting Super Buu in his Super Saiyan form, and later during Dragon Ball Super, battling with Zamasu in his Super Saiyan Blue form. His name is a portmanteau of Vegeta and Kakarotto.
wiki.broly (dragon ball z): The main antagonist of Dragon Ball Z Movies 8 and 10, Broly: Legendary Super Saiyan and Broly: Second Coming, with a variation of the character, Bio Broly, serving as the antagonist of Movie 11, Bio-Broly. He is the son of Paragus (dragon ball z).
wiki.cheelai: Dragon Ball Super character, introduced in the Broly movie. She's a short lime green skinned alien humanoid, with purple eyes, short white hair, thin white eyebrows, and a slender, toned build.
wiki.lunch (dragon ball): One of the side characters from the original Dragon Ball manga and anime. A seemingly gentle and ordinary girl. However, she transforms into a hot-tempered and trigger-happy alter-ego whenever she sneezes. Though she's unable to remember anything after reverting back to her normal persona.

wiki.muten roushi: Muten Roushi, or Kamesennin, is the master of the Turtle school of martial arts in the Dragon Ball universe. He is the creator of the legendary Kamehameha (dragon ball) attack which would later become Son Goku's signature technique, and is a notoriously dirty old man.
wiki.final form frieza: Frieza's true form, and his most iconic.
wiki.android 17: Character from the Dragon Ball series. The twin brother of Android 18.
wiki.lunch (bad) (dragon ball): The blonde-haired version of Lunch (Dragon Ball) from Dragon Ball, a hot-tempered and trigger-happy teenage girl full of potent rage, often engaging in criminal acts and using firearms.
wiki.goku black: Primary antagonist of the Future Trunks arc of Dragon Ball Super who looks exactly like Goku. Desires to exterminate all mortals for the sake of "justice" in Future Trunks's timeline. Has a unique Super Saiyan Rose transformation.
wiki.shihouin yoruichi: A Bleach character. She is the former (22nd) head of the Shihōin Clan, one of Soul Society's four great noble houses. She also served as captain of the 2nd Division of the Gotei 13 and as commander of the Onmitsukidō. Shihouin Yuushirou is her younger brother.
wiki.matsumoto rangiku: A Soul Reaper from the Manga/Anime series Bleach. A lieutenant from the 10th division of the Gotei 13. Is recognized by her large breasts, something she normally brings up in conversations and excuses.
wiki.sui-feng: Sui-Feng, also romanized as Soifon or Soi-Fon, is a character from Bleach. The leader of the Gotei 2nd Division of Soul Society and former subordinate of Shihouin Yoruichi.
wiki.tier harribel: Female character from Kubo Taito (Tite)'s Bleach. Arrancar (Current Espada #3).
wiki.unohana retsu: Bleach character. Captain of the Fourth Division of the Gotei 13. Formerly known as Unohana Yachiru, the first captain of the Eleventh Division of the Gotei 13.
wiki.ulquiorra cifer: A character from Bleach. An Arrancar and the Cuatro (4th) Espada in Aizen Sousuke's army.
wiki.grimmjow jaegerjaquez: A character from Bleach. An Arrancar and the Sexta (6th) Espada in Aizen Sousuke's army.

wiki.jeanne d'arc (fate): A Servant of the Ruler class, with the additional classification of the Saber class. Bears a notable resemblance to Artoria Pendragon (fate). As shown in Fate/Apocrypha and Fate/Zero, she is a blonde haired woman with blue/purple eyes and a long braid.

wiki.miyamoto musashi (fate): Saber-class servant in Fate/Grand Order. She's a genderswap of the famous samurai of the same name who killed his first man in a duel at age 13, founded the Niten Ichi-ryū (二天一流) style of swordsmanship and wrote The Book of Five Rings (五輪の書).
wiki.cu chulainn (lancer) (fate): The first Lancer-class servant of the Fate (series) series, first appeared in Fate/stay night. Also known simply as Lancer, he is the depiction of the famous Celtic folk hero of the same name.
wiki.florence nightingale (fate): Berserker-class Servant in Fate/Grand Order featured in the E Pluribus Unum (fate/grand order) singularity. The eponymous "Angel of Crimea", a British nurse from the Victorian era best known for her contribution to the modern medical study and effort to improve the conditions in hospitals.
wiki.kotomine kirei: A character from Fate/stay night. He is a priest that oversees the 5th Holy Grail War.
wiki.iskandar (fate): Fate/Zero character. The Rider-class servant of Waver Velvet. He also appears in Fate/Grand Order. His true name is Iskandar, aka Alexander the Great.
wiki.waver velvet: A character from Fate/Zero. College student, apprentice mage, ended up in way over his head after absconding with Kayneth El-Melloi Archibald's summoning catalyst, and then summoning Rider for the Fourth Holy Grail War in Fuyuki. wiki.clorinde (genshin impact): A playable Electro character in Genshin Impact. Strongest Champion Duelist of Fontaine and Furina_(genshin_impact)'s bodyguard.
wiki.navia (genshin impact): Genshin Impact character from Fontaine. The current president of the company Spina di Rosula, a position she inherited from her father, Callas (Genshin Impact), after his death. Despite losing many of her loved ones along the way, Navia continues pushing on, with the story serving as a coming-of-age story for her.
wiki.kafka (honkai: star rail): A playable character in Honkai: Star Rail. A member of the Stellaron Hunters (honkai: star rail), voiced by Itou Shizuka in Japanese and Cheryl Texiera in English.
wiki.acheron (honkai: star rail): Playable character in Honkai: Star Rail. Real name Raiden Bosenmori Mei, voiced by Sawashiro Miyuki (JP) and Allegra Clark (EN).

wiki.robin (honkai: star rail): A playable character in Honkai: Star Rail. She is a famous singer from Penacony and the younger sister of Sunday (Honkai: Star Rail). Voiced by Nazuka Kaori (JP) and Alice Himora (EN).

wiki.black swan (honkai: star rail): Playable character from Honkai: Star Rail. A Memokeeper and Pathstrider of Remembrance, voiced by Nabatame Hitomi in Japanese and Arryn Zech in English.

wiki.himeko (honkai: star rail): A playable character in Honkai: Star Rail. The Navigator of the Astral Express (honkai: star rail), voiced by Tanaka Rie in Japanese and Cia Court in English.
wiki.ruan mei (honkai: star rail): A playable character in Honkai: Star Rail. Member #81 of the Genius Society, she is an expert of biological sciences. Voiced by Oonishi Saori (JP) and Emi Lo (EN).
wiki.sunday (honkai: star rail): A playable Honkai: Star Rail character, and brother to Robin (Honkai: Star Rail). Voiced by Ootsuka Takeo in Japanese.
wiki.jing yuan: A playable Honkai: Star Rail character. One of the seven Arbiter-Generals of the Xianzhou Alliance, voiced by Ono Daisuke (JP) and Alejandro Saab (EN).
wiki.acheron (slashed dream) (honkai: star ra: An appearance used by Acheron (Honkai: Star Rail) in Honkai: Star Rail while using her full power in combat.
wiki.tingyun (honkai: star rail): A playable character in Honkai: Star Rail. Amicassador of the Sky-Faring Commission of the Xianzhou Luofu. Voiced by Takada Yuuki in Japanese and Anya Floris (replacing Laci Morgan from Version 2.7 onward) in English.
wiki.sunday (sacerdos' relived ordeal) (honka: An outfit worn by Sunday (Honkai: Star Rail) as an NPC, prior to becoming playable in version 2.8; he also wears this outfit in the Light Cone, After the Charmony Fall.

wiki.tingyun (harmony) (honkai: star rail): The default outfit and playable version of Honkai: Star Rail's Tingyun (honkai: star rail) when you first encounter her in-game.
wiki.luocha (honkai: star rail): A playable character in Honkai: Star Rail. He is a traveling merchant with surprising skill in medicine. Voiced by Ishida Akira (voice actor) in Japanese and Craig Lee Thomas in English.
wiki.sampo koski: A playable character in Honkai: Star Rail. A silver-tongued salesman and Masked Fool, he travels between Belobog's Overworld and Underworld to do dubious business. Voiced by Hirakawa Daisuke in Japanese and Roger Rose in English.

A member of the noble Landau family and captain of the Silvermane Gaurds in Belobog, he is responsible for the city's defense and peacekeeping. The younger brother of Serval and older brother of Lynx. Voiced by Furukawa Makoto in Japanese and Bryson Baugus in English.
wiki.sensei (blue archive): The player character of Blue Archive, a teacher in Kivotos, the Academy City, leading their students to solve various incidents happening throughout the streets. They are of unspecified gender, though for the game's anime adaptation, the player character is a male.
wiki.izayoi sakuya: The "Perfect and Elegant Maid". Stage 5 boss of Touhou's Embodiment of Scarlet Devil and later the third most recurring playable character (being playable in six official games) after protagonists Hakurei Reimu and Kirisame Marisa.
wiki.yakumo yukari: The "Youkai of Boundaries". Phantasm Stage boss of Touhou's Perfect Cherry Blossom and later a recurring playable character.

wiki.yakumo ran: The "Nine-Tailed Strategist". Extra Stage boss and Phantasm stage midboss of Touhou's Perfect Cherry Blossom.

wiki.hijiri byakuren: "The Sealed Great Magician", introduced as the final boss of Touhou Undefined Fantastic Object.
wiki.yagokoro eirin: The "Brain of the Moon". Secondary final boss of Touhou's Imperishable Night.
wiki.morichika rinnosuke: A half-human, half-youkai merchant, and one of the only few named male characters in Touhou.
wiki.hoshiguma yuugi: The "Rumored Unnatural Phenomenon". Stage 3 mid-boss and boss of Touhou's Subterranean Animism. Has the ability to control supernatural phenomena, but is usually just depicted as physically strong.
wiki.megurine luka: A Vocaloid originally released for the VOCALOID2 engine on January 30, 2009. She was the third of the Character Vocal Series and is an official PIAPRO character.
wiki.kaito (vocaloid): KAITO is a Japanese VOCALOID developed by the YAMAHA Corporation and distributed by Crypton Future Media, Inc., and was originally released for the first VOCALOID engine on February 14, 2006. wiki.kamui gakupo: Camui Gackpo (or Kamui Gakupo) is a Japanese VOCALOID developed and distributed by Internet Co., Ltd., and was released for the VOCALOID2 engine.
wiki.cynthia (pokemon): Cynthia, known as Shirona (シロナ) in Japan, is a character introduced in Pokémon Diamond and Pearl.
wiki.leon (pokemon): Leon, known as Dande in Japan, is a character introduced in Pokémon Sword and Shield.

wiki.n (pokemon): Lead antagonist of Pokémon Black and White , and supporting character in Pokémon Black 2 and White 2.

wiki.skyla (pokemon): Skyla, known as Fuuro (フウロ) in Japan, is a character introduced in Pokémon Black and White.
wiki.joseph joestar: A catch-all tag for all versions of Joseph Joestar from the JoJo no Kimyou na Bouken series.
wiki.joseph joestar (young): Joseph Joestar as he appears in Battle Tendency. As a young teenager, Joseph uses the power of the Hamon (jojo) (Ripple) to defeat the Pillar Men.

wiki.jean pierre polnareff: One of the central protagonists in JoJo no Kimyou na Bouken Part 3: Stardust Crusaders. Also appears in Part 5:: Vento Aureo as a supporting character. His stand is the Silver chariot.
wiki.bruno bucciarati: A central protagonist in JoJo no Kimyou na Bouken Part 5: Vento Aureo. His Stand is Sticky Fingers. Wears his hair in a bob cut with two hairclips. Reflecting his Stand's power, Buccellati wears a suit with a zipper motif.
wiki.joseph joestar (old): Joseph Joestar as he appears in Stardust Crusaders and Diamond wa Kudakenai.
wiki.gyro zeppeli: One of the main protagonists of Steel Ball Run, alongside Johnny Joestar. A competitor in the Steel Ball Run race, he possesses control over a mysterious ability known as the Spin.
wiki.guido mista: A supporting character from JoJo no Kimyou na Bouken Part 5: Vento Aureo. His Stand (jojo) is Sex Pistols (stand). He has short black hair, often concealed by his distinctive hat with a downward-facing arrow design in the front, an argyle sweater that exposes his midriff as well as tiger print pants.
wiki.kars (jojo): Main antagonist of JoJo no Kimyou na Bouken Part 2. Leader of the Pillar Men, ancient vampires vastly superior to those created by the Stone Mask, which he invented. He has three horns and long, wavy hair and his default attire has him topless male, showing off his muscles and abs.
wiki.kira yoshikage: The main antagonist of JOJO no Kimyou na Bouken 4: Diamond wa Kudakenai. Son of Kira Yoshihiro.
wiki.diego brando: Diego Brando commonly referred to as Dio, is a primary antagonist featured in the seventh part of the JoJo No Kimyou Na Bouken 's series, Steel Ball Run.
wiki.mohammed avdol: A protagonist in Stardust Crusaders. His stand (JOJO) is Magician's Red.

wiki.leone abbacchio: A supporting character from JoJo no Kimyou na Bouken Part 5: Vento Aureo. His Stand is Moody Blues.

wiki.prosciutto (jojo): Prosciutto is a secondary antagonist featured in the fifth part of the JoJo No Kimyou Na Bouken's series, Vento Aureo. His Stand (jojo) is The Grateful Dead (Stand).

wiki.wamuu: A central antagonist of JoJo no Kimyou na Bouken Part 2. One of the Pillar Men, ancient vampires vastly superior to those created by the Stone Mask. Subordinate of Kars and Esidisi.

Drawstrings are commonly used to secure hoods on hoodies and hooded jackets and tighten waistbands on garments such as sweatpants and bloomers. They may also be used to to keep bags closed.
wiki.center frills: Frills that are in the midcenter of a dress or shirt. Most of the time it runs between the collarbone and navel or lower chest.
wiki.center opening: A large opening in a shirt, dress, leotard, bodysuit, or other top that exposes a lot of skin in the center of the body, including most or all of the cleavage, without fully exposing the breasts. This can be because it is the garment's intended appearance, or because the garment has been unzipped or unbuttoned.
wiki.bikini under clothes: A bikini being worn underneath clothes.
wiki.lowleg: Low-cut attire (such as underwear or bikinis), typically featuring a thin waistband: • lowleg bikini: low-cut bikini bottoms • lowleg panties: low-cut panties • lowleg pants: low-cut pants • lowleg pantyhose: low-set pantyhose • lowleg shorts: low-cut shorts • lowleg skirt: low-set skirts
wiki.star print: Clothing or a fabric item that has the printed motif of star (symbol)s (☆).
wiki.paw print: A marking or design that looks like the impression of an animal's paw.
wiki.hip vent: A clothing cutout in the hip area of a garment, like those found at the sides of the waistband of a hakama.

wiki.v-neck: Topwear with a V-shaped neckline, most commonly found in shirts and sweaters.
wiki.see-through sleeves: A pair of sleeves that are made of see-through or sheer fabric material. The sleeves have to either be detached, or different from the rest of the garment the character is wearing (such as raglan sleeves).
wiki.coat on shoulders: A coat draped over the shoulders, rather than worn with the arms in the sleeves.
wiki.heart cutout: A clothing cutout in the shape of a heart. Typically a cleavage cutout, but it may also be an ass cutout, crotch cutout, or navel cutout.
wiki.unworn skirt: A skirt that is present but not being worn.
wiki.low neckline: A neckline that is extremely low, seemingly supported only by the curve of the breasts or the nipples themselves. Because the clothing appears millimeters away from a nipple or areola slip, this often means there's ample cleavage.
wiki.heart print: Clothing or an object that has at least one heart printed on it.
wiki.leotard under clothes: Wearing a leotard underneath a set of other clothing, such as a shirt, pants, skirt, etc.
wiki.jacket partially removed: When a jacket is pulled down and worn off shoulder (hanging low around the arms or elbows), rather than on top of the shoulders.
wiki.asymmetrical sleeves: Sleeves that, by design, lack symmetry. • For differences in length, use uneven sleeves. • For differences in color or pattern, use mismatched sleeves.
wiki.unworn clothes: When an article of clothing is present in the image but it is not being worn by any character.
wiki.unworn jacket: A jacket that is completely or partially removed from the body. The arms shouldn't be in the sleeves and the jacket shouldn't be on the body.
wiki.see-through cleavage: When a piece of clothing that otherwise would cover the character's cleavage has a portion of see-through material that allows to see it.
wiki.covered collarbone: When the outline of a person's collarbone is visible beneath their clothing.
wiki.coattails: Flaps at the back of a coat or jacket that are not joined together but continue to extend past the waist area. A variation of a tailcoat.
wiki.notched lapels: The "standard" and most common style of lapels. They are sewn to the collar at an angle creating a "step" or a "notch".
wiki.rose print: Clothing or an object that has roses printed on it.
wiki.cat cutout: A clothing cutout in the shape of a cat. Normally this is a cleavage cutout, but more rarely it may be an ass cutout or some other type of cutout. The cutout may be shaped like a cat's face or like a whole cat.
wiki.underboob cutout: A clothing cutout that exposes underboob.
wiki.see-through silhouette: When the silhouette of a person's body is visible through a translucent object, usually clothing or curtains. Not necessarily see-through clothes, since there can be just enough light to pierce the fabric.
wiki.american flag print: Clothing or an object that has printings resembling the American flag.
wiki.sideless outfit: An outfit that exposes a large area of a character's side skin.
wiki.jacket around waist: When a jacket is tied around a character's waist.
wiki.fruit print: Clothing or another object with a fruit design printed on it. A type of food print.
wiki.unworn shirt: A shirt that is not being worn.
wiki.dragon print: Clothing or an object that has a dragon printed on it.
wiki.wet swimsuit: When a swimsuit is wet with water. Visible clues that this tag can be used include the character being wet, droplets of water on the swimsuit itself, and/or a white one-piece swimsuit suddenly being see-through.
wiki.spider web print: Clothing or an object that has a spider web printed on it.
wiki.borrowed clothes: When a character wears an outfit or accessories belonging to another character for some reason other than cosplay (trying to dress as the other character).
wiki.undersized clothes: The opposite of oversized clothes, this is for posts showing a situation wherein the clothes are obviously too small for the wearer.
wiki.rabbit print: Clothing or an object that has either a rabbit's body or just its face printed on it.
wiki.bodysuit under clothes: A bodysuit being worn under some other form of clothing.
wiki.character print: Clothing or an item that has a specific character printed on it.
wiki.snowflake print: Clothing or an item that has at least one snowflake printed on it.
wiki.enpera: When hair poofs out above a scarf (or similar apparel, like headphones around neck).
wiki.shared clothes: Two or more persons are wearing/using any type of clothes together.
wiki.stomach cutout: A clothing cutout that exposes the stomach.
wiki.skull print: Clothing or an object that has a skull printed on it.
wiki.cat print: Clothing or an object that has either a cat's body or just its face printed on it.
wiki.uneven sleeves: Sleeves of different lengths. For example, one short sleeve and one long sleeve.
wiki.butterfly print: Any article of clothing or object made out of fabric that has a butterfly printed motif.
wiki.dirty clothes: Clothes that have been stained with dirt, mud, or filth.
wiki.spandex: A synthetic fiber known for its exceptional elasticity. Frequently used to make sportswear and other skin tight clothing.
wiki.diamond cutout: A cutout on any article of clothing that has a diamond shape.
wiki.argyle cutout: A cutout on any article of clothing that has a diamond shape.
wiki.feather-trimmed sleeves: Sleeves that have a feather trim at the base.
wiki.constellation print: The printed motif of constellations. As long as there's stars connected by lines, it matters not whether the constellation actually exists.
wiki.single vertical stripe: A (narrow) vertical stripe in skin tight clothing with usually tags like bodysuit, gym uniform, spandex, swimsuit, wetsuit. To be used only when the stripe is significantly visible and emphasizes body proportions. Seams and shining do not count as stripes. A good example: post #158338
wiki.sweater around waist: A sweater worn around the waist.
wiki.loose clothes: Clothes that are loosely draped over the body.
wiki.fine fabric emphasis: Sheer fabric (typically pantyhose or thighhighs) whose fine weave is visible.
wiki.front slit: When an outfit like a dress or skirt has a front cutout slit. The slit usually begins just below the chest or stomach, but there are also cases where the slit begins just below the neck or groin. Also found on camisole, babydoll, chemise, nightgown and shirts.
wiki.strawberry print: An article of clothing or item that has a strawberry pattern printed on it.
wiki.thigh cutout: A clothing cutout in the thighs of a character's pants or legwear, exposing bare skin underneath.
wiki.flame print: Clothing or an object with the printed motif of flames from a fire.
wiki.yellow trim: An article of clothing that has a yellow trim around at least one of its edges.
wiki.lace-trimmed sleeves: Sleeves with lace trim, not to be confused with lace sleeves
wiki.unworn bikini top: A bikini top that is present, but not being worn.
wiki.cutout above navel: A clothing cutout in the front of a garment somewhere above the navel but below the breasts.
wiki.snap-fit buckle: A plastic buckle where one half is made up of three prongs that are inserted into the other half that acts as a shell. The buckle is released by pressing on the sides to push the prongs inward. A "snap" noise is created when you connect the buckle together and when you pull it apart.
wiki.single off shoulder: An outfit that hangs off of one arm, exposing a single bare shoulder. If the sleeve is completely off the arm, it's arm out of sleeve.
wiki.ribbed sleeves: A pair of sleeves that have a ribbed pattern. The sleeves have to either be detached, or differently patterned from the rest of the garment the character is wearing (such as raglan sleeves).
wiki.yellow sleeves: A pair of sleeves that are colored yellow. The sleeves have to either be detached, or differently colored from the rest of the garment the character is wearing (such as raglan sleeves).
wiki.shorts under dress: Shorts worn along with a dress.
wiki.ass cutout: A clothing cutout that exposes the ass or butt crack.
wiki.full-length zipper: A one-piece garment with a full-length zipper from the neck past the navel.

wiki.mismatched sleeves: Sleeves of two different colors or patterns. For differences in length, see uneven sleeves.
wiki.sweaty clothes: Clothing dampened, darkened, or made see-through due to sweat soaking through the fabric.
wiki.single horizontal stripe: A lone horizontal stripe running along an article of clothing.
wiki.food-themed clothes: Clothing with a distinctive food-related theme.
wiki.pinching sleeves: Pinching or holding one's own sleeve cuffs, usually to hold up sleeves that have fallen past the wrists.
wiki.triangle print: Clothing or a fabric object that has the printed design of triangles.
wiki.single stripe: Clothing article of object that has only one stripe.
wiki.fish print: Any type of clothing that has printed patterns resembling fish.
wiki.pants tucked in: When the legs of pants are tucked into the wearer's footwear (e.g. boots). Commonly used by samurai, their baggy pants under the armor are actually tucked in hakama.
wiki.red trim: An article of clothing that has a red trim around at least one of its edges.
wiki.brown sleeves: A pair of sleeves that are colored brown. The sleeves have to either be detached, or differently colored from the rest of the garment the character is wearing (such as raglan sleeves).

wiki.unworn coat: When an unworn coat is present in the image, along with someone who could be wearing it.
wiki.clothes between thighs: Clothing that is distinctly caught between the legs around the crotch area. Naturally a result of loose clothing like a skirt/dress or a pelvic curtain, but can also be utilized as a form of convenient censoring.
wiki.armpit cutout: A clothing cutout on the underside of outfit sleeves that exposes the armpits in otherwise sleeved outfits.
wiki.expressive clothes: Clothes or an object worn by a character that changes to match the character's mood or to show their thoughts.
wiki.anchor print: Clothing or an object with an anchor printed on it.
wiki.frog print: Clothing or an object that has either a frog's body or just its face printed on it.
wiki.cross-laced sleeves: Sleeves with criss-crossing laces, strings, or ribbons, sometimes paired with cross-laced cutouts.
wiki.unworn dress: A dress is present but not being worn.
wiki.sparkle print: Clothing or a fabric item that has the printed motif of sparkles.
wiki.silver trim: An article of clothing that has a silver trim around at least one of its edges.
wiki.baggy clothes: Clothes that are loose-fitting, roomy, or oversized, favored for their comfortable, relaxed fit and ease of movement. Baggy clothes tend to be wide.
wiki.white trim: An article of clothing with a white-colored trim around at least one of its edges.
wiki.cardigan around waist: A cardigan worn around the waist.
wiki.orange sleeves: A pair of sleeves that are colored orange. The sleeves have to either be detached, or differently colored from the rest of the garment the character is wearing (such as raglan sleeves).
wiki.unworn swimsuit: A swimsuit that isn't being worn.
wiki.unzipping: Opening a zipper, so that it becomes unzipped. If the zipper is already open, use unzipped instead.
wiki.crotch cutout: An intentional clothing cutout that exposes a character's crotch.
wiki.skirt cutout: One or more clothing cutouts on the skirt or dress, especially near the hem of bottom. Do not confuse with slit (side slit, front slit, back slit).
wiki.cross-laced slit: A slit in an article of clothing with criss-crossing laces, strings or ribbons.
wiki.wet dress: A dress that is visibly wet, sometimes causing it to become see-through.
wiki.jacket over swimsuit: Typically describes an open light jacket being worn with a swimsuit, but can also be applied to open shirts with swimsuits as well. If the character is wearing more clothing or the garment is zipped/buttoned up completely, consider using swimsuit under clothes.
wiki.print sleeves: Any detached sleeves or arm warmers that have a printed pattern on them. The sleeves have to either be detached, or differently patterned from the rest of the garment the character is wearing (such as raglan sleeves).
wiki.puff and slash sleeves: A style of puffy sleeves; thin slits are slashed into the sleeves, revealing another layer of clothing below, typically to showcase another color.
wiki.skirt under dress: A character wearing a skirt under a dress, sometimes as part of a layered dress.
wiki.see-through body: When objects behind (and sometimes simultaneously inside) a character can be seen through a character's skin and/or clothes, either partially or wholly. This might include a visible skeleton and/or organs.
wiki.patchwork clothes: Clothes created from various pieces or scraps of fabric being sewn together. Could be intended design choice or the result of the person not having sufficient fabric to make their clothes from one cloth, often an indicator in art of poverty.
wiki.embroidery: The art of decorating clothes or other fabric with intricate stitched designs using a sewing needle and thread.
wiki.object in pocket: A pocket with an item in it.
wiki.wringing clothes: Squeezing wet clothes with the hands, to force water out to dry the clothes.
wiki.double horizontal stripe: Two lines running parallel to each other, forming an = shape on an article of clothing.
wiki.shorts around one leg: Used when a character has a pair of shorts partially removed and wrapped around only one leg.
wiki.sayagata: An intricate traditional Japanese pattern of joined manji (Buddhist crosses).
wiki.square neckline: A top having a square-shaped neckline.
wiki.exposed pocket: When a pair of cutoffs or denim shorts are so short that the pockets are visible beneath the hemline of the shorts.
wiki.unworn shoes: Shoes that currently aren't being worn.

wiki.tengu-geta: Geta sandals that have a single elongated peg or tooth rather than the traditional two tooth design.

wiki.two-tone boots: Multicolored boots that have exactly two colors.

wiki.rabbit: A small animal with long ears, long hind legs, and a short tail.
wiki.snake: An elongate legless carnivorous reptile of the suborder Serpentes.
wiki.stuffed rabbit: A stuffed animal resembling a rabbit, akin to a teddy bear.
wiki.frog: A tailless amphibian with a short squat body, moist smooth skin, and very long hind legs for leaping.
wiki.bat (animal): A flying nocturnal mammal with two wings of the order Chiroptera. With their forelimbs adapted as wings, they are the only mammals capable of true and sustained flight.
wiki.blue butterfly: A butterfly that is coloured blue.
wiki.mouse (animal): A small rodent that typically has a pointed snout, rounded ears, and a long scaly tail. This tag includes both smaller mice and larger rats.
wiki.penguin: A type of flightless aquatic bird with upright posture and black-and-white plumage.
wiki.digimon (creature): A creature from the Digimon series.
wiki.fox: Foxes are small-to-medium-sized omnivorous mammals belonging to various genera within the Canidae family, but, strictly speaking, the term refers to the species classified as “true” foxes (genus Vulpes), especially the "red fox" species (Vulpes vulpes).
wiki.wolf: Commonly known as a gray wolf, a species of canid native to the wilderness and remote areas of North America, Eurasia, and North Africa. It is the largest member of its family, with males averaging 43–45 kg (95–99 lb), and females 36–38.5 kg (79–85 lb) It is similar in general appearance and proportions to a german she…
wiki.chick: A young bird, especially of a terrestrial domestic fowl.
wiki.shiny pokemon: A Pokémon with a coloration that is different than usual for its species. For example, Gyarados are blue, but Shiny Gyarados are red. Known for being incredibly rare.
wiki.crab: Crustaceans with eyes on short stalks, a broad flattened carapace with a small abdomen folded under the thorax, and pincers.
wiki.bear: Big furry mammals with claws, teeth, and a large appetite. They eat a lot in the fall to hibernate through the winter.
wiki.squeans: A symbol next to a character's head to indicate a state of sleepiness, drunkenness or intoxication. Often has dashes arranged in a circle, or can just be multiple circles. Often includes a curved line.
wiki.sleep bubble: A symbol next to a character's head to indicate a state of sleepiness, drunkenness or intoxication. Often has dashes arranged in a circle, or can just be multiple circles. Often includes a curved line.
wiki.tiger: The tiger (Panthera tigris) is a member of the Felidae family and the largest and possibly most dangerous of the five "big cats". Native to much of eastern and southern Asia, the Tiger is an apex predator and an obligate carnivore.
wiki.octopus: An eight-limbed marine animal from the order Octopoda. They have two eyes with horizontal pupils and a beaked mouth at the center of their eight suction-cupped tentacles.
wiki.duck: A general term for wading waterfowls.
wiki.chicken: A domestic fowl bred for flesh or eggs.
wiki.sheep: An animal with a thick woolly coat and, in males, curving horns. It is kept in flocks for its wool or meat.
wiki.seagull: Sea birds in the family Laridae other than terns, noddies and skimmers.
wiki.clothed pokemon: A Pokémon wearing clothes, including hats. This includes naturally humanoid and anthropomorphic Pokémon like Gardevoir and Lopunny, but generally does not extend to personified Pokémon.
wiki.white cat: A cat whose fur is entirely white. Often associated with maneki-neko, the Japanese lucky cat. White cats are associated with purity and are said to bring about positive changes.
wiki.owl: A nocturnal bird of prey from the order Strigiformes. About a third of all species have tufts of feathers on their heads colloquially known as "ears," which play no role in hearing but instead are used for display and communication.
wiki.stuffed cat: A stuffed animal that is a cat.
wiki.goldfish: A type of domesticated freshwater fish that are commonly kept as pets in aquariums, ponds or goldfish bowls.
wiki.jellyfish: A type of aquatic creature with a gelatinous umbrella-like bell and long tentacles. The bell helps with movement in the water while the tentacles capture prey.
wiki.shark: A large species of predominately carnivorous ocean-dwelling cartilaginous fish belonging to the clade Selachii. Most have sharp teeth, are able to smell blood in the water from a far distance, and detect electrical currents.
wiki.panda: A black-and-white bear species native to China. Easily recognizable by the patches of black around the eyes, over the ears, and across the body. Not to be confused with red panda which is not a bear.
wiki.mega pokemon: A temporary transformation form of some Pokémon. This can be achieved if the Trainer has a Key Stone while the Pokémon holds a Mega Stone.
wiki.pig: Used for the animal and for dolls and other objects depicting one.
wiki.shrimp: Shrimp are crustaceans that have beady eyes, long antennae, and segmented parts. They swim forwards by paddling with swimmerets on the underside of their abdomens.
wiki.oversized animal: An animal or creature that's much larger than it would be in real life: for example, a housecat the size of a horse or even a house.
wiki.dove: For tagging purposes, this tag refers to the white or mostly white birds, such as the "dove of peace" that is commonly associated with the term "dove."
wiki.hamster: A small Eurasian rodent of the subfamily Cricetinae, especially Mesocricetus auratus, having large cheek pouches and a short tail. They are often kept as a pet or used in laboratory research.
wiki.whale: A very large marine mammal with a streamlined hairless body, a horizontal tail fin, and a blowhole on top of the head for breathing.
wiki.starter pokemon trio: A full trio of starter Pokémon.
wiki.turtle: Shelled reptiles famed for their slow pace and longevity. Most are able to fully retract into their shells for protection.
wiki.squirrel: A type of rodent with a large bushy tail that eats nut (food)s and berries.
wiki.spider: An eight-legged predatory arachnid with an unsegmented body consisting of a fused head and thorax and a rounded abdomen. Spiders have fangs that inject poison into their prey, and most kinds spin webs in which to capture insects.
wiki.lion: The Lion (Panthera leo) is one of the five big cats species. Also known as "The King of the Beasts". It is a large gregarious predatory feline of Sub-Saharan Africa and India having a tawny coat with a shaggy mane in the male.
wiki.pokemon on head: A Pokémon (creature) located on someone's head.
wiki.monkey: A primate of the Haplorrhini suborder and simian infraorder, either an Old World monkey or a New World monkey, but excluding apes and humans. Traditionally identifiable from apes by having a tail.
wiki.dolphin: A sea mammal that is large, smooth, and grey, with a long, pointed snout.
wiki.stuffed shark: A stuffed animal resembling a shark.
wiki.youkai (youkai watch): The namesake creatures from the Youkai Watch series.
wiki.dinosaur: General term given to many diverse species of reptiles of the clade Dinosauria that lived between 230 and 65 million years ago.
wiki.squid: Squid are marine cephalopods of the order Teuthida, which comprises around 300 species. Like all other cephalopods, squid have a distinct head, bilateral symmetry, a mantle, and arms. Squid, like cuttlefish, have eight arms arranged in pairs and two, usually longer, tentacles.
wiki.shiba inu: The Shiba Inu is a distinct purebred dog from Japan. It looks very similar to the Akita Inu but is smaller, has a curled fluffy tail, and tends to have tan-colored fur.
wiki.eagle: A bird of prey with keen vision and broad wings in the family Accipitridae. Eagles are the apex predators of the avian world; only condors and some vultures are larger.
wiki.deer: A type of medium to large size ruminant mammal with antlers. It usually lives in forested areas. Male deer are known as "buck", and female deer are referred to as "doe".
wiki.tropical fish: Fish found in warm, tropical environments. They are often vibrantly colored and considered exotic. "Tropical fish" is not a taxonomical term but an informal one that can refer to fish from many different lineages.
wiki.pokemon on shoulder: A Pokémon (creature) located on someone's shoulder.
wiki.witch (madoka magica): The primary antagonistic entities from the series Mahou Shoujo Madoka Magica, said to manifest due to negative emotions and actions in the world ( ). Upon targeting their victims they leave a mark called a Witch's Kiss. To conceal themselves the witches create barriers called Witch's Labyrinths.
wiki.flock: Multiple birds, usually of the same species, flying together or behaving as a group.
wiki.white butterfly: A butterfly that is colored white.
wiki.snail: A mollusk with a spiral snail shell into which the whole body can be withdrawn. If the snail is seen without its shell, it's called a slug. When made into food, they’re called escargot.
wiki.white snake: A snake that is white in coloration. Often considered a sacred animal.
wiki.yellow butterfly: A butterfly that is colored yellow.
wiki.cow: A bovine, four-legged animal commonly used in agriculture and livestock.
wiki.pikmin (creature): The titular plant-like organisms from the Pikmin (Series) series. They come in multiple varieties and have three distinct developmental stages (leaf, bud and flower).
wiki.reindeer: A species of deer native to arctic, tundra, and mountainous regions. Popularly associated with Christmas as Santa Claus' mode of transportation along with his sleigh. They're also the only species of deer where females normally have antlers.
wiki.boar: The wild boar, a relative of the common domesticated pig that usually has brown fur and small tusks. 2007 and 2019 are notable for being the year of the pig according to the Chinese zodiac.
wiki.calico cat: A cat with patches of white, orange and black fur. For the pattern itself, which can be applied to anything else with this coloration, see calico (pattern).
wiki.pigeon: For tagging purposes, pigeons are the mostly-gray birds commonly found in cities.
wiki.sparrow: A general term for birds in the Passeridae family, as well as similar but unrelated birds in other families.
wiki.bagged fish: A fish in a water-filled plastic bag.
wiki.angora rabbit: A variety of domestic rabbit bred for its long fur.
wiki.white tiger: White tigers are a kind of tiger whose fur is white or almost white. White tigers tend to be larger both at birth and at full adult size than normal tigers.
wiki.ladybug: A small beetle, 1 to 10 millimeters in length, with elytra (wing cases) of a bright red, orange, or yellow color, overlaid with black spots. Generally considered to be useful because it helps control bug pest populations.
wiki.stuffed winged unicorn: A stuffed toy version of a winged unicorn (a mythological creature resembling a pegasus and a unicorn).
wiki.shiny and normal: A Shiny Pokémon and its normal form depicted together.
wiki.moth: An insect related to the butterfly, but are generally agricultural pests. The domesticated moth Bombyx mori, or silkworm larvae, is bred for silk production. Moths are known for being especially attracted to light and can often be found swarming lanterns.
wiki.squidbeak splatoon: The Squidbeak Splatoon was formed by Cap'n Cuttlefish after the Great Zapfish was stolen by the Octarians. He recruited into the platoon to search for the missing Zapfish, and later persuaded Agent 3 to join the platoon as well.
wiki.chocobo: Trademark steed of the Final Fantasy JRPG series by Square Enix (formerly Squaresoft).
wiki.polar bear: Large carnivorous bears that live in arctic areas of the northern hemisphere. They have thick white fur that blends in with the snow and are extremely ferocious and aggressive, even to humans.
wiki.parrot: A bird in the Psittaciformes order characterized by a short, powerful hooked beak, high intelligence, social nature and talent for mimicry. Most are brightly-colored, but some, like the alpine kea, have quite dull plumage.
wiki.hedgehog: A small animal with spines across their back - when threatened, it will bristle these spines. They are often brown and/or white in color.
wiki.snow rabbit: A rabbit made from snow, with leaves for ears and red berries for eyes.
wiki.chimera: A fire-breathing monster from Greek mythology with a lion's head, goat's body, and a serpent's tail.
wiki.crocodilian: An order of reptiles including both crocodiles and alligators, as well as caiman (animal)s and gharials, all of which belong to the order Crocodilia.
wiki.puppy: A newborn and/or juvenile dog. Smaller breeds are considered puppies until around 1 year, while larger breeds are the same for up to 2 years.
wiki.goat: A hardy domesticated ruminant animal that has backward curving horns and (in the male) a beard. It is kept for its milk and meat and is noted for its lively and frisky behavior.
wiki.flying fish: Ambiguous tag, currently being used for: • Fish that appear to be in flight, i.e., the scene is not underwater but the fish are depicted as if swimming. • A family of fish with enlarged pectoral fins that enable them to glide for short distances above water. → Fish, underwater, water, skyfish (cryptid), flying whale, List of animals
wiki.anglerfish: A bony fish from the order Lophiiformes named for the fleshy growth on its head that it uses to lure in prey.
wiki.japari bun: A form of bread that is eaten by "Friends" in Kemono Friends as a nutritional substitute so they don't need to fight, kill and eat each other to survive.
wiki.lizard: A reptile that typically has a long body and tail, four legs, movable eyelids, and rough, scaly, or spiny skin.
wiki.crane (animal): A long-legged, long-necked bird. The most frequently depicted crane in Japanese art, recognizable by its red forehead and black markings, is the red-crowned crane.
wiki.beetle: A type of bug (scientifically, an insect of the order Coeloptera) with two pairs of wings, the outer of which is adapted into a hardened protective shell (elytra). Not to be confused with any of several models of automobile manufactured by Volkswagen.
wiki.simple bird: A simplified depiction of a distant bird, typically drawn as a simple curved v-shape, but can also be of a slightly more complex shape.
wiki.elephant: A five-toed herbivore with large ears, tusks, and trunk. The largest land animal alive today, it is a symbol of wisdom in Asian culture.
wiki.blood: A red bodily fluid that supplies cells with nutrients and oxygen and remove waste products. If it appears outside the body, then something is wrong.
wiki.?: A standalone question mark in the image, either inside or outside a speech bubble. Usually denotes wonder, confusion, or curiosity.
An expression of three (or more) dots, commonly called an ellipsis. It is used to show that a character is at a loss for words.
wiki.!: An exclamation mark, used to depict comical shock or surprise.
wiki.spoken ellipsis: An ellipsis (...) that is spoken aloud in a speech bubble or thought bubble. Meant to show that a character is at a loss for words.
wiki.!?: A combination of the exclamation and question marks, conveying both surprise and wonder/disbelief at the same time. The order of the marks depends on the context being shown by the "conveyer." This symbol is also called an interrobang, or ‽.
wiki.vision (genshin impact): A jeweled amulet worn by many characters in Genshin Impact, as proof that one has been granted the power of an element by the gods.
wiki.spoken question mark: A question mark symbol (? or ??) that is spoken aloud in a speech bubble or thought bubble. Often indicates confusion.
wiki.+++: A symbol drawn next to a character's head to represent laughter, mirth, happiness or chatting noise. Looks a bit like ╀─╀, but with a curved line. Commonly used for laughter or the noise of a crowd that happens in the background, or in a scene that is otherwise silent.
wiki.heart of string: A line that forms a heart-shaped loop. It doesn't have to be a literal string, it may be a ribbon, a typographical element or a background decoration, etc.
wiki.air bubble: A ball of air sorrounded by liquid or by a soft or frozen material. Usually goes along with underwater.
wiki.spoken exclamation mark: An exclamation mark symbol (! or !!) that is spoken aloud in a speech bubble or thought bubble. Often indicates surprise.
wiki.transparent: An object other than clothing that actually, physically allows some amount of light to pass through it. If a normally opaque object such as a wooden desk is rendered partly invisible by artistic fiat, that's x-ray.
wiki.!!: Double exclamation marks often express excitement, surprise or sudden pain.
wiki.gap (touhou): A portal_(object) created by the Touhou character Yakumo Yukari. Yukari's gaps look like black or purple ribbons with red bows at the ends, and are filled with demonic-looking red or purple disembodied eyes.
wiki.floating object: An object such as a book or weapon floating in air without visible, physical support.
wiki.blood on hand: Blood on a person's fingers or hands. It could be their own blood or someone else's.
wiki.blood on hands: Blood on a person's fingers or hands. It could be their own blood or someone else's.
wiki.infection monitor (arknights): A device in the setting of Arknights.
wiki.crack: A line on the surface of something along which it has split without it being completely broken into separate parts.
wiki.broken: An object that has ceased to fulfill its designed purpose or task.
wiki.blood splatter: Blood splattered freely in a mess on a surface, usually caused by a blood spray.
wiki.oripathy lesion (arknights): A character design element of Arknights, which manifests as chips of jagged, black, crystalline material growing out of the body.
wiki.damaged: When an object has been damaged in some way but still remains functional or the object can still fulfill its original purpose.
wiki.energy: Power derived from the utilization of physical, chemical, or magical resources, especially to provide light and heat or to work machines.
wiki.spoken blush: A blush sign in a speech bubble, with text or without. Often appears as several slashes: ///.
wiki.stand (jojo): A unique power possessed by characters in the JoJo no Kimyou na Bouken series, which are typically portrayed as ghost-like projections of a person's psyche or fighting spirit. The special powers vary widely, such as the ability to control sand or summon a sword-wielding warrior.
wiki.danmaku: Mode of attack used by enemies in bullet hell shooting games. Complex attack patterns, made of hundreds to thousands of projectiles fill the screen. The player must weave through tiny gaps in the barrage. End-stage boss attacks are especially spectacular, in an attempt to intimidate and dazzle the player.
wiki.command spell: A symbol from the Fate (series) series depicting a Master's control over a particular Servant, often seen as a red mark on the Master's hand of various shape. Jeanne d'Arc (Fate) bears a large one upon her back as a sign of her Ruler class privilege to command all servants in the Grail War.
wiki.spoken squiggle: A squiggle inside a speech bubble, often to depict annoyance, embarrassment, confusion, or exasperation.
wiki.spoken interrobang: An interrobang symbol (!?) that is spoken aloud in a speech bubble or thought bubble. Often indicates a combination of surprise and confusion.
