wiki.??: Used when two or more question marks exist in an image. They express a more intense wonder, curiosity, or confusion than a single question mark (?) does. Also used to express surprise, albeit at a considerably lower level than !?.
wiki.super saiyan: A form exclusive to the Saiyan race in Dragon Ball Z and onward. In order to go Super Saiyan for the first time, one must be either full-Saiyan or half-Saiyan. Early on, one must have gone through months or years of rigorous training, and have a pure heart or pure purpose.
wiki.spoken anger vein: An anger vein that is spoken. Sometimes, but not always, inside a speech bubble.
wiki.colored blood: Blood of a color other than the typical red.
wiki.paint: A mixture of a pigment and a suitable liquid to form a closely adherent coating when spread on a surface in a thin coat.
wiki.broken glass: Glass that has been shattered into many pieces. Usually refers to glass that is still in "one piece" but has cracks inside of it.
wiki.reflective liquid: A reflective surface of water or other liquid.
wiki.reflective water: A reflective surface of water or other liquid.
wiki.e.g.o (project moon): E.G.O equipment (Extermination of Geometrical Origin) is a recurring theme in Project Moon media. They can be used by characters in order to enhance their fighting prowess. They can take the form of weapons, clothing, items, and even pocket dimensions or locations.
wiki.liquid: A non-suggestive fluid that isn't clearly illustrated. Often used in cases were the liquid may be blood or paint. If someone is drinking or holding the substance from a drinking container, include the drink. For those submerged and/or wearing a swimsuit, they are likely in or near a body of water.
wiki.footprints: Imprints left by feet or shoes, usually on soft surface like sand or snow.
wiki.blood stain: When blood seeps into a material (such as fabric from clothing) and forms a visible mark (usually colored red, depending on color of blood).
wiki.spoken character: When a character's face or the entire inset of them appears in a speech bubble. Often used to show an off-screen character's reaction or when the spoken character is referring to that said person.
wiki.spoken sweatdrop: A large sweatdrop symbol inside a speech bubble. Often used to represent nervousness or embarrassment.
wiki.pink blood: Blood that is distinctly colored pink instead of red. Sometimes used to censor red blood to appear less gruesome. The Danganronpa (series) series is its most famous example which often gets parodied.
wiki.ink: A colored liquid, usually black, used for writing, drawing (action), and printing. This tag may also refer to inkblots and ink stains that stand out within a picture.
wiki.breath weapon: An ability used by dragons, kaiju, and other monsters to expel a harmful substance from their mouth. This may take the form of fire, ice, lightning, poison, acid, magic, energy, or any other substance.
wiki.spoken object: A speech bubble or thought bubble that contains an object instead of text. Used to indicate what a character is talking or thinking about in a simple, language-independent way.
wiki.blood in hair: When blood is present on someone's hair.
wiki.hydrokinesis: Water that appears to be mentally controlled by someone, whether by magic, element bending, or some other means.
wiki.blood on knife: A knife that is covered in blood.
wiki.heartbeat: This tag is for heartbeat sounds (typically ドキドキ, dokidoki).
wiki.dotted line: A continuous line that is broken up into smaller dots or dashes.
wiki.blood on arm: Blood that is on somebody's arm.
wiki.mochi trail: When mochi is pulled or stretched in some way, leaving a trail. Usually while eating.
wiki.floating weapon: A weapon floating on its own with no apparent propulsion system or force applied, usually next to a character.
wiki.snowball: A ball made of snow, that is, frozen water. Can be used for snowball fights or to make a snowman.
wiki.sand sculpture: A sculpture made out of sand. This includes both sand castles and other structures that don't resemble a castle.
wiki.cracked wall: A wall that is cracked, but not necessarily completely broken through.
wiki.smoke trail: A visible trail of smoke coming from a source, such as a cigarette or the barrel of a gun.
wiki.bullet hole: A hole left in an object by the impact of a bullet.
wiki.pool of blood: A puddle of blood on the ground or a flat surface, whether from a character or from something else.
wiki.warning sign: A traditionally triangular sign with an exclamation mark or diamond (shape) (⚠️) in the middle used to indicate dangerous areas/chemicals.
wiki.devil fruit power: A special power granted by a Devil Fruit in One Piece, a supernatural fruit that grants a unique power when eaten. An example is Monkey D. Luffy's power to stretch his body like rubber, granted by the Gomu Gomu no Mi devil fruit.
wiki.energy beam: A beam of energy, usually fired as a weapon or attack. It may start out as an energy ball that coalesces together before being launched as a beam, as in case of the most iconic example, Dragon Ball's Kamehameha (dragon ball).
wiki.super saiyan 1: The original Super Saiyan, the first to debut in the long lineage of transformations in the series of Dragon Ball.
wiki.paint splatter on face: Paint spattered or smeared on a person's face.
wiki.dissolving: When a character or object becomes incorporated into a liquid, or turns to smoke. • Use fading if the character is becoming transparent. • Use melting instead if a character or object is dripping. • Use disintegration instead if the character is breaking into shards.
wiki.splatter: A liquid or liquid-like substance splattered across a surface.
wiki.copy ability: Kirby's signature ability to acquire the special abilities of the enemies he swallows, usually accompanied by a change in costume or appearance.
wiki.kuji-in: Hand gestures and chanted mantras commonly depicted in popular culture being used by ninjas, monks and mikos to summon or use magic.
wiki.floating card: Any sort of card that appears to be falling, flying, or floating in midair, for any reason.
wiki.pokemon move: A special move used by Pokémon creatures in Pokémon media.
wiki.core crystal (xenoblade): Object in Xenoblade Chronicles 2. An blue colored gem that can resonate with a Driver to become a Blade. The crystal is then embedded in the chest or head of the Blade.
wiki.flower on liquid: When a flower is resting on the surface of a liquid, most often water.
wiki.breaking: Shattering an object by dropping it, using excess force, or otherwise causing it to become broken by any other means.
wiki.blood on leg: Blood that is on somebody's leg.
wiki.handprint: The typical shape left by a hand upon contact with a surface.
wiki.foam: A cluster of minute bubbles shown coming from someone's mouth, poured beverages with head such as beer or root beer, et cetera. For bubbles produced while using soap products during bathing, see soap bubbles.
wiki.sand castle: A handmade structure made out of sand made to specifically resemble a castle.
wiki.flying paper: When pieces of paper are visibly airborne in the image.
wiki.floating book: A book floating in midair, possibly by magic.
wiki.muzzle flash: The light that is visible at the muzzle of a gun when firing.
wiki....?: An expression that combines ... and ?. Generally used to describe a moment where a person has nothing to say but unlike ... there is confusion or curiosity.
wiki.broken window: A window that has been broken. Might include glass shards or shards, depending on the level of detail.
wiki.glass shards: Glass broken into small pieces. Use glass shard if there is only one piece or a piece is significantly larger than other shards.
wiki.speech bubble: A bubble that shows what a character is saying or thinking. A bubble can be white or colored, be spiky, notched or of other shapes. It can have text, a spoken object or symbol, or be blank.
wiki.glass: A type of material made by exposing a silica and sodium oxide mixture into a furnace to melt it into liquid glass, then shaping it into windows, usable kitchen tools, bottles and other drinking cups, and glass art.
wiki.disposable cup: A one-time use cup, usually made of paper or plastic.
wiki.drink can: A metal container designed to hold liquid drinks.
wiki.sakazuki: A flat, saucer-like cup used for drinking sake. Usually red in color, with a small base.
wiki.egg: A hard-shelled vessel containing an embryo. See egg (food) for eggs consumed as food.
wiki.meat: Generic, unidentifiable meat. If you can identify the type of meat or at least the method of cooking (e.g. yakitori, yakiniku), use those tags instead.
wiki.heart-shaped food: Any food item that is heart-shaped.
wiki.cake slice: A piece of cake cut off for service.
wiki.drink carton: A small, hand-sized cardboard container used to contain a drink, such as juice, milk, or even alcohol, which is often drunk directly from it with an included drinking straw.
wiki.spring onion: A Japanese long onion, a variety of Welsh onion, sometimes called a Japanese leek in English due to their similar appearance. It is a vegetable often depicted as being shaped like a Y; a white twig with two green branches.
wiki.jar: A widemouthed container commonly made of earthenware or glass.
wiki.mandarin orange: An orange-colored citrus fruit that is smaller than an orange (fruit).
wiki.chewing gum: Chewing gum made for the intent of blowing bubbles of all sizes.
wiki.milk: Milk produced by cows or other mammals. Often packed in cartons, bottles, jug (bottle)s, and bags, and usually consumed as a drink.
wiki.lemon: A yellow oval fruit with juicy acidic flesh.
wiki.tomato: Considered a vegetable, particularly for culinary purposes, the tomato is botanically a fruit produced by the plant Solanum lycopersicum of the nightshade family.
wiki.vegetable: Edible seeds or roots or stems or leaves or bulbs or tubers or nonsweet fruits of any of numerous herbaceous plant. A carrot for example.
wiki.banana: An elongated curved fruit. Known commonly for its yellow skin. It has a fleshy edible inner portion.
wiki.beer can: An aluminum drink can containing beer.
wiki.mochi: A type of wagashi - a Japanese rice cake made of glutinous rice pounded into paste and molded into shape. It is a traditional food for the Japanese New Year and is commonly sold and eaten during that time.
wiki.cream: A dairy product composed of the higher-butterfat layer skimmed from the top of milk before homogenization. Cream extracted from milk is sweeter compared to extracting it from whey. It is the principal ingredient in butter.
wiki.candy apple: Also known as Toffee apple, in Commonwealth English.
wiki.cheese: A type of typically solid dairy products; mostly made from cow's milk (types from other animals exist), beaten and stirred until it has reached the right texture and softness.
wiki.soda can: An aluminum or steel drink can containing soda, or in some cases, an energy drink.
wiki.sake bottle: A glass bottle containing sake. Similar to a wine bottle, but sake bottles often have a longer neck.
wiki.chips (food): A type of snack food also called crisps, made by slicing potatoes, corn tortillas, or other foods into very thin strips, deep frying them, then seasoning them with salt or other savory flavors.
wiki.pudding: In the United States, pudding characteristically denotes a sweet milk-based dessert similar in consistency to egg-based custards, though it may also refer to other types such as bread and rice pudding.
wiki.flask: A glass container commonly used in laboratories to hold liquids. The most common shapes of flask are a conical body with a tubular neck (an Erlenmeyer flask) and a spherical body with a tubular neck (a round-bottom flask).
wiki.candy cane: A hard, commonly striped candy resembling a cane, mostly seen around Christmas.
wiki.french fries: Long cut strips of potatoes that are deep fried. They are referred to as chips in British English and fried potato(es) in Japanese.
wiki.yunomi: A tall, roughly cylindrical cup with no handle, traditionally used in Japan to drink tea.
wiki.disposable coffee cup: A disposable cup designed for holding coffee. They're usually made of paper, with a snap-on lid and an insulating cardboard sleeve.
wiki.ice cube: A small piece of ice shaped like a square or rectangle. Water is frozen in an ice cube tray, then broken out and deposited into a glass to serve a beverage cold without relying on refrigeration.
wiki.omelet: A breakfast dish consisting of scrambled eggs with other ingredients folded in, such as cheese, meat (often ham or bacon), vegetables, or mushrooms.
wiki.bread slice: A single slice of bread, usually toast.
wiki.shaved ice: A Japanese dessert consisting of shaved ice in a cup, flavored with syrup and a sweetener (often condensed milk), and eaten with a spoon.
wiki.tokkuri: A ceramic bottle used to pour sake.
wiki.spatula: A flat kitchen utensil used for flipping in cooking, transferring food products from one tray/plate to another, or scraping food off a pan or bowl. A spatula can also refer to a flat rubber utensil for spreading frosting over dessert foods.
wiki.swirl lollipop: A lollipop that is flat and circular with a decorative (flavored) swirling pattern.
wiki.pastry: A baked good. This tag can be used if you don't know what pastry is being shown in the image, and you can't find the right one in the Food Tags group linked below.
wiki.dessert: Sugary sweet foods offered at the end of a meal. Usually topped with ice cream, whipped cream, or a fruit.
wiki.sweets: Foods that are rich in sugar. Candy for example.
wiki.cocktail glass: A drinking glass with a long stem and a wide conical bowl, designed to serve cocktails such as martinis.
wiki.milk bottle: A bottle that contains milk for shipment.
wiki.instant noodles: A form of noodles sold in a dry, precooked block, the most common noodles to be presented such being ramen. Invented in Japan in 1958 by Nissin, it has since spread to other countries, examples include America's "Top Ramen" and Britain's "Super Noodles".
wiki.strawberry shortcake: A cake with three layers (or more), the middle being cream and strawberries. Traditionally, the other two layers would be shortcake; but in Japan, strawberry "shortcake" is actually sponge cake. Include personification where it may apply.
wiki.egg (food): An egg meant to be eaten as food.
wiki.lemon slice: A slice of lemon, commonly seen as a garnish to cool drinks.
wiki.champagne flute: A drinking glass with a footed stem and a tall narrow bowl. It allows one to drink champagne without affecting its temperature.
wiki.milk carton: A drink carton that holds milk. Milk cartons can range in size from small square cartons carried on the go, to tall cartons kept in a refrigerator. The carton forms a triangle at the top that is easy to open.
wiki.skewer: A thin stick used to hold small pieces of food, especially grilled meat or vegetables.
wiki.potato chips: Snack food consisting of thinly sliced potato discs that are deep fried for crunchiness.
wiki.fried egg: An egg that has been fried with the yolk left intact. If the yolk is uncooked then the egg is sunny side up. A traditional breakfast food in western countries.
wiki.toast: A slice of bread that has been toasted. Often topped with butter or jam.
wiki.juice box: A small hand sized, typically rectangular, drink carton used to contain fruit juice. The drink inside is usually consumed with a drinking straw.
wiki.whisk: A mixing utensil made of stiff wire loops fixed to a handle; used for whipping eggs or cream. Typically used in a mixing bowl to form a batter. If a character is in the middle of using a whisk, add the whisking tag as well.
wiki.crepe: A type of very thin, cooked pancake usually made from wheat flour. Rolled up and often have a fruit filling of syrup, mixed berry, fresh fruit or lemon cream.
wiki.taiyaki: A Japanese fish-shaped cake. The most common filling is a red bean paste made from sweetened azuki beans.
wiki.sweet potato: Also called a camote, it is a type of tuber vegetable that isn't as starchy as the potato, but instead has a sweeter taste. Tends to be mislabeled as a yam, but they are from an entirely different botanical species. This is also known as a food that makes you gassy.
wiki.melting popsicle: A popsicle that is visibly melting. Common visual signs include large drops forming at the edge of the popsicle, a deformed appearance, and dripping down onto someone's body or onto the ground.
wiki.choko (cup): A small cylindrical cup for drinking sake. Not to be confused with the dish-shaped sakazuki.
wiki.chicken (food): Chicken as food, also known as chicken meat.
wiki.fish (food): Fish depicted as food. Popular around the world, especially in Asian countries.
wiki.sanshoku dango: Pink, green and white dango on a single skewer, also known as hanami dango (flower-viewing dango).
wiki.omurice: A Western-inspired Japanese dish that features rice cooked into an omelet, forming a pouch, and usually topped with ketchup. The ketchup is often poured to spell out words (such as the intended eater's name).
wiki.baguette: A baguette is a long thin loaf of bread. The slit cuts give it distinction, and is important during baking. Usually associated with France, its country of origin.
wiki.orange slice: A slice of orange (fruit), whether it is a thin slice cut through it or an actual slice that grows inside the rind.
wiki.chocolate bar: A large, flat block of chocolate, intended to be broken up into smaller pieces.
wiki.pie: A baked pastry crust encasing a fruit, chocolate, heavy cream, meat or vegetable filling.
wiki.berry: Ambiguous tag. → strawberry, blueberry, raspberry, cranberry, fruit, berry (pokemon), pokemon, Oran Berry
wiki.lettuce: An edible plant, eaten as a vegetable. This plant is popularly used in salads and on sandwiches, therefore lettuce is eaten raw.
wiki.ramune: A carbonated soft drink sold in Japan, typically in Codd-neck bottles, which use a glass marble as a stopper to keep the drink carbonated. The original formula is lemon-lime; nowadays there are many other flavors as well.
wiki.cucumber: A cylinder-shaped fruit, Cucumis sativus, with a thin green rind and white flesh. It is prepared and eaten as a vegetable, and is a favorite of kappas. Cats have an instinctual revulsion to the sight of them; it is believed they associate their appearance with snakes.
wiki.cotton candy: Melted sugar spun into thin threads and collected into a fluffy mass, usually on a stick or cone. Mostly enjoyed during festival events.
wiki.boned meat: A cartoonish portrayal of a large cylindrical cut of meat with the bone still in the center. Often used to represent hunger, or to symbolize food in general.
wiki.juice: A drink that is made from the extraction of liquid inside of various fruits and vegetables.
wiki.bendy straw: Also known as bendable straw or articulated straw. A drinking straw with a concertina-type hinge.
wiki.tiered tray: A stand for displaying and serving food with multiple levels.
wiki.oversized food: A food item that is much larger than normal, or large relative to the character holding it.
wiki.takoyaki: Japanese ball-shaped snack made out of batter, usually with octopus (tako) filling inside, but sometimes alternative fillings include corn kernels, meat, or tempura. Typically served with sauce, seaweed, and scallions sprinkled on it.
wiki.ketchup: A thick, tangy sauce used as a condiment. It is made from tomatoes, vinegar, and various seasonings and spices. Dispensed from a ketchup bottle.
wiki.fast food: Food such as burgers, hot dogs, and pizza that is ordered on the go and served quickly. It can be eaten at the restaurant or taken home.
wiki.mixing bowl: A type of bowl used for mixing various ingredients while cooking. Often seen in images showing characters making chocolate or baking a cake for someone's birthday.
wiki.picnic basket: A type of basket used to carry food for an outdoor picnic.
wiki.syrup: A thick, sticky, usually sweet liquid. Various syrups are commonly used as toppings, flavorings, or general sweeteners for all manner of food and drink.
wiki.tempura: A Japanese dish of deep fried battered meats, seafoods, or vegetables.
wiki.soup: A liquid food, generally served warm, made by cooking meat, noodles, or vegetables in broth, milk, or water, and flavored with salty, savory, spicy or other seasonings.
wiki.sausage: Similar to a hot dog, but has ground meat pumped into an edible casing either synthetically made or derived from animal intestines. Sausage making is a common method of preserving meats.
wiki.makizushi: Makizushi (巻き寿司, lit. "rolled sushi") is a type of long cylindrical sushi, usually rolled in nori (seaweed) sheets. A thick roll is called 太巻き (Futomaki) and a thin roll is called 細巻き (Hosomaki). For when the seaweed is on the inside of the roll, see uramaki.
wiki.cutting board: A wooden board that is used as a stable surface for food to be cut on.
wiki.cooler: An insulated container meant to keep drinks or food cool. Handy when going to the beach.
wiki.curry rice: Rice topped with curry. A popular dish in Japan.
wiki.oven mitts: Thick padded mittens that are used for handling hot pots and pans.
wiki.tropical drink: A beverage that is prepared and served in a glass decorated with tropical-themed items such as flowers and/or fruits.
wiki.icing: Icing, also called frosting, is a sweet glaze used to coat and decorate baked goods.
wiki.soda bottle: A bottle that stores soda. The bottle can either be made out of glass or plastic, and usually tapers to a thin neck.
wiki.eggplant: Egg-shaped fruit having a glossy skin and white flesh. Usually has a purple skin, but also comes in other colors such as white and orange. Used as a vegetable in cooking, closely related to tomatoes and potatoes. Also refers to the plant, which is a hairy herb of the nightshade family.
wiki.soda: A flavored carbonated soft drink, usually served in soda bottles, aluminum soda cans, or regular drinking glasses.
wiki.candy wrapper: A type of loose covering for a piece of candy, keeping it as fresh as possible until someone intends to eat it.
wiki.sundae: A dessert consisting of ice cream with any of various toppings added.
wiki.box of chocolates: A small gift box containing a tray lined with various shapes and/or flavors of chocolates. The chocolates inside the box should be visible. If you only see the lid covering the box's contents, just use gift box.
wiki.potato: A starchy tuber vegetable that grows in the ground. It is commonly made into mashed potatoes, chips (food), and french fries.
wiki.watermelon bar: A watermelon-flavored popsicle product made by Lotte (company), which really looks and tastes like a watermelon slice.
wiki.popcorn: A popular snack food made by heating up maize kernels until it can no longer tolerate the pressure and pops, releasing its starches inside. From there, the popcorn can be seasoned or sweetened as desired. It is iconic with watching movies.
wiki.honey: A sweet substance that is exclusively produced by honey bees using nectar from flowers. It is widely used for sweetening foods, for flavoring, and for medicinal properties.
wiki.bamboo steamer: A round or oval cookware made from bamboo with a lattice bottom and a cover. They are often stacked on top of each other so that the steam can cook many different servings simultaneously.
wiki.hot dog: A sausage served in a hot dog bun. The term can refer to the sausage itself, which is typically a wiener or a frankfurter, or the sausage and bun as a whole.
wiki.energy drink: A drink marketed for its stimulating effects, particularly soda-like drinks loaded with sugar and caffeine or other stimulant drugs.
wiki.cocktail: A mixed drink, usually a mixture of alcohol with fruit juice, flavored syrups, cream, or other ingredients. Usually served in a specialized cocktail glass, but an ordinary drinking glass may be used as well. More exotic cocktails are typically garnished with fruit and flowers and may be served in a coconut shell.
wiki.pizza slice: A single piece of pizza cut out from a whole pie.
wiki.snack: Any kind of light finger food consumed in between larger meals to satisfy hunger. Sweets covers sugary snacks, while dessert is for sweets served after a meal, usually dinner. Thus, this tag is for miscellaneous snacks like chips, popcorn, pretzels and crackers to name a few.
wiki.corn: Also known as maize. A cereal that consists of a cob with countless sweet kernels growing on it. Eating it straight off the cob is 'corn on the cob'.
wiki.dumpling: A dish that consists of small pieces of cooked dough, often wrapped around a filling. Dumplings may be prepared using a variety of cooking methods and are found in many world cuisines.
wiki.seaweed: A general term for macroscopic multi-cell marine algae. They generally appear like non-arboreal terrestrial plants. They are used for a variety of uses, including food, medicine, and fertilization.
wiki.pancake stack: A series of pancakes piled on top of each other until they form a small tower.
wiki.beans: Any type of legume vegetable grown inside a pod, such as chickpeas and soybeans, to name a few.
wiki.coconut: The fruit of the coconut tree. It has a hard brown shell, which holds edible white flesh; the liquid inside the cavity is called coconut milk. The entire fruit is covered by a fibrous outer husk which is usually removed before the coconut is further processed.
wiki.berry (pokemon): Items from the Pokémon franchise. They are fruit which have a wide range of applications, ranging from curing status ailments to cooking.
wiki.spaghetti: A type of pasta shaped like long circular strands when cooked. Arguably the most well-known kind of pasta in the world.
wiki.bag of chips: A bag of potato chips, or any other type of chip.
wiki.butter: A popular dairy product made by churning milk or cream and emulsified with water. The difference with margarine is that it is extracted from plant oils rather than animal. Often used on bread, pancakes, and waffles.
wiki.grill: A cooking device with a metal frame of parallel or crisscrossing bars used for grilling food over fire or other heating means.
wiki.kiwi (fruit): The edible fruit of the plant Actinidia deliciosa. It has a fuzzy brown skin and slightly acidic typically green flesh.
wiki.tongs: A tool consisting of two long arms joined at one end, used for picking up or holding things. Commonly used as a kitchen utensil.
wiki.green tea: A variety of tea made from matcha (food) powder. It is sometimes depicted in a yunomi, which is a Japanese teacup without handles.
wiki.crumbs: Small particles of crumbly food such as bread, cookies, cake, potato chips, and such.
wiki.shrimp tempura: A Japanese dish consisting of shrimp deep fried in tempura batter.
wiki.melon: Any of numerous fruits of the gourd family having a hard rind and sweet juicy flesh.
wiki.sugar cube: A small cube of sugar, used to sweeten coffee or other hot beverages.
wiki.ice cream float: A drink consisting of 1-2 scoops of ice cream (usually vanilla) mixed with cola, root beer, or other soda beverages.
wiki.steak: A cut of meat that is cooked to varying degrees of doneness, ranging in the following: very rare - rare - medium rare - medium - medium well done - well done. Without a qualifier, steak refers to beefsteak. Other types of steaks are defined, such as fish steak or venison steak.
wiki.onion: A type of bulb vegetable used in many cooking applications such as deep frying, seasoning, mirepoix, and even as a spice. A common joke is that cutting onions causes people to cry. This is due to a reaction that creates a type of gas that stings the eyes.
wiki.melon bread: A sweet crispy bread, so called because its appearance resembles a melon. It traditionally does not have melon flavoring, although some manufacturers may add melon flavoring when desired. There are also many variations depending on the additional ingredients.
wiki.kamaboko: A seafood product made by forming surimi (fish paste) into round loaves. They are usually then cut into thin slices and served over dishes such as ramen. The ones with a spiral pattern are called narutomaki.
wiki.salad: A dish consisting of cut vegetables tossed together in a bowl, typically doused in salad dressing to give it flavor.
wiki.radish: An edible root vegetable of the Brassicaceae family.
wiki.kagami mochi: A traditional Japanese New Year decoration consisting of two round mochi (rice cakes), the smaller placed atop the larger, and a daidai (mikan-like fruit) with an attached leaf on top.
wiki.chocolate cake: A cake made out of or flavored to be chocolate.
wiki.swiss roll: A type of cake where a flat sheet of baked batter is rolled together and held together with icing or whipped cream.
wiki.pizza box: A flat cardboard box made for delivering pizza.
wiki.food art: Food that has been arranged or prepared to create a work of art.
wiki.marshmallow: A confection that consists of sugar, corn syrup, water, gelatin that has been softened in hot water, dextrose, vanilla flavorings, and sometimes coloring, whipped to a spongy consistency. Common uses include hot chocolate, s'mores, and open fire roasting.
wiki.whiskey: A distilled alcoholic spirit. Whiskey (also spelled "whisky" in much of the English-speaking world outside the United States) is made from fermented grain mash in a process that starts out similarly to the brewing of beer, but it is then distilled and aged in a wooden cask, making the final product very different from…
wiki.pineapple: Edible fruit plant with a prickly outer skin and sweet, succulent yellow flesh.
wiki.invisible chair: When a character is sitting, as if on a chair, even though there is no visible structure beneath them.
wiki.on throne: Someone is on the throne. Usually they're sitting on it, but can include any other poses.
wiki.heart-shaped pillow: A pillow shaped like a heart.
wiki.swing: A hanging seat fastened to ropes or chains. If hanging from a purpose-built framework, it may be part of a swing set. Unconventional types of swings may lack a defined seat and can be made from other materials such as vines in a flower swing.
wiki.wheelchair: A chair with wheels to serve as a mobility aid when walking is difficult or impossible due to illness, injury, old age, or disability. Wheelchairs are moved either manually by its user or an attendant or by a built-in or attached electric motor.
wiki.yes-no pillow: A matching set of pillows, one blue and the other pink, with the words "Yes" and "No" written on them.
wiki.dakimakura (object): A dakimakura appearing within a picture. A dakimakura is a Japanese body pillow printed with anime characters on the both sides of the pillow, usually as a full-length portrait, lying on bed sheets on the one side, and frequently in a state of undress or nightwear variant on the another side.
wiki.mat: A padded piece of fabric used to cushion a person. Commonly used in sports like gymnastics to suppress the impact of a person during falls.
wiki.washing machine: An appliance used to wash clothes. The term applies primarily to machines that use water as opposed to dry cleaning or ultrasonic cleaners. The user adds laundry detergent, sold in liquid or powder form, to the wash water.
wiki.under kotatsu: A character sitting or lying under a kotatsu. Sometimes, the entire image is viewed from underneath the kotatsu.
wiki.zabuton: A zabuton (座布団) is a flat rectangular cushion used when sitting seiza on the floor.
wiki.wall clock: A clock that is hung on the wall.
wiki.easel: An upright tripod that is used to hold a drawing medium (such as an artist's canvas (object)) in position.
wiki.wading pool: A small, usually inflatable, shallow pool. Used as a makeshift outdoor swimming pool.
wiki.windowsill: The horizontal structure or surface at the bottom of a window.
wiki.bath stool: A stool, usually made of plastic, commonly used in Japanese bathrooms.
wiki.bicycle basket: A basket attached to the front of a bicycle or scooter for carrying bags, groceries, etc. while leaving the rider's hands free.
wiki.guard rail: A barrier placed alongside a road to prevent motor vehicles from going off the road.
wiki.card: A piece of small, flat material with something printed on it. This includes business cards, playing cards, trading cards, tarot cards, and any other type of card.
wiki.card (medium): An entire image drawn to look like a card, or is the image of the card face itself.
wiki.controller: A device used to operate or control a machine. This includes game controllers, remote controls for televisions and other appliances, and joysticks for arcade games or fighter jets.
wiki.trading card: A card with a picture or design printed on it, designed to be collected and traded as part of a collectible card game.
wiki.game console: A home video game console, used to play video games by connecting them to a television set.
wiki.d-pad: A D-pad (short for directional pad; also known as a joypad) is a flat, usually thumb-operated directional control with one button on each point, found on nearly all modern game controllers, and on the remote control units of some television, keypad cellphones and DVD players.
wiki.tarot: An image featuring a tarot card, or drawn to look like a tarot card.
wiki.board game: A tabletop game that involves moving pieces around a board according to a set of rules. It may also involve rolling dice or drawing cards to add an element of randomness.
wiki.poker chip: A small disk-shaped counter purchased at a casino, used to represent money when gambling. Different colors on the chips represent varying monetary values.
wiki.checkerboard cookie: A chocolate and butter squared cookie with a checkerboard pattern.
wiki.mahjong: A game for four players that originated in China. A very popular gambling game in east Asia, comparable to poker in the West. The object is to score points by forming certain combinations of mahjong tiles.
wiki.tarot (medium): An entire image drawn in the style of a tarot card.
wiki.yo-yo: A toy consisting of an axle connecting two discs, and a spool of string wound up in the center. It is played with by holding the loose end of the string and either throwing or dropping it to let gravity unwind the string, then rewind back into the user's hand.
wiki.ace of hearts: A playing card depicting the Ace (playing card) of hearts.
wiki.rook (chess): A chess piece with the design of a siege tower, meant to represent the rook, formerly called the castle, in the game of chess. The rook moves horizontally or vertically, through any number of unoccupied squares.
wiki.hanetsuki: Traditional Japanese New Year's game similar to badminton played with a feathered ball (hane) and a wooden paddle (hagoita). Players who fail to hit the ball have their face painted.
wiki.bishop (chess): A chess piece with the design of an abbot's mitre, meant to represent the bishop in the game of chess. The bishop has no restrictions in distance for each move, but is limited to diagonal movement.
wiki.queen (chess): A chess piece with a spiked crown design, meant to represent the queen in the game of chess. The queen is the most powerful piece in the game of chess, able to move any number of squares vertically, horizontally or diagonally.
wiki.king (chess): A chess piece with a crown that has a cross on top, meant to represent the king in the game of chess. The objective in chess is to capture the opponent's king piece in a move called checkmate. Although the king is the most important piece, it is usually the weakest piece in the game until a later phase, the endgame.
wiki.ace of spades: A playing card depicting the Ace (playing card) of spade (shape)s.
wiki.instrument: An instrument used for playing music.
wiki.eighth note: A musical note representing an eighth note (1/8 of a whole note). Notated with a filled-in note head with a straight stem and one flag, like this: ♪.
wiki.cowbell: A typically rectangular bell used on neck bells for livestock, such cattle or sheep, or more frequently in anime, cow girls and cow boys.
wiki.electric guitar: A guitar that uses a pickup to convert the vibration of its strings into electrical impulses. The most common guitar pickup uses the principle of direct electromagnetic induction. The signal generated by an electric guitar is too weak to drive a loudspeaker, so it is amplified before sending it to a loudspeaker.
wiki.beamed eighth notes: A group of eighth notes connected with a horizontal beam. For example: ♫.
wiki.plectrum: A small flat tool used to pick or strum any string instrument, such as guitars and harps. Also called a pick.
wiki.treble clef: The musical symbol (𝄞) used to designate notes on the treble staff, or in layman's terms, the upper range of notes. This most common of clefs is associated with soprano and alto voices, violin, flute and many other high-pitched instruments. In art, the treble clef is sometimes used as a general symbol for music.
wiki.mp3 player: A portable digital device that stores, organizes and plays audio files. Mainly used to play MP3 music files, although most devices can play other file formats as well, and some can even play videos.
wiki.flute: A cylindrical wind instrument with one embrochure hole and six to eleven finger holes or keys. It is usually made of wood or metal.
wiki.bass guitar: A plucked string instrument, closely related to the guitar. See double bass for the traditional bowed string instrument.
wiki.electric bass guitar: A plucked string instrument, closely related to the guitar. See double bass for the traditional bowed string instrument.
wiki.speaker: A device that converts electronic signals into audible sounds. Often placed on the floor or on a desk mounted to a pole or a wall. Often used a a part of a stereo system, public address system, computer setup, or home theater system.
wiki.quarter note: A musical note representing a quarter note (1/4 of a whole note). Visually, it appears like ♩ (a filled-in oval with a note stem (vertical line) that can be drawn upward or downward).
wiki.drumsticks: A pair of sticks used to strike drums or other percussion instruments to produce sound.
wiki.instrument case: A case that holds and protects a musical instrument for transport and storage.
wiki.beamed sixteenth notes: A group of sixteenth notes connected with a horizontal beam, like this: ♬
wiki.keyboard (instrument): A musical instrument that has a piano-style keyboard but is not itself a piano.
wiki.musical staff: A set of five horizontal lines and four spaces that each represent a different musical pitch or, in the case of a percussion staff, different percussion instruments. Appropriate musical notes, depending upon the intended effect, are placed on the staff according to their corresponding pitch or function.
wiki.staff (music): A set of five horizontal lines and four spaces that each represent a different musical pitch or, in the case of a percussion staff, different percussion instruments. Appropriate musical notes, depending upon the intended effect, are placed on the staff according to their corresponding pitch or function.
wiki.trumpet: A brass musical instrument which is played by means of three piston or rotary valves. It has an oblong-shaped tubular body and a flared bell.
wiki.guitar case: An instrument case that holds and protects a guitar for transport and storage.
wiki.bow (music): A special rod used in the playing of stringed musical instruments such as violin, viola, cello, double bass/contrabass and their various relatives.
wiki.grand piano: A type of acoustic piano whose strings, frame and soundboard are laid out horizontally. Can be found in varying lengths between roughly five and ten feet, from the keyboard at one end to the tail at the other.
wiki.acoustic guitar: A guitar that uses only an acoustic sound board to help transmitting the strings' vibrational energy to the air in order to produce music.
wiki.sheet music: A sheet of paper bearing musical notes and symbols used as a reference to play a piece of music.
wiki.phonograph: A device used for playing recorded sound by picking up recorded grooves with a stylus. A modern phonograph with an electronic pick-up is called a turntable.
wiki.fortissimo: A dynamic notation used in written music, which denotes a dynamic or volume of "very loud" and is typically depicted in script "ff" letters.
wiki.drum set: A collection of drums and other percussion instruments such as cymbals arranged to be played by a single person. Also called a drum kit or a trap set.
wiki.bass clef: The musical symbol (𝄢) used to designate notes on the bass staff, or in layman's terms, the lower range of notes. This most common of clefs is associated with bass voices, contrabass (a.k.a. double bass), bass guitar and other low-pitched instruments.
wiki.recorder: A family of woodwind instruments. The most common type are soprano recorders, with low cost plastic versions frequently issued to school children since the 20th century.
wiki.amplifier: A device used to amplify electric instruments so they can produce sound. Amplifiers are most commonly used for electric guitars and basses.
wiki.lute (instrument): A family of plucked string instruments with a neck (either fretted or unfretted) and a deep round back.
wiki.conductor baton: A baton used by a conductor to instruct a musical group, such as an orchestra, band (music), or choir.
wiki.baton (conducting): A baton used by a conductor to instruct a musical group, such as an orchestra, band (music), or choir.
wiki.harp: A string instrument having an upright triangular frame consisting of a pillar, a curved neck, and a hollow back containing the sounding board, with strings of graded lengths that are played by plucking with the fingers.
wiki.cross: A symbol or object that consists of two intersecting perpendicular lines, with one or both lines divided in half by the intersection.
wiki.box: Any cubic or rectangular container used to hold something inside it.
wiki.rigging: Equipment worn by the shipgirls of Kantai Collection or Azur Lane for example, usually strapped to their backs and limbs.
wiki.thought bubble: A speech bubble that shows what a character is thinking, imagining, or dreaming of. It consists of a large bubble followed by a series of smaller bubbles coming out of a character's head, rather than a pointed end coming out of the character's mouth.
wiki.paper: A thin material mainly used for writing upon, printing upon, drawing or for packaging. It is produced by pressing together moist fibers, typically cellulose pulp derived from wood or grass, and drying them into flexible sheets.
wiki.abyssal ship: Abyssal ships (深海棲艦, shinkaisei-kan) are monstrous enemy ships in the Kantai Collection universe.
wiki.poke ball: A spherical capsule used to capture and store Pokémon. The most common and recognized Poké Ball is the basic Poké ball, which has two colored halves: red on top and white on bottom. It is one of the central symbols of the franchise. Known as a Monster Ball in Japan.
wiki.skull: The bony remains of one's head.
wiki.open book: A book that is visibly open.
wiki.sign: A piece of typically flat material meant to display certain information.
wiki.arrow (symbol): A symbol, such as → or ←, that is used to point or indicate a direction. Not to be confused with arrow (projectile), which is an arrow fired from a bow.
wiki.character doll: A doll representation of a human character. For animal or creature characters, use stuffed animal instead.
wiki.anchor symbol: A symbol bearing the appearance of an anchor.
wiki.chinese zodiac: The Shēngxiào (Chinese: 生肖), better known in English as the Chinese Zodiac, is a scheme that relates each year to an animal and its reputed attributes, which, combined with the 5 Chinese elements (fire, water, earth, wood, metal), creates a 60-year cycle.
wiki.holding poke ball: Someone is holding a Poké Ball of any type. (it may be a Master Ball, a Repeat Ball, etc.)
wiki.flag: A piece of fabric, often flown from a pole or mast, decorated with emblems, symbols, or shapes to represent a country or an event.
wiki.id card: Any type of card used for identification: student IDs, driving licenses, employee badges, and so on. May be held by a lanyard.
wiki.anchor: A hooked device used to restrain a ship to the seabed.
wiki.duel monster: A card monster from the Yu-Gi-Oh! series. This is not limited to Monster cards, and also includes elements, items or characters seen on Spell and Trap cards. This tag also covers cards from Yu-Gi-Oh! Rush Duel.
wiki.string: A long flexible structure made from fibers twisted together into a single strand. It is thicker than a thread.
wiki.photo (object): When a drawing contains a photograph, but the actual post is not a photo (medium).
wiki.in container: A character inside a container of some kind.
wiki.shell: The hard outer covering that protects the soft insides of certain animals, such as insects, turtles, and mollusks. Humans use them for a wide variety of purposes.
wiki.oversized object: A character holding or interacting with an object significantly bigger than normal relative to their size. This includes minigirls and miniboys interacting with normal-sized objects much bigger than them.
wiki.syringe: A syringe is a simple piston pump consisting of a plunger that fits tightly in a tube. This tag is used to describe a hypodermic needle, which is a hollow needle commonly used to inject substances into the body or used to take liquid samples from the body.
wiki.tape: A long strip of plastic or adhesive material.
wiki.iron cross: The Iron Cross (Eiserne Kreuz) is a German military symbol and medal, consisting of a black cross pattée with a white outline. It has been used by Kingdom of Prussia, the German Empire (1871-1918), Nazi Germany (1933-1945), and by the Bundeswehr (the modern German armed forces) since 1956.
wiki.yin yang: A circular symbol consisting of a white and black droplet; a tomoe (symbol). In Chinese philosophy, Yin and Yang represent opposite but complementary qualities (Balance).
wiki.object on head: An object that isn't conventional headgear resting or balancing atop someone's head.
wiki.saucer: A small plate that is use to support cups, more specifically teacups.
wiki.orb: A sphere; be it for decoration, containment, or the shape one manifests magic. Usually, but not limited to, the size of a crystal ball.
wiki.mobile suit: Mobile Suit, often abbreviated as MS, is the name of the mecha in the Gundam series. It basically refers to any (mostly) humanoid giant robot (standing from about 15 to 20+ meters tall) that is piloted by a human soldier (aside from G Gundam, which uses the term Mobile Fighter).
wiki.gold: A soft, dense yellow metal often used for both money and jewelry.
wiki.single mechanical arm: A character with one mechanical arm.
wiki.karakasa obake: An umbrella traditional youkai. It has one eye, a long tongue and a single foot. Also known as 唐傘小僧 (Karakasa Kozou, Karakasa Boy).
wiki.heart-shaped box: A box shaped like a heart. Popular with Valentine gifts containing chocolates.
wiki.drawing (object): A drawing that a character is making, or has already made. This is not to be used for the whole image itself.
wiki.flip phone: A cellphone that features a clamshell design that flips open.
wiki.paper fan: A paper fan that isn't a harisen, the type of folded paper fan often found in Japanese comedy.
wiki.bone: The substance that forms the skeleton of the body. It is composed chiefly of calcium phosphate and calcium carbonate. It also serves as a storage area for calcium, playing a large role in calcium balance in the blood. There are 206 bones in the adult human body.
wiki.colored speech bubble: Speech bubble that is colored any color other than black or white.
wiki.sticker: A piece of paper or plastic, sticky on one side and non-stick on the other, with a design or text printed on it. Stickers are often used for play or advertising.
wiki.painting (object): A physical painting set inside an image. For example, a painting hanging on a wall.
wiki.lightning bolt symbol: A symbol shaped like a stylized lightning bolt (ex: 🗲 or ↯).
wiki.gears: A mechanical part of a clockwork system, a gear is a wheel with so-called flanks so it will interlock with other gears and spin. Radius of the wheel and edge sizes allow spinning at different speeds and thus make processing different. Obviously used the most in non-digital watches.
wiki.stick: A relatively short, small piece of wood, of the kind roughly broken off a tree. Do not use for other objects that have a more specific tag; see below.
wiki.lock: A device used to hold a door, chain, container, or other similar object securely shut. It may be opened with a key inserted in a keyhole, or by using a code in a combination lock.
wiki.hose: A long rubber tube through which water runs.
wiki.gourd: The gourd is a member of the plant family Cucurbitaceae and a relative of the pumpkin. When dried, its fruit can be hollowed out and used as a container. It is also used as food.
wiki.towel on head: Someone wearing a towel on their head.
wiki.radio antenna: A metallic device used to receive radio signals.
wiki.pentagram: A five-pointed star (symbol) drawn with five straight lines.
wiki.assault visor: A type of glass visor prominent in science fiction works, frequently seen as part of helmet designs or as part of mecha head designs.
wiki.circle: A circle is a curved two-dimensional shape in which all points on the curve are the same distance from its center. Images with this tag include one or more circular shapes as a major part of the image.
wiki.shide: A paper streamer cut in a zig-zagging fashion used in Shinto rituals. A common element of a gohei or shimenawa.
wiki.folded fan: When a folding fan is closed.
wiki.tomoe (symbol): A comma-shaped symbol. Three of them in a circular arrangement make a mitsudomoe_(shape).
wiki.diamond button: One or multiple buttons in the shape of a diamond (shape) (♢).
wiki.christmas ornaments: Ornaments for hanging on Christmas trees. They come in many shapes and colors, with the most common being a round ball.
wiki.latin cross: A cross where the descending arm is longer than the other three arms. It is the most common form of Christian cross.
wiki.lifebuoy: A type of swim ring designed to be thrown to a person in the water to prevent drowning.
wiki.stylus: A pen-like pointing device used for drawing (action) and writing on a digital device, such as a drawing tablet.
wiki.string of fate: The red string of fate (unmei no akai ito, 運命の赤い糸) is an East Asian belief that every person in the world is connected to another by an invisible red string tied to the little finger of their left hand. The two people connected by the red string are destined to be lovers. Closely related to the concept of soulmates.
wiki.head-mounted display: A display device which completely covers the eyes and is not transparent. It doesn't need to be used for virtual reality, but odds are that the visor displays some sort of visual or tactical image to the user.
wiki.toy: An object designed to provide amusement, often a replica or model of something, but can be baubles, trinkets, or electronics.
wiki.figure: A small-scale statue modeled after a character. This includes both figures physically present inside an image, and photos of actual figures.
wiki.triangle: Any shape that is formed using three straight lines.
wiki.in box: Someone or something is in a box.
wiki.running bond: An extremely common style of brickwork or paving where regular rectangular bricks are laid in rows end to end, with each row staggered by the length of half a brick. Also known as stretcher bond.
wiki.mitsudomoe (shape): Three tomoe_(symbol) (comma-shaped symbols) in a circular arrangement.
wiki.shikishi: Shikishi is a particular format of paperboard for art, calligraphy, poetry and autographs. Recognizable by its squarish dimensions, it also has characteristic edges which are often evident in posts that are photo (medium)s of traditional media pieces.
wiki.puppet: A doll of cloth or wood, which can be operated by a puppeteer by means of strings and cable or by wearing it as a glove.
wiki.japari symbol: A symbol used to represent Japari Park in Kemono Friends; it can also represent the real-world franchise.
wiki.lotion: Any kind of cream or gel applied to the skin.
wiki.flower symbol: An illustration of flowers as a symbol, rather than actual flowers themselves.
wiki.pill: A dose of solid medicine compressed into an easy to swallow size. Usually comes in blister packs or pill bottles.
wiki.string of flags: A string of flag or pennants strung together for decorative purposes.
wiki.skull and crossbones: A symbol consisting of a human skull and two long bones crossed together under the skull. This symbol has a few different uses, but two of the more common uses are as a symbol for poison and as a symbol for piracy.
wiki.roman numeral: The ancient Roman way of writing numbers. Likely because of the elegant style, it is still usually recognized and understood by everyday people (at least from 1 to 10), and is frequently used on clocks.
wiki.clothes hanger: An object meant to imitate human shoulders so clothes can be hung on it. It is normally triangular in shape, with a C-hook at the top.
wiki.paddle: An object with a broad blade attached to a handle. Uses include table tennis and spankings.
wiki.keyhole: The hole in a lock where the key is inserted and turns.
wiki.mallet: A hammer-like device with flat pounding ends.
wiki.hadanugi dousa: Wearing a kimono (or other similar garment) with one shoulder stripped to the waist, often done by kyuudou practitioners.
wiki.magazine (object): A periodical publication containing articles and illustrations, typically covering a particular subject or area of interest. For pornographic magazines also use pornography.
wiki.hexagram: An often hollow six-pointed star (symbol) (✡︎) formed by overlapping two equilateral triangles. When used as a symbol of Jewish religion or cultural identity, it is called the Star of David. Its three-dimensional analogue is the stellated octahedron.
wiki.wire: A bare, uncoated cylindrical length of metal, commonly used to conduct electricity.
wiki.sun symbol: A graphical representation of the sun, composed of a central disk with a definite number of rays (☼), that appears as design or prints in shirts, emblems, medals, flags, and the like. (See post #715813)
wiki.emoji: A small icon embedded in text used to express various emotions or concepts.
wiki.inflatable toy: An air-filled beach toy or flotation device (aside from innertubes, inflatable rafts, and beachballs). These are usually shaped like sea creatures such as crocodiles, sharks, dolphins and whales.
wiki.corded phone: A phone with a cord attached to the receiver, as opposed to a cordless phone or modern cellphone.
wiki.drone: An unmanned vehicle (aerial, ground, or sea), piloted via remote control (remote control vehicle) or autonomous AI.
wiki.vial: A small, usually glass, vessel typically used to contain small amounts of liquids or powders, especially medicine or chemical samples. They are made in various shapes and sizes, but typically small enough to be hold between fingers.
wiki.cube: A geometric object with six faces of equal area. A common example would be dice.
wiki.year of the ox: The Ox occupies the second position in the Chinese Zodiac. Years of birth include 1913, 1925, 1937, 1949, 1961, 1973, 1985, 1997, 2009, 2021, 2033.
wiki.manga (object): A manga or doujin appearing within an image. This includes western comic books.
wiki.industrial pipe: A tube of metal, plastic, or other material used to convey water, gas, oil, or other fluid substances.
wiki.drawing tablet: On Danbooru this will typically refer to a flat, rectangular surface used as a tactile interface to a computer-based drawing program. Often this is used in conjunction with a stylus, to better approximate the handling of a real-life pen, pencil or brush.
wiki.striker unit: The magic-powered flight mechanisms attached to the girls' legs in World Witches Series, loosely based on World War II-era aircraft. Very often the girls wear no pants when equipping them. There are also land striker units based on tanks.
wiki.ufo: Short for "Unidentified Flying Object". Stereotypical depiction of an alien spacecraft originated from various description of the supposed spotting of alien spacecraft during the 1950 - 1970s "UFO craze" around the Americas.
wiki.flying saucer: A disc shaped spacecraft often popularized by UFO descriptions and early 20th century Sci-Fi. Examples include the vessel in The Day the Earth Stood Still, and Red Noah from Fushigi no Umi no Nadia.
wiki.coral: Corals are marine invertebrates belonging to the class Anthozoa of the phylum Cnidaria. Typically, many identical polyps live in dense colonies. Corals contain important reef producers in tropical oceans that secrete calcium carbonate to form a hard skeleton.
wiki.thrusters: Rocket or jet based propulsion systems usually used in aircraft, spacecraft, or mecha.
wiki.racket: A type of bat with strings hung in a round frame. Used for playing tennis, badminton, and squash.
wiki.poke ball print: Clothing or an object with printings of the Poké Ball from the Pokémon franchise.
wiki.mars symbol: The ♂ symbol representing the male gender. This symbol is considered to be a stylized representation of the shield and spear of Mars from Roman mythology.
wiki.trick or treat: Ambiguous tag. See Trick or Treat (phrase) for the phrase "Trick or Treat" written in an image, or trick-or-treating for characters going trick-or-treating.
wiki.video camera: A camera that captures video. This includes both personal camcorders and professional TV and movie cameras.
wiki.pocky day: Posts referencing 11/11, known as Pocky Day, or Pocky & Pretz Day (Pepero Day in South Korea).
wiki.scepter: A ceremonial rod that has been used as a symbol of power since ancient times. Scepters are usually relatively short, hand-held objects made of precious metals and inlaid with gems, often carried by royalty.
wiki.heart balloon: A balloon that is shaped like a heart.
wiki.poke ball symbol: A symbol representing a Poké Ball. This does not include Poké Ball prints, Poké Ball hair ornaments, or actual Poké Balls.
wiki.ritual baton: A long and flat scepter, often made from bamboo. It originates from ancient China, where it originally served as an object to write on. It is strongly associated with ancient noblemen, shinto priests, and hina ningyou.
wiki.banknote: Paper money, as opposed to coins.
wiki.super robot: Super Robot (スーパーロボット Sūpā Robotto) is an old genre of anime focused on giant robot mecha with various super powers, special and flashy weapons, and the cliche of attack/special move naming.
wiki.mimikaki: A tool used for ear cleaning. The most common design has a fuzzy tip on one end and small spoon on the other end. Also known as an ear pick or an ear spoon.
wiki.red cross: A + sign colored red, commonly used as the Red Cross logo and seen on nurse caps.
wiki.hammer and sickle: The hammer and sickle is a part of communist symbolism and its usage indicates an association with Communism, a Communist party, or a Communist state. It symbolizes the unity of peasants and workers.
wiki.union jack: Also known as the Union Flag, it is the name given to the national flag of the United Kingdom. It is a combination of three different flags: the red St. George's Cross of England, the white St. Andrew's Cross of Scotland, and the red St.
wiki.colored shoe soles: Shoe soles that are differently colored from the rest of the shoe.
wiki.triforce: The Triforce is the symbol of Hyrule in The Legend of Zelda series. The Triforce is split into three different parts, which in the games are always borne by the three central characters of the Zelda saga: • The Triforce of Courage, which is held by Link (lower right) • The Triforce of Wisdom, which is held by Princess…
wiki.wheel: A circular device that can rotate on its axis and can facilitate movement and transportation, or perform labor on machinery.
wiki.screen: A variety of forms or formats of information display, such as viewing surfaces or areas for movies or motion pictures, slide presentations, information viewing areas for electronic device display output, various areas of video games, etc.
wiki.halloween bucket: A container used by trick-or-treaters for holding Halloween candy. Frequently pumpkin-shaped and/or decorated like a jack-o'-lantern.
wiki.soap: Hygiene product used for washing, bathing and cleaning yourself.
wiki.three-dimensional maneuver gear: In Shingeki no Kyojin, the Three-Dimensional Maneuver Gear is a set of gear developed by humans that allows great mobility when facing the Titan (Shingeki no Kyojin)s.
wiki.akeome: Akeome, short for akemashite omedetou gozaimasu, is a casual Japanese New Year's greeting. Functionally equivalent to "Happy New Year" in English.
wiki.venus symbol: The ♀ symbol representing the female gender. This symbol is considered to be a stylized representation of the hand mirror of Venus from Roman mythology.
wiki.handkerchief: A small piece of fabric used for personal hygiene such as wiping one's face or blowing one's nose.
wiki.traditional youkai: A class of supernatural entities in Japanese mythology. Youkai include a vast range of beings, including shapeshifters, ghosts, demons, and tricksters. They can be mischievous, helpful, or malevolent, often appearing as animal-like figures, possessed objects, or humanoids.
wiki.year of the dragon: The Dragon is the fifth of the 12 Chinese zodiac animals. Years of the Dragon include 1928, 1940, 1952, 1964, 1976, 1988, 2000, 2012, and 2024.
wiki.inverted cross: An upside-down † symbol, generally a Latin cross. Also called St. Peter's Cross.
wiki.crest: A very intricate, detailed symbol used for the highest means of representing nobility such as for a well regarded family.
wiki.caution tape: Various colored tape that can carry words like "Keep out" or "Crime scene: Do not enter". Usually the tape has a yellow background with black text, but other variants do exist like orange/black or in the case of police caution tape, white background with blue or black text with or without a checkered square pattern.
wiki.paint palette: A thin board on which a painter lays and mixes colors.
wiki.palette (object): A thin board on which a painter lays and mixes colors.
wiki.potion: A vial, flask, bottle, or other container holding a usually brightly colored liquid. Common depictions are healing potions, mana potions, and aphrodisiacs.
wiki.vaulting horse: A vaulting horse (Jap. tobibako), is a common piece of equipment in Japanese school gyms, and is often used to establish that the scene is in a gym storeroom.
wiki.intravenous drip: Medical therapy in which a liquid is infused into the body by means of a small bag connected to a tube which is injected into a person's veins. It is commonly abbreviated as "IV" or "IVD".
wiki.pointer: A stick (wood, plastic, or metal) used by instructors such as teachers and military persons. Some even have tips shaped like a pointing hand. Not to be confused with a laser pointer or riding crop.
wiki.phallic symbol: An innocuous object that resembles or is sexually suggestive of a penis. Common examples include bananas, mushrooms, carrots, cucumbers, eggplants, makizushi, popsicles and hot dogs, especially since some of these items can produce suggestive fluids.
wiki.cat teaser: A toy wand used to entertain cats. At its tip there can be feathers, beads, or a bell.
wiki.mechanical pencil: A pencil with a push button on the top and an internal mechanism which pushes its lead through the tip.
wiki.no blindfold: A character who normally wears a blindfold is seen without one. Frequently seen with Medusa (rider) (fate), 2B (nier:automata), and Jingliu_(honkai:_star_rail).
wiki.dowsing rod: A Y or L shaped rod used for divining the location of water, oils, gravesites, or finding radioactive materials. Dowsing rods are sometimes used in a way not too dissimilar from a Ouija board, in which you ask a question and if the Dowsing rod moves the answer is yes. It can be made from a variety of materials.
wiki.school briefcase: A type of briefcase carried by students. Compared to a school bag, it has more rigid appearance, and often a handle on top.
wiki.hexagon: A polygon with six sides and six angles.
wiki.shikigami: Originally from Onmyoudo mysticism, a deity represented by a small ghost. In the context of modern storytelling, they're usually portrayed as summoned shape-shifters originating from parchment, sometimes in the shape of a small paper doll or talisman resembling a rudimentary human figure.
wiki.broken chain: A broken chain is present in the image.
wiki.ankh: The ancient Egyptian hieroglyphic character that means "life". It is a cross shape topped by a droplet-shaped loop.
wiki.spiked shell: A shell adorned with spikes, such as a turtle shell, clam shell, or snail shell.
wiki.konohagakure symbol: The symbol of Konohagakure, a village in Naruto (series).
wiki.runes: Letters from real or fictional runic alphabets, or other similar writing symbols.
wiki.bookmark: A thin tool, usually made of cardboard, plastic, or ribbon, inserted between the pages of a book to mark a place where the reader intends to continue reading or to refer back to later.
wiki.sunscreen: A cream, lotion, or oil used to protect against sunburn, or to promote a suntan.
wiki.antique phone: A vintage phone from before the advent of push-button phones with touch-tone dialing in the 1960s. This includes antique candlestick phones, as well as rotary phones.
wiki.lighter: A small hand-held object used to create a small fire. Commonly used to light cigarettes.
wiki.pentacle: An amulet used to cast magic; not to be confused with pentagram, which is a geometric shape. While the word implies the use of a pentagram, it can also use a hexagram. Often worn as a pendant.
wiki.party popper: A popular noise maker, commonly used at parties. It emits a loud popping noise by means of a small explosive charge when its string is pulled. Sometimes there are streamers hidden inside. They are also referred to as 'party crackers'. They are not considered fireworks.
wiki.pornography: In-world pornographic or erotic media (DVD (object)s, posters, manga (object), magazine (object)s, etc.). Not for entire images that are pornographic themselves.
wiki.star sticker: A sticker shaped like a star.
wiki.streamers: Streamers are thin strips of paper in various sizes thrown at parties and celebrations. Larger streamers are usually hung as decorations, while party poppers often contain very small streamers.
wiki.angel and devil: An angel and a demon appearing together. This is usually done in an artistic way that shows contrast between light and darkness, but in anime art angel/devil yuri and yaoi pairings are also very popular.
wiki.reins: A long, narrow strap attached at one end to a horse's bit, typically used in pairs to guide or check a horse while riding or driving, the rider typically holding the reins.
wiki.deer antlers: The antlers of a deer girl or deer boy.
wiki.arrow through heart: A symbolic representation of a character being in love (💘). Comes from Greek mythology with the god Eros (mythology) (Cupid) shooting people with magic arrows which could create feelings of love.
wiki.duster: A small handheld cleaning implement that is used to remove dust off surfaces. For the cowboy garment, use duster coat.
wiki.donation box: A box used to store monetary donations or religious offerings, usually at a shrine. In Japanese, the offerings are known as saisen (賽銭), and in turn, the donation boxes are known as saisen-bako (賽銭箱).
wiki.italian flag: The national flag of Italy, which consists of three different colored stripes in a column; green on the left, white in the middle, and red on the right.
wiki.puppet strings: The wires attached to a marionette and either a control bar or puppet rings, often used as a graphical metaphor of one person controlling another.
wiki.sponge: A soft porous object used for washing or cleaning.
wiki.canvas (object): A fabric stretched across a wooden frame, used as a painting surface for acrylic painting and oil_painting_(medium). A canvas is often held upright on an easel while the artist is working on it.
wiki.gem (symbol): The 💎 symbol. A symbol representing a diamond_(gemstone) gem. Typically seen on Idolmaster character cards as a white symbol over a blue background.
wiki.portrait (object): When a post contains a portrait, but the post itself is not a portrait.
wiki.yin yang orb: An orb with the appearance of a yin yang sign.
wiki.pinwheel: A small toy consisting of paper or plastic curls attached as its axle to a stick, designed to spin when blown by the wind or a person.
wiki.machine: Any device that uses energy to perform some activity.
wiki.rolling suitcase: A suitcase that has wheels on the bottom and commonly an elongating handle that makes it easier to roll heavier suitcases on the ground.
wiki.propeller: A multi-bladed device that rotates to push against air or water. Commonly seen on a piston-powered aircraft or ship.
wiki.visor (armor): The part of a helmet that covers and protects wearer's face. It can be lifted.
wiki.coffin: A commonly 6-sided funerary box with removable lid used in the display and containment of dead people, either for burial or cremation.
wiki.round-bottom flask: A type of laboratory flask with a spherical bottom and a cylindrical neck.
wiki.pennant: A type of flag that is triangular in shape.
wiki.drugs: Narcotics and/or stimulants which change a person's behaviour, perception, or numbs them to pain.
wiki.spell card: A magically infused card used to cast spells.
wiki.loaded interior: A room or indoor scene loaded with dense visual details. The outdoors equivalent is complex exterior.
wiki.inkwell: A small container holding ink, into which a pen can be dipped.
wiki.ink bottle: A small container holding ink, into which a pen can be dipped.
wiki.grimoire: A grimoire is a book of instructions on magic and/or alchemy.
wiki.poster (medium): When the entire image is a poster. This can be a scan or photo (medium) of a real poster, or a fanart parody of a poster.
wiki.doily: A circular, ornamental mat made in a lace-like pattern, made of lace, paper, or linen.
wiki.laundry: Dirty clothes that have been hand or machine washed, and then hung out to dry in the sun or dried inside a tumble-dry machine. Visual cues include a bundle of clothes or towels, a laundry hamper, a clothesline, clothespins, laundry pole, laundry basket, and/or washing and drying machines.
wiki.heart-shaped lock: A lock in the shape of a heart.
wiki.rotary phone: A type of phone that utilizes a wheel with holes and a finger stop to dial phone numbers. Later supplanted by the "touch-tone" phone that uses a keypad to enter phone numbers.
wiki.kine: A kine (杵) is a lopsided mallet-like pestle used to pound rice into mochi.
wiki.teruterubouzu: A Japanese doll hung by the window to bring about the change of weather. Hanging it right-side-up acts as a prayer for fair weather, while hanging it upside-down acts as a prayer for rain.
wiki.pendulum: A weight suspended from a pivot so that it can swing freely. When a pendulum is displaced sideways from its resting, equilibrium position, it is subject to a restoring force due to gravity that will accelerate it back toward the equilibrium position.
wiki.screw: A fastener. May be similar in appearance to a bolt (hardware). Screwed in place either by hand or with a screwdriver. Some have a tapered end; but others, such as computer screws, do not.
wiki.haniwa (statue): Terracotta clay sculptures buried with the dead as funerary objects during the proto-historic Kofun period in Japan. Various types of haniwa were created, ~ soldier, horse, dog and other animals. The haniwa soldiers wear ancient-style body armors, tentatively called tankou (lit.
wiki.art brush: A small, round- or flat-tipped brush typically used for painting art.
wiki.radio: A system used for wireless communication, often compact in size and having adjustment dials.
wiki.butterfly net: A type of hand net used for capturing butterflies. For tagging purposes this is used for any type of net used for capturing bugs.
wiki.blank speech bubble: An empty speech bubble, commonly an exploitable template for others to insert their own comment.
wiki.henshin: Henshin (変身, lit. "transformation") is the term for the transformation sequences commonly seen in tokusatsu, mecha, and magical girl anime where a character transforms from their ordinary form into a more powerful form. The term is derived from Kafka's The Metamorphosis.
wiki.kaiju: Kaiju (怪獣, lit. "strange beast") is a genre of tokusatsu entertainment involving giant monsters.
wiki.kaijuu: Kaiju (怪獣, lit. "strange beast") is a genre of tokusatsu entertainment involving giant monsters.
wiki.evangelion (mecha): A type of giant robot mecha from the anime Neon Genesis Evangelion.
wiki.broken heart: A pair of disjoint pieces of a heart, which signify a crushing blow to one's romantic desires. Can be representative of disappointment, sadness, or rejection. It is generally used for comedic purposes.
wiki.crayon: A stick of pigmented wax used for writing or drawing.
wiki.spoiler (automobile): An extension at the back of a car, typically in the shape of a flat plate with two smaller plates covering both ends. The spoiler improves the vehicle's aerodynamic quality at high speed by redirecting airflow to the back.
wiki.napkin: A piece of cloth or paper manufactured to clean off the hands and face while eating.
wiki.toilet paper: Papers in either sheets or a roll, used for wiping one's genitalia after using the restroom.
wiki.oda uri: The kamon (family crest) of the Oda clan
wiki.pencil case: A bag or case often carried by students meant to secure smaller items like pencils, pens, erasers, and so on to prevent their loss.
wiki.fumo (doll): A line of stuffed character dolls most often based on Touhou characters. Dolls based on characters from other franchises such as Elden Ring and Mahou Shoujo Madoka Magica are also available.
wiki.family crest: A crest used as a symbol of various clans/families in Japan. Especially one with considerable amount of influence within their region or the entire country. Also referred outside of Japan as "mon" (紋), though the word mon is used to refer to any crest in general in Japan.
wiki.pet bowl: A bowl intended to contain food or water for a pet.
wiki.barbed wire: Barbed wire is a type of steel fencing wire constructed with sharp edges or points arranged at intervals along the strands.
wiki.star of david: A six-pointed star ✡️ recognized as a symbol of Judaism and Jewish identity, as well as mysticism and occultism. Its shape consists of two interlocking equilateral triangles.
wiki.kikumon: (For the Japanese slang word with the same pronunciation see anus.)
wiki.portal (object): A gateway connecting two distant points in space through magical or technological means.
wiki.spray can: A pressurized can with a nozzle that releases its liquid contents as a fine mist when depressed.
wiki.gathers: Sewing consisting of small folds or puckers made by pulling tight a thread in a line of stitching.
wiki.eldritch abomination: A type of monster defined by their complete disregard for the natural laws of the universe as we understand them and oftentimes the love for body horror. Their physical form (if they even have one) is so bizarre, it even can make someone mad just by looking at it.
wiki.red oni: An oni with red skin, or occasionally with some other form of red color scheme. Often depicted alongside a blue oni, typically with humorously contrasting personalities. In such cases, the red oni tends to be more hot-blooded, while the blue oni tends to be cooler and more cynical.
wiki.saddle: A saddle is a seat placed on the back of a vehicle or an animal, especially a horse, for the rider to sit on with comfort.
wiki.papers: Lots of pieces of loose paper (usually scattered everywhere).
wiki.war: An organized, armed, and, often, a prolonged conflict that is carried on between states, nations, or armed political organization using armies and soldiers. Typically to either resolve diplomatic or political disputes or as an aggressive diplomatic tool against other countries.
wiki.racecar: A car made for racing, usually featuring many sponsor logos and advertising on the chassis.
wiki.breast padding: Padding designed to fit inside a bra or other clothing to enhance the appearance of the breasts. Also known as falsies, jellies or bust enhancements.
wiki.rocket: A rocket engine used by a spacecraft or in another non-military context.
wiki.drum (container): A large cylindrical container for storing and transporting fluids or bulk goods. Best known for being used to store and transport crude oil. Generally made of metal; plastic versions also exist that are visually similar. For barrels made of wood, see barrel.
wiki.hologram: A 3D solid image projected in space.
wiki.miku day: Works created to celebrate Vocaloid Hatsune Miku on March 9th (3/9). Often includes a reference to the date somewhere in the image.
wiki.electric plug: The end of an electrical cable that plugs into and draws power from an electrical outlet.
wiki.lattice: The ornamental, usually wooden, panels often found in Chinese windows and furnishings, like those in the backgrounds of post #1786314 and post #1818178.
wiki.brick: A small rectangular block typically made of fired or sun-dried clay, stone or concrete. Used for building structures or pavements.
wiki.year of the rat: The Year of the Rat is the first in the Chinese zodiac cycle. Birth years include 1924, 1936, 1948, 1960, 1972, 1984, 1996, 2008, 2020.
wiki.ink tank (splatoon): A cylinder made of clear plastic, with green parts on the top and bottom to store the ink and allow the Inkling player character / Octoling player character to wear it.
wiki.no eyepatch: A character who usually wears an eyepatch is not wearing it.
wiki.tools: Items that are commonly used to assist in working on a project. Some of them can be used as makeshift weapons.
wiki.diamond (gemstone): A type of precious crystal gemstone known for its hardness.
wiki.nata (tool): A usually double-handed striking tool with a sharp rectangular blade used to cut and split wood. It resembles an oversized cleaver.
wiki.chalice: A metal cup with a footed stem and a round bowl.
wiki.electrical outlet: A socket, typically placed in a wall, into which electric plugs are fitted to power electrical devices.
wiki.winding key: A key that is used to operate some toys. The key is turned to wind up a spring that powers the device.
wiki.checkered flag: A flag that has a checkered pattern.
wiki.cd: A Compact Disc (CD) is an optical disc used to store digital data, originally developed for storing digital audio.
wiki.maid day: A day in which artists celebrate maids, held on May 10th of every year.
wiki.potara earrings: A set of earrings worn by Kaioushin such as the East Kaioushin and Zamasu, and can be used for the purposes of Potara fusion if two characters wear each earring on opposite ears, resulting in beings such as Kibitoshin and Vegetto, fusing even their clothes.
wiki.rising sun flag: The flag of the former Imperial Japanese Army and Navy and the current naval ensign of Japan, still used in the Japan Maritime Self-Defense Force. It has a red sun with sixteen rays on a white field, with the sun being off-center to the left in the naval ensign version.
wiki.infinity symbol: The ∞ symbol, used to represent the concept of infinity. The symbol looks like a sideways number 8, or two interconnecting loops.
