wiki.christmas present: A gift decorated with ribbons and usually topped with a bow, specific to a Christmas setting.
wiki.survey corps (emblem): The emblem of Shingeki No Kyojin's Survey Corps; a group of explorers that venture beyond the safety of the walls, and suffer a high mortality rate as a result. Many, if not most, of the series' characters belong to it. Generally found emblazoned on the sleeves and back of the characters' uniforms.
wiki.cartoon bone: A cartoonish depiction of a bone: 🦴. Usually a femur bone with two large heads.
wiki.onbashira: Yasaka Kanako's logs. The Onbashira are sacred logs that are used, after being cut using special ceremonial tools, in renewal of the Suwa Grand Shrine that occurs every six years, the ceremony which has gone uninterrupted for 1200 years. There are used in two festivals, Yamadashi and Satobiki.
wiki.roundel: A circular symbol typically consisting of concentric rings of different colors, commonly used in heraldry and in military aircraft insignia.
wiki.radiation symbol: A symbol used to warn people of the presence of radiation. It is a trefoil around a small inner circle.
wiki.wallpaper (object): Paper that is pasted in vertical strips over the walls of a room to provide a decorative or textured surface.
wiki.paper stack: A stack of individual pieces of paper. May be held or resting on a surface.
wiki.kinchaku: A cloth drawstring pouch, sometimes with a wicker bottom, worn with and often matching a kimono or yukata. Common summer festival accoutrement.
wiki.st. gloriana's (emblem): Emblem from the series Girls und Panzer signifying the St. Gloriana Girls Academy team.
wiki.nib pen (object): A pen that uses a nib to write with liquid ink. Quill pens are considered visually distinct and have their own tag.
wiki.kotoyoro: Short for kotoshi mo yoroshiku onegai shimasu, the second part of traditional New Year's greetings, comes after akeome. It's somewhat difficult to translate into English, meaning roughly "this year we hope for your support/good relationships as well".
wiki.bunny day: Bunny Day is a date pun that occurs on August 2nd or 21st.
wiki.poke ball theme: Something that is not a Poké Ball, but either ressembles one or is decorated with drawings of one or more Poké Balls.
wiki.maneki-neko: A cat figurine, often with a raised paw, displayed on the entrance of shops, restaurants and similar venues.
wiki.shared speech bubble: A speech bubble with two or more pointed ends indicating that multiple characters are saying the same thing at the same time.
wiki.zodiac: The zodiac is the "band" of the night sky roughly corresponding to the solar system's ecliptic plane. Western astrologers divide it into twelve signs, named for the constellation that is nearest the position of the Sun for one-twelfth of the year.
wiki.koishi day: A date pun celebrating Komeiji Koishi from Touhou. The 14th of May is considered Koishi day because the numbers 5-14 can be read as go-i-shi [五一四] (ko-i-shi).
wiki.omikuji: Random fortunes written on strips of paper at Shinto shrines in Japan. Tying these strips of paper to trees or wires is a common custom, especially when receiving a negative fortune.
wiki.paper crane: A common origami model based on the long necked bird, the crane_(animal).
wiki.peace symbol: The ☮ symbol, commonly known as the peace symbol.
wiki.hole: A hole or pit in the ground; an opening in or through a solid body.
wiki.army: A large group of soldiers or other combatants. May also refer to a specific branch of many nations' armed forces (primarily ground forces).
wiki.joestar birthmark: A signature star-shaped birthmark found near the necks of the Joestar bloodline's members, the protagonists of Jojo no Kimyou na Bouken.
wiki.ultra ball: A type of Poké Ball. Its top is black with a yellow "H" across it. Has a better catch rate than a Great Ball.
wiki.crt: A CRT (cathode-ray tube) is a display technology used in televisions and computer monitors, before LCDs and plasma displays replaced them. Characteristically fat and boxy.
wiki.kamisato clan (emblem): Emblem of the Kamisato clan from Genshin Impact.
wiki.grave: A site on the ground where one's dead body is buried. This is usually signified by a marker, such as cross or a tombstone mentioning the dead person's name.
wiki.license plate: A sign affixed to a vehicle displaying a series of letters or numbers indicating that the vehicle has been registered with the state.
wiki.shoulder blush: When a character's shoulders appears to be blushing.
wiki.white day: A holiday celebrated on March 14th, one month after Valentine's Day, where men give gifts to women who gave them gifts on Valentine's Day.
wiki.searchlight: An extremely bright outdoor spotlight. Originally used to search for enemy aircraft or escaped detainees at night, hence the name. They were later used for decorative purposes.
wiki.multiple torii: A row of multiple torii, often forming a tunnel at the entrance to a shrine.
wiki.blood bag: A small bag full of blood, which has been collected from the patient or from a blood donor in order to replace that patient's blood should there be a lot of blood loss during surgery, or from exsanguination due to a critical injury.
wiki.themed object: An object that looks like something it is not, for example a guitar that looks like a leek, a pillow that looks like a banana, or a purse that looks like a dog.
wiki.rayman limbs: When a character's hands or feet float around them as opposed to being physically attached via arms or legs. Rayman is one of the most iconic characters with this trait, hence the tag's name.
wiki.trigram: Eight diagrams used in Taoist cosmology to represent the fundamental principles of reality, seen as a range of eight interrelated concepts. Each consists of three lines, each line either "broken" or "unbroken," representing yin or yang, respectively.
wiki.team 9 (touhou): A group of Touhou characters commonly thought of as weak, childish, and plot-irrelevant. Named after the chief member, Cirno, who takes the moniker ⑨. Often drawn together doing childish things, or as students in Kamishirasawa Keine's classroom.
wiki.net: Thread or cord worked into an open meshed fabric.
wiki.pelt: The skin and fur of a dead animal, or the skin with the fur removed.
wiki.hishaku: A cylindrical wooden ladle used for temizu at temizuya, during tea ceremonies, to sprinkle the ground in summer (uchimizu), or by funayūrei in Japanese mythology. For ladles used for cooking, see ladle.
wiki.wet towel: A towel that has been drenched in water. Usually the character is wearing a wet towel, and it has become partially transparent to show what's underneath.
wiki.on head: A character, creature, or other living thing atop someone's head.
wiki.stripper pole: A type of pole that strippers use for pole dancing at a strip club.
wiki.on person: When a part of someone's body is resting on another person.
wiki.on motorcycle: Riding, sitting, or resting on a motorcycle. The motorcycle may be stationary or being driven.
wiki.on car: Riding, sitting, standing or resting on a car. The car may be still or being driven. The character must sit on either the hood, the trunk or the roof. This tag should not be used if the character is sitting inside the car.
wiki.on stool: Someone is on a stool, regardless if they're sitting, squatting, standing, lying and such.
wiki.on railing: Standing, climbing, lying, or sitting on a railing. In cases of sitting the character's entire buttocks should be positioned on the railing; if they're merely leaning on it use against railing instead.
wiki.leaf on head: When a leaf is on a character's head. Often associated with foxes and tanuki.
wiki.planted: An object that is stabbed into the ground so that it stands upright. For example, a sword planted in the ground.
wiki.clover: Any plants in the genus Trifolium, usually with leaves of three leaflets and flowers that have spiked petals.
wiki.thorns: A stiff, sharp-pointed, straight or curved woody projection on the stem or other part of a plant.
wiki.four-leaf clover: An extremely rare mutation of a three-leaf clover believed to bring good luck.
wiki.holly: An evergreen plant of the genus Ilex with shiny red berry and prickly leaves. It is traditionally used for making Christmas decorations and as an ornamental.
wiki.bud: The first sproutings of a flower or plant.
wiki.foliage: Plants and trees growing in nature, especially when indistinct enough that individual bushes, trees, or plants aren't prominently visible.
wiki.cactus: A family of plants native to the arid regions of the New World and which are mostly succulent plants with thick, fleshy stems that typically bears spines, lacks leaves, and has brilliantly colored flowers. They are now cultivated around the world, especially as houseplants.
wiki.flower over eye: When one of the character's eyes is covered by a flower.
wiki.flower on head: A flower literally growing from the top of a character's head, usually with a stem and a set of leaves. The Pikmin (creature)s from the Pikmin (series) series are examples of this tag.
wiki.grey flower: A flower that is colored grey.
wiki.peony (flower): An ornamental and medicinal plant known for its showy flowers, often scented. The plant itself comes in herbaceous, treelike, and hybrid forms.
wiki.wheat: One of the major staple foods of the world, alongside rice, corn, potatoes, and barley. The single most grown and traded food on the planet, almost every culture consumes wheat in some form. Most commonly prepared into flour before being baked into various breads.
wiki.anemone (flower): A genus of buttercup (flower) that grows from tubers, producing red, yellow, white or violet flowers.
wiki.acorn: The nut (food) of the oak tree.
wiki.plant roots: Roots of a tree or plant.
wiki.roots: Roots of a tree or plant.
wiki.brown flower: A flower that is colored brown.
wiki.sheath: A container for a sword, knife, axe, or other edged weapon. If it's for a sword, it's called a scabbard. If it's for a knife or dagger, it's a knife sheath.
wiki.sheathed: When a sword, dagger, etc. is held within a sheath or scabbard, usually on the hip or back, rather than unsheathed and ready to use.
wiki.cannon: A cannon is any mounted, tubular piece of artillery with 20 mm or more in caliber, that uses gunpowder or other usually explosive-based propellant to launch a projectile.
wiki.assault rifle: An infantry rifle designed for combat, with selective fire capability. The German StG44 was the very first mass-produced assault rifle ever designed and introduced in battle.
wiki.scythe: A traditional long handled agricultural tool used to harvest whole plants, such as hemp or wheat. Commonly depicted as a weapon of choice used by the Grim Reaper as a tool to reap souls, or by other mythological beings.
wiki.dagger: A double-edged knife used for stabbing or thrusting. They are often a secondary defense weapon in close combat.
wiki.scabbard: A sheath for long bladed weapons, such as swords or bayonets. See sheath for other types of weapons, such as knives and axes.
wiki.huge weapon: A very large weapon, generally at least as large as the character wielding it.
wiki.submachine gun: A carbine-length, pistol-caliber firearm that is capable of fully automatic fire. Early SMGs such as the MP18 have rifle-like appearance. While more modern models do have features like a folding stock, a pistol grip and a fire selector. The term "submachine gun" (SMG) was coined by John T.
wiki.torpedo: A self-propelled weapon with an explosive warhead, launched above or below the water surface, propelled underwater towards a target, and designed to detonate either on contact with its target or in proximity to it.
wiki.tank: An armored, tracked military vehicle with a cannon mounted in a tank turret. Most tanks have a single cannon, but some may have mounted machine guns, more than one cannon, or a hull-mounted cannon instead of a turret.
wiki.sniper rifle: A high-precision rifle designed to accurately engage targets at long range, equipped with a telescopic sight most of the time. Most modern sniper rifles feature a buttstock with adjustable length and cheekpiece position, as well as a (detachable) bipod for stability.
wiki.explosive: Any type of material designed to explode, including (but not limited to) weapons such as grenades, mines, and bombs.
wiki.whip: An instrument with a handle and a long rope-like lash used for striking or making a cracking sound. It can be used for various purposes, including as a tool for directing animals, as a weapon, or as a fetish implement in BDSM.
wiki.water gun: A type of toy gun that is designed to shoot water, though other liquids are occasionally also used in them. Most are shaped like a gun, but other shapes exist as well (such as tube or hose shape).
wiki.revolver: A gun that has a single barrel and a rotating cylinder that contains multiple rounds (usually five or six). The cylinder revolves as the weapon fires.
wiki.machine gun: A firearm designed for sustained automatic fire. Machine guns are distinguished from assault rifles and battle rifles by size and ammunition capacity. Machine guns are divided into three categories: • Light machine gun: Fires intermediate-power cartridges (except earlier and World War II-era designs like the Bren).
wiki.planted sword: A sword whose pointed end is visibly planted on or in the ground. Commonly seen with the hands on hilt pose.
wiki.energy sword: A sword with a blade made of some sort of energy instead of a physical blade.
wiki.beam saber: A sword with a blade made of some sort of energy instead of a physical blade.
wiki.unsheathed: A sword, a dagger, a knife or other similar weapon that is outside its sheath. The sheath should be present in the image.
wiki.bullet: A projectile fired from a gun. Technically, most modern bullets are released from a cartridge, which contain a shell casing, a primer, gunpowder, and then the bullet itself.
wiki.bolt action: A type of firearm mechanism in which the shooter has to manually cycle the action to chamber a new round for each time they need to shoot, by directly moving the bolt via a bolt handle (also known as a cocking handle).
wiki.shotgun: A smoothbore gun that fires shells containing pellets, rifled slugs, or other munitions.
wiki.rapier: A long and slender, yet sharp-tipped sword used in thrusting attacks. It usually has a complex hilt which provides protection for the hand of the person who wields it.
wiki.kunai: A Japanese weapon possibly derived from the masonry trowel. It's a multi-functional weapon that can be used for slashing, stabbing, throwing, and other various uses. It is commonly associated with the ninja.
wiki.lance: A type of polearm, traditionally used by cavalry or in jousting, which has a distinct and large cone for its head intended to maximize the thrusting power on impact. The cone can be as long as, or even longer, than the actual haft. Lances are a popular symbol for a knight.
wiki.magazine (weapon): A device used for storing ammunition and feeding it into a repeating firearm. May be referred to as a "mag" for short. Found in internal as well as external types, the most common is the detachable box magazine, such as that used by most modern assault rifles and semi-automatic handguns.
wiki.energy gun: A weapon that fires energy beams, lasers, plasma, or other types of directed energy, instead of projectiles.
wiki.scope: A common term for a telescopic sight, an optical sighting device for long-range aiming attached to weapons (usually a sniper rifle). Long and tubular in shape, they have crosshairs on the eyepiece lens.
wiki.riding crop: A short, semi-rigid whip without a lash. Normally used for horseback riding, but nowadays more often associated with BDSM.
wiki.laevatein (touhou): The legendary wand (or sometimes sword) of Loki_(mythology) from Norse mythology. Flandre Scarlet of the Touhou series incorporates this into one of her spell card attacks in Embodiment of Scarlet Devil, where she turns laevatein into a giant flaming sword.
wiki.grenade: A small explosive bomb thrown by hand.
wiki.ammunition: Any manufactured material fired from a gun or other similar ranged weapon systems. Generally consists of a projectile (i.e. bullet) and shell casing containing the propellant.
wiki.bullpup: A type of non-handgun firearm configuration where the action is located behind the trigger group/housing and alongside the shooter's face, instead of in front as in conventional designs. This permits the weapon to be shorter for the same barrel length, improving maneuverability and reducing weight.
wiki.shell casing: An empty, spent ammunition casing or shotgun shell.
wiki.chainsaw: A portable mechanical, motorized saw. It is used to fell trees and remove branches and foliage. It's frequently seen as a weapon in horror films, often inflicting extremely bloody wounds and severing limbs.
wiki.gae bolg (fate): Barbed Spear that Pierces with Death
wiki.rod of remorse: A ritual baton used by Enma (mythology) to carry out Judgments of Death upon the deceased who traverse the Higan and cross the Sanzu River, where no living being can go.
wiki.club (weapon): A heavy stick intended for use as a weapon.
wiki.caterpillar tracks: A continuous track running between drive wheels, intended to give the vehicle greater off-road capability. Commonly used on on tanks, half-tracks, as well as some bulldozers, excavators and farm tractors.
wiki.short sword: A sword with a short blade, short enough to be held one-handed, but longer than a knife or dagger.
wiki.sword of hisou: Hinanawi Tenshi's weapon of choice. It has the ability to shape shift and find any enemy's weaknesses, no matter how powerful or well defended the enemy may be.
wiki.rocket launcher: A man-portable weapon that fires a rocket-propelled projectile at a target. This tag is a catch-all term for any types of them, including multishot rocket launchers, man-portable air-defense systems (MANPADs), anti-tank systems, and more. Because missiles they fire are considered as guided rockets.
wiki.shuriken: A shuriken, commonly known as "throwing stars", is a traditional Japanese concealed weapon that was generally for throwing, and sometimes stabbing or slashing.
wiki.greatsword: A large two-handed sword, usually with a very long or wide double-edged blade.
wiki.multiple weapons: A character carrying several different kinds of weapons, or more than two of the same type of weapon, or a large number of weapons in general.
wiki.anti-materiel rifle: A rifle that can be used against targets other than humans, such as parked aircraft, soft-skinned or lightly-armored vehicles, ammunition dumps, and the like. Usually has caliber of 12.7mm (.50) or larger.
wiki.beam rifle: A mecha-sized energy rifle originating in the Gundam universe, first appearing in Mobile Suit Gundam.
wiki.mini-hakkero: A small octogonal box with magical symbols (bagua) engraved on it, carried by Kirisame Marisa in Touhou. It's primarily used to unleash her infamous Master Spark spell card attack, and was crafted by Morichika Rinnosuke.
wiki.bomb: A type of explosive weapon. Typically small, spherical, and set off by fuse, but there are many, many variations.
wiki.suppressor: A firearm accessory designed to minimize audible report and muzzle flash. A suppressor basically consists of a tube that may screw or latch onto the end of a gun barrel and is filled with baffles that allow air otherwise pushed out the front of the gun to slow down and expand.
wiki.gatling gun: A type of heavy machine gun with multiple rotating barrels.
wiki.claw (weapon): A weapon consisting of sharp blades attached to the back of the hand or forearm to form a "claw".
wiki.missile: A long-range explosive military weapon propelled by a engine. See rocket for non-weapon civilian rockets.
wiki.mage staff: An ornate staff often carried by magic users, and used as focusing implement for casting spells. Often decorated with gems, crystals and metal bands; or is carved from gnarled wood with knobbly/curly projections at the end. Sometimes both.
wiki.crossbow: A weapon consisting of a bow (weapon) mounted on a stock that shoots crossbow bolts.
wiki.multiple swords: A character carrying more than one sword, or multiple swords being present.
wiki.scissor blade (kill la kill): Matoi Ryuuko's primary weapon in Kill la Kill. She wields one half of a red pair of scissors capable of cutting apart Goku Uniforms. The Scissor Blade can shrink into a regular-sized scissor half, or morph itself via mechanical joints into a much larger version that Ryuuko uses to fight, which she calls Decapitation Mo…
wiki.mace: A melee weapon that uses a heavy head on the end of a handle to deliver powerful blows.
wiki.gun sling: A strap attached to a gun used to carry it on the body.
wiki.naginata: A Japanese weapon composed of a long pole and a curved blade at the end. It is similar to the Chinese guan dao or the European glaive (polearm). Commonly used by and associated with women due to their relative ease of use, and widespread usage by women militias during the Sengoku period
wiki.battle axe: Any axe specifically designed for combat. Historical battle axes tend to have sharper, thinner and lighter heads than their wood-cutting counterparts, as they're designed to chop human limbs rather than tree limbs. Oversized fantasy examples also fall under this tag.
wiki.arm blade: A blade attached to the arm. If the character's hand itself is a blade, use blade arm.
wiki.spear the gungnir: The name of one of Remilia Scarlet's spell cards, named after the mythological spear of Odin (mythology). Usually appears as a large red spear, made of demonic energy, blood, or fire.
wiki.wooden sword: A sword that consists of wood.
wiki.halberd: A polearm with a head consisting of an axe blade, a spearhead, and a hook or angled spike opposite the axe.
wiki.kitchen knife: A type of knife used for preparing food. Also known as a chef's knife or a butcher knife.
wiki.master sword: The Master Sword, also known as the "Blade of Evil's Bane" is Link's iconic weapon in The Legend of Zelda series.
wiki.alternate weapon: When a character is shown using a weapon other than their signature one. This also includes alternate weapons said character has used officially.
wiki.kanabou: A traditional Japanese spiked club. Also known as tetsubou (鉄棒). Typically made of heavy oak wood and studded with iron spikes, later versions were sheathed in iron or even made of solid iron.
wiki.sorcerer's sutra scroll: Hijiri Byakuren's magical accessory. It's a colorful scroll with sutras written on it, said to be able to chant them on its own. Only Byakuren is able to handle it.
wiki.flaming weapon: A weapon ablaze with flame, or made entirely out of fire.
wiki.ootachi: A type of Japanese sword. The ootachi (also known as "nodachi") is essentially a very long katana, often longer than the wielder's height. The best-known examples are probably Sephiroth's Masamune (ff7) in Final Fantasy VII and the various long sword-class weapons featured in the Monster Hunter (series) series.
wiki.excalibur morgan (fate): A black and red version of Excalibur (fate/stay night) used by Saber Alter.
wiki.lord camelot (fate): Mash Kyrielight's [spoilers]and by extension Galahad (fate)'s[/spoilers] large black shield, made from the Round Table of Camelot where the Knights of the Round Table (fate) would sit. It is capable of repelling attacks, so long as the user's willpower doesn't falter.
wiki.adapted turret: A specific type of gun that is formed from a naval gun turret (and sometimes part of the rigging) belonging to (usually) a shipgirl. The resulting weapon is very clearly some kind of gun, and not simply a held turret.
wiki.battle rifle: A rifle that uses full-power ammunition (e.g. 7.62×51mm NATO), capable of semi and full auto fire, and fed by removable magazines. They were the connecting link between early semi-automatic rifles (SVT-40, Gewehr 43) and assault rifles.
wiki.optical sight: Sighting device on weapons that use optics with aligned aiming point or pattern (such as reticle or red dot) superimposed onto the target image. Some firearm designs such as the Steyr AUG and G36 feature an integrated optical sight.
wiki.bo staff: A long staff used as a martial arts weapon to strike and block opponents.
wiki.antique firearm: Guns that have an old style appearance, particularly a body shape resembling early 19th century or older firearms.
wiki.wakizashi: A traditional Japanese short sword with a blade between 30 and 60 centimeters (12 and 24 in), with an average of 50 cm (20 in). It is similar to but shorter than a katana, and usually shorter than the kodachi ("small sword"). It was often paired with the katana, and used as a backup or auxiliary weapon.
wiki.light machine gun: A type of machine gun designed to be operated by a single person, with or without an assistant.
wiki.glaive (polearm): A European polearm weapon, consisting of a single-edged blade on the end of a pole. It is similar to the Japanese naginata and the Chinese guan dao.
wiki.shinai: A kendo practice sword made of four bamboo slats, held together with white leather fittings at the handle, the tip, and around 3/4ths up the length of the "blade".
wiki.buster sword: Cloud Strife's huge sword in Final Fantasy VII.
wiki.broken weapon: Any type of weapon that has been broken.
wiki.pickaxe: A tool with a hard, curved steel head attached perpendicular to a wooden or steel handle. It is mainly used in mining for breaking up hard rock.
wiki.smoking barrel: A recently shot firearm. The smoke emerging from the barrel is from the gunpowder which, upon combustion, propelled the bullet out of the gun.
wiki.smoking gun: A recently shot firearm. The smoke emerging from the barrel is from the gunpowder which, upon combustion, propelled the bullet out of the gun.
wiki.bayonet: A knife, dagger, or spike-shaped weapon designed to fit on the end of a gun muzzle, allowing it to be used for melee attack or ceremonial purpose.
wiki.musou isshin (genshin impact): An unobtainable sword from Genshin Impact that was originally created by Makoto (genshin impact) and is currently used by the Raiden Shogun. It's name translates to "Wholehearted Dream" in English.
wiki.tantou: A single or double-edged short sword or dagger carried by samurai in Japan or by noblewomen for self-defense. The sides of the blade are nearly flat.
wiki.lightsaber: An energy sword from the Star Wars series, most often wielded by the honorable Jedi knights and their mortal enemies, the evil Sith.
wiki.cleaver: A single-handed butcher's knife with a square blade resembling a small nata (tool).
wiki.flaming sword: A sword that is either made of flame or that is giving off flames.
wiki.saber (weapon): A curved, heavy-bladed, single-edged sword with a large handguard used mainly by cavalrymen and officers.
wiki.foregrip: A protruding part located on the front of a gun, meant to be grasped for stability and easier control.
wiki.boxcutter: A knife, also known as a utility knife, with a replaceable blade used for cutting open boxes.
wiki.grenade launcher: A grenade launcher is a weapon that launches a grenade further and more accurately than a soldier could. There are those designed to be attached to long arms and those that are used as standalone weapons. Automatic grenade launchers also exist. These are usually crew-served or mounted on vehicles.
wiki.kaleidostick: In Fate/Kaleid Liner Prisma Illya, a Kaleidostick is a magical device that enables its user to become a magical girl. Magical Ruby and Magical Sapphire are Kaleidosticks that Illyasviel von Einzbern and Miyu Edelfelt use to transform.
wiki.pump action: A repeating gun action that is operated by manually pumping a sliding handguard on the gun's forestock. When shooting, the sliding forend is pulled rearward to eject the expended shell casing and typically to cock the hammer/striker, and then pushed forward to load a new cartridge into the chamber.
wiki.energy cannon: A cannon that fires energy instead of shells. Frequent in most science fiction media.
wiki.tonfa: A baton (weapon) with a T-shaped handle, from which the modern side-handled police baton is derived. Often dual wielded in pairs.
wiki.bokken: A lethal kendo practice sword made of solid, heavy wood. It's shaped and balanced like a katana.
wiki.weapon case: A type of portable case designed to safely store, carry and transport weapons (including the accessories) in concealed manner. It comes in various colours and shape, though rectangular is the most common one - as well as being made from various material (e.g. fabric, leather, or plastic).
wiki.jeweled branch of hourai: An accessory of Houraisan Kaguya and one of her Five Impossible Requests from her source legend. Appears as a tree branch with colorful bobbles on it.
wiki.missile pod: A missile launcher system used in modern military vehicles to stock and fire those weapons.
wiki.falchion (fire emblem): A legendary sword wielded by Marth in the Fire Emblem series. It was created from the fang of the divine dragon, Naga. It's also wielded by Chrom and Lucina.
wiki.shotgun shell: Ammunition for a shotgun, also known as a shotshell. Tubular in shape and with a brass base, the shell is often made of plastic of various colors, most often red. It can contain various types of projectiles, such as pellets that spread out against close range targets, or solid slug.
wiki.splattershot (splatoon): A shooter-class main weapon from Splatoon (series) that resembles a water gun.
wiki.knife sheath: The sheath for a knife, common among soldiers and hunters. May also be used for other short blades such as daggers, machetes, etc.
wiki.gunblade: A revolver/sword hybrid weapon from science fiction and fantasy. Notable examples include Squall Leonhart's gunblade in Final Fantasy VIII and Lightning Farron's gunblade in Final Fantasy XIII.
wiki.weapon: A tool or object designed to hurt, maim or kill a person/an animal, as well as to destroy objects or vehicles.
wiki.snout: The protruding portion of an animal's face, consisting of its nose, mouth, and jaw. In many animals, the equivalent structure is called a muzzle, rostrum, or proboscis.
wiki.flexible: A character making a pose that requires an unusual degree of flexibility or mobility.
wiki.big belly: A stomach that is noticeably large, as if decisively full, fat, or pregnant. Commonly seen when a character has eaten a great deal of food. This tag should not be used when a character is pregnant, unless their belly is noticeably even larger than a typical pregnancy belly.
wiki.covered abs: Where the impression of the abs can be seen through opaque skin tight clothing such as one-piece swimsuit, taut clothes, bodysuits, bunnysuits, leotards, etc.
wiki.no feet: A character that naturally doesn't have normal feet; instead their legs end in a point or something similar.
wiki.notched ear: A cut in a creature's ear, may be from a past injury. Usually a triangular notch, but can also be a hole or a missing ear tip.
wiki.large hands: Hands that are larger than normal. More specifically, the hands tend to be as big as the head, or slightly bigger. This does not take into account perspective or foreshortening.
wiki.pointy nose: A large, long nose that is distinctive enough to stand out from the rest of one's facial features.
wiki.nostrils: Either of the two orifices located on the nose (or on the beak of a bird); used as a passage for air and other gases to travel the nasal passages.
wiki.large nose: A nose that is larger or more bulbous than usual.
wiki.big nose: A nose that is larger or more bulbous than usual.
wiki.pointy breasts: Breasts that point and jut forward, with a slight conical/tapered shape. Their shape under clothes is usually the result of wearing a bullet bra. Can either be perky or saggy.
wiki.multiple heads: A character with more than one head/neck, sometimes in unconventional locations, like at the end of a tail. Commonly seen on monsters and fantasy animals such as the mythical Cerberus and Hydra, or Dodrio.
wiki.multiple legs: A monster girl or mecha with more than two legs.
wiki.dorsiflexion: Flexing the foot in an upward direction, toward the shin. The opposite of plantar flexion.
wiki.greek toe: A condition in which the second toe is longer than the first (big) toe. Also known as Morton's toe or Greek foot.
wiki.long neck: A neck that is abnormally long, longer than what is anatomically feasible.
wiki.long earlobes: Earlobes that are naturally elongated, without piercings or body modification.
wiki.long nose: A character's nose is unusually long. This is typical of some folkloric portrayals, e.g., tengu.
wiki.oversized limbs: Any character designs which intentionally portray limbs disproportionally large in comparison to the rest of the body.
wiki.bishounen: Androgynous, beautiful men. Often drawn delicately with slender frames, long eyelashes, and long flowing hair. The archetypical bishounen is elegant, sensitive, emotionally intelligent, and often has a mysterious past, and may frequently be an idol or some kind of warrior. They often dress in ouji fashion.
wiki.reverse trap: Per trap, a female character who looks and may or may not act masculine. Most likely also dresses like a male, although unlike mere crossdressing the character is assumed by others to be male until demonstrated otherwise.
wiki.shortstack: Literally "short" + "stacked"; a short woman who has large breasts and/or wide hips.
wiki.fake facial hair: Facial hair that is obviously not real. Females may wear fake beards or mustaches if it’s part of a disguise or costume, like Santa Claus.
wiki.sparse chest hair: When chest hair is visible only at the top or mid section of the chest.
wiki.girly boy: A boy who presents and/or acts femininely but is still obviously male. Often overlaps with bishounen and androgynous.
wiki.sparse stubble: A small amount of short, scattered facial hair, typically seen during uneven facial hair regrowth after shaving.
wiki.very long beard: A full beard that extends past roughly the level of the navel of the wearer. Use long beard instead for those that extend past the level of the shoulders.
wiki.flower-shaped pupils: When a character's pupils are shaped like a flower symbol. Not to be confused with flower in eye, where the flower pattern covers the iris of the eye.
wiki.half-closed eye: A single eye partially closed, while the other eye is fully open or closed. Also applicable if you see the half-closed eye, but the other eye is covered by something like hair, an eyepatch, a hat, or something else. It's also possible the character only has one eye.
wiki.shading eyes: Covering the eyes with one's hands or an object to block the sun.
wiki.x x: Both eyes in the shape of a literal X, to show that a character is comically dead, knocked out or just tired.
wiki.mechanical eyes: A character having one or more mechanical or cybernetic eyes.
wiki.eye trail: A glowing light trail following a character's eyes. Often used to show anger or determination. The trail can either be a straight, or flickering line (which may resemble fire).
wiki.button eyes: Eyes that are comprised of buttons, seen on dolls or hats that mimic a face.
wiki.eye of horus: An ancient Egyptian symbol, also known as the eye of wadjet, wedjat, or udjat.
wiki.cephalopod eyes: Eyes with pupils that resemble a figure eight. Unique to octopus and squid.
wiki.eyelid pull: Pulling down the lower eyelid, typically with a single finger. If done with the tongue out, it is an akanbe.
wiki.compound eyes: An eye with a meshlike appearance (photoreceptor units). Such eyes commonly found among invertebrate animals such as bugs, arachnids, crustaceans.
wiki.green sclera: When the normally white part of the eye is colored green.
wiki.solid circle pupils: Wide open, circular eyes with large, solid black, circular pupils (◉‿◉). May depict shock, creepiness, or a wide-eyed stare. Often seen in Muppo.
wiki.v-shaped eyes: For when the top part of the eyes form a downward sloping v-shape. Often used in comical situations to denote a funny type of evil or scary.
wiki.flower in eye: When a character has a flower design located in the iris of their eyes. This isn't to be confused for flower-shaped pupils.
wiki.wavy eyes: When a character's eyes are shown to be wavy circles instead of smooth ones. Can be part of the artist's style, that the character is sad or part of a "puppy-dog" ploy to get affection.
wiki.blind: A person who cannot see. Blind people are commonly depicted either with a blindfold, completely closed eyes, pitch white eyes with a lack of pupils, or even completely blank eyes.
wiki.dashed eyes: When a character has a dash through their eyes, usually due to intense pleasure.
wiki.mismatched sclera: When the sclera (the whites of the eyes) are different colors in each eye. For example, the irises would be the same color, but one eye would have white sclera while the other has a black sclera.
wiki.hollow eyes: Eyes that appear to be or are dark empty voids.
wiki.tentacle hair: Hair that is composed of tentacles. Commonly also prehensile hair, though not necessarily guaranteed.
wiki.bow-shaped hair: Hair in the shape of a bow.
wiki.hair beads: Beads that are strung together and worn as a hair ornament for decoration, or a hairpiece that keeps hair into a ponytail, twintails or similar.
wiki.steamed bun: A type of steamed, filled bun or bread-like dumpling originating in China, with regional varieties in many world cuisines. There are many variations in fillings (meat or vegetarian) and preparation (usually steamed).
wiki.baozi: A type of steamed, filled bun or bread-like dumpling originating in China, with regional varieties in many world cuisines. There are many variations in fillings (meat or vegetarian) and preparation (usually steamed).
wiki.pompadour: A hair style in which the front hair is swept up from the forehead into a high roll at the top of the head. Often exaggerated in animation to comical proportions. Popular with rockers (particularly Elvis impersonators), gang members, and other rebels.
wiki.feather hair: Hair that includes feathers which grow out of a character's head, typically seen on bird girls and bird boys.
wiki.colored bangs: Two-tone hair where the entire bangs are colored differently than the rest of the hair. Similar to split-color hair, except the split is between the front and back halves of the hair.
wiki.dyed bangs: Two-tone hair where the entire bangs are colored differently than the rest of the hair. Similar to split-color hair, except the split is between the front and back halves of the hair.
wiki.donut hair bun: A type of hair bun where the hair is rolled using a hairdressing item called a hair donut, rather than coiling hair around repeatedly as seen in the traditional odango-styled hair bun. The resulting hair bun indeed resembles a circular donut. Usually seen as double bun.
wiki.doughnut hair bun: A type of hair bun where the hair is rolled using a hairdressing item called a hair donut, rather than coiling hair around repeatedly as seen in the traditional odango-styled hair bun. The resulting hair bun indeed resembles a circular donut. Usually seen as double bun.
wiki.drill: A tool primarily used for making holes. It can also be used as a weapon.
wiki.wispy bangs: Bangs that consist of thin, wispy strands with gaps between them, resulting in a "fringe" look. A relatively popular style of bangs among Japanese women in real life.
wiki.expressive hair: Hair that expresses a character's emotions, such as excitement or depression. Signified by flapping, lowering, or (in the case of an ahoge) wilting, standing up, or forming shapes such as a heart or question mark.
wiki.sidecut: A hairstyle where one side is shaved, while the other rest of the character's hair is at standard length. Also known as Skrillex hair.
wiki.kinky hair: Hair that grows in small, tightly coiled curls - also known as coily or afro-textured hair. In real life, this hair type is common in people indigenous to areas with hot climates, especially Africa. This term usually refers to type 4 hair, but can sometimes also include type 3c hair.
wiki.ponytail with braided base: A ponytail with a braid wrapped around the base.
wiki.side part: Hair that is parted distinctly to the left or right side of the head. If it's noticeably parted from the roots, it's parted hair as well.
wiki.snake hair: Hair that is composed of snakes, snake-like, or just evocative of snakes.
wiki.bunching hair: When a character holds part of their hair up with their hands to give the appearance that they have a certain hairstyle, usually twintails.
wiki.asymmetrical sidelocks: Sidelocks that have either different lengths or thicknesses on either side. You should also use asymmetrical hair when applicable.
wiki.ears visible through hair: When a person's ears should be obscured by their hair, but are somehow not.
wiki.choppy bangs: Bangs with rough, choppy ends and large, uneven gaps between them. Found most commonly with male characters.
wiki.kishimen hair: A hairstyle with many thin, flat locks of hair. It originates from the Japanese noodle dish kishimen.
wiki.brown nails: Fingernails and/or toenails that are colored brown.
wiki.aged up: When a character is portrayed as older (physically) than they usually are. Often, this is a character who is normally a teenager or young adult being shown as a (more) mature adult or even elderly, though children being shown as teenagers is also common.
wiki.white fur: Body fur that is colored white.
wiki.skin-covered horns: Horns that have the same color as the person's skin. Commonly associated with oni.
wiki.animal nose: A human or furry character with an animal-like nose.
wiki.two tails: A character with exactly two tails. Only use this tag if both tails can clearly be seen.
wiki.old: A person who is old, typically more than 50 or 60 years old. Common signs include grey hair and wrinkled skin.
wiki.head fins: Fins protruding from the head, usually around ear level. Sometimes extending from or serving as character's ears. Seen most often on mermaids and monster girls, but may appear on other water-type creatures.
wiki.black tail: A character with a tail of black color.
wiki.prosthesis: An artificial replacement for a lost limb.
wiki.brown fur: Body fur that is colored brown.
wiki.two-tone fur: Body fur that is two-toned (comprised of only two colors).
wiki.amputee: A character missing part or all of one or more limbs.
wiki.missing limb: A character missing part or all of one or more limbs.
wiki.bird ears: Animal ears with bird-like characteristics. Note that birds in real life don't have external ears. The structures on some bird species (e.g., many types of owl) that resemble upright animal ears are just tufts of feathers.
wiki.whiskers: Thin hairs on the face that animals use for sensing.
wiki.v-fin: A V or U-shaped head attachment commonly found on Gundams and similar mobile suits, where they function as potent radio antennas or other sensory and detection equipment.
wiki.yellow fur: Body fur that is colored yellow.
wiki.black fur: Body fur that is colored black.
wiki.white feathers: Feathers that are white, don't use this tag if they are attached to wings.
wiki.blue tail: A character with a tail of blue color.
wiki.robot ears: Robotic ears that look like radio antennae or other robotic components rather than being shaped after real ears. If the ears are shaped like human or animal ears, use mechanical ears instead.
wiki.ears down: Animal ears which would normally point upward at rest but are turned into a downward posture. Generally indicative of sadness, dismay, timidity, etc.
wiki.brown tail: A character with a tail of brown color.
wiki.cat paws: A human, humanoid, kemonomimi character with cat paws for hands, or cat-themed paw gloves. Not to be used for paws of actual cats.
wiki.animal feet: Feet (shins often included) on humanoids that resemble the hindfeet of animals.
wiki.prosthetic arm: An artificial arm, typically intended to replace a missing arm.
wiki.small horns: Horns that are much smaller in size compared to typical horns, leading to them being mistaken for things such as hair ornaments or animal ears.
wiki.purple tail: Used if a character has a purple-colored tail.
wiki.non-humanoid robot: A robot that doesn't have a humanoid shape. Robot animals, pods, walker (robot) robots, spider tanks, all count.
wiki.beak: The hard, curved, or pointed part of a bird's mouth, used for various functions such as eating, grasping, and preening. Beaks may also be found in non-avian dinosaurs and some mammals.
wiki.talons: The sharp, hooked claws at the end of the toes of dromeosaurids and some predatory avians. Raptors have one talon on every toe with thumb talons being particularly big and shaped like sickles. Birds have one talon on every toe, and they may differ in overall shape, curvature and thickness.
wiki.striped tail: A tail that has a striped pattern.
wiki.large tail: A tail at least as large as the character it belongs to.
wiki.striped horns: Any type of horns with stripes of a different color or tone.
wiki.blue fur: Body fur that is colored blue.
wiki.mechanical legs: An android, cyborg, or other human-like character with mechanical legs instead of human legs.
wiki.black feathers: Feathers that are black, don't use this tag if they are attached to wings.
wiki.fluffy: A trait of being soft, light and airy. Invokes a feeling of wanting to cuddle it (e.g. animals with thick fur).
wiki.colored inner animal ears: When the inside of the ears is an unusual colour that doesn't match natural fleshy colours or the character's hair/fur.
wiki.hair horns: Hair resembling fake horns. Almost like cone hair bun, except the hair is tied a lot tighter so that they resemble horns. Can also be produced when a character's hair naturally sticks up to form a spike.
wiki.pawpads: The soft pads that cushion an animal's legs as it walks. Characteristic of digitigrades.
wiki.grey fur: Body fur that is colored grey.
wiki.skin fangs: Skin-colored fangs that are drawn as part of the outline of the mouth, as opposed to being actual teeth.
wiki.jackal ears: Characters who have animal ears based off of a jackal.
wiki.flame-tipped tail: A fire at the tip of one's tail.
wiki.turtle shell: The shell of a turtle. Should not actually be used in conjunction with turtle, only in cases with anthropomorphic characters that display it like Bowser and his relatives. Can also be used if an abandoned turtle shell is present (not on the back of a turtle).
wiki.mechanical tail: A tail that is mechanical or cybernetic in nature.
wiki.white tail: A character with a tail of white color.
wiki.mechanical horns: Horns that look mechanical or cybernetic in nature.
wiki.very long tail: A tail longer than the legs, up to the length of the full body.
wiki.grey tail: Used if a character has a grey-colored tail.
wiki.bird legs: Bird-like legs, normally featuring claws (usually talons). Covered in scales and, sometimes, feathers. A common feature of harpies and half-harpies.
wiki.cyclops: A character with a single eye in the middle of their forehead.
wiki.hooves: The tip of a toe of an ungulate mammal, strengthened by a thick keratin covering.
wiki.orange fur: Body fur that is colored orange.
wiki.multicolored fur: Body fur comprised of more than one color.
wiki.red fur: Body fur that is colored red.
wiki.multicolored horns: Horns with different colors in them.
wiki.pink fur: Body fur that is colored pink.
wiki.hair ears: Hair resembling fake animal ears. Could be the result of intense hair intakes, cone hair buns, hair flaps or pointy hair. Can be impossible hair if it looks unrealistic enough.
wiki.fangs out: When a character shows multiple fangs outside a closed mouth.
wiki.pink tail: A character with a tail of pink color.
wiki.digitigrade: A non-human character who walks on their toes rather than the sole of their foot. In real life, many animals are digitigrade, including cats, dogs, and foxes.
wiki.purple fur: Body fur that is colored purple.
wiki.neck fur: Area of thick fur around a character's neck. Commonly seen on anthropomorphic animals and monster girls.
wiki.prosthetic leg: An artificial leg, typically intended to replace a missing leg.
wiki.hair on horn: Hair is resting over a character's horns or antlers.
wiki.blue feathers: Feathers that are blue, don't use this tag if they are attached to wings.
wiki.mechanical ears: Mechanical ears shaped after real ears. For ears that look like radio antennae or other similar robotic components use robot ears instead.
wiki.snow leopard ears: Use when a character has animal ears based off a snow leopard.
wiki.red tail: A character with a tail of red color.
wiki.cetacean tail: A character with a tail of a dolphin, orca, whale or any other cetacean.
wiki.yellow tail: A character with a tail of yellow color.
wiki.monkey ears: A character has a pair of monkey ears rather than regular ears.
wiki.jaguar ears: Characters who have animal ears based off of a jaguar.
wiki.robot animal: A robot in the shape of an animal.
wiki.tapir tail: Use this tag when a character has a tapir-like tail. Most commonly featured on Doremy Sweet. → tapir, tail, Doremy Sweet, tapir ears
wiki.animal skull: The skull of an animal rather than a human. Mammalian skulls are easier to tell apart than others due to horns.
wiki.green tail: A character with a tail of green color.
wiki.arthropod limbs: A human character with the limbs of a bug, crustacean, arachnid, or other arthropod animal. Most recognizable by the separations at the joints.
wiki.green fur: Body fur that is colored green.
wiki.short tail: Stubby tails that don't extend past the thighs.
wiki.weasel ears: Characters who have animal ears based off a weasel.
wiki.crocodilian tail: Tails characteristic to the species pertaining to the order of Crocodilians. To name a few examples, this includes crocodile, alligator and caiman_(animal) tails.
wiki.orange tail: Used if a character has an orange-colored tail.
wiki.owl ears: Tufts of feathers on the top of the head of some species of owl that resemble ears. They are not the owl's actual ears, which are located on the side of their faces, adjacent to their eyes.
wiki.gills: Respiratory organ that is similar to lungs but for aquatic organisms to filter oxygen from water.
wiki.alpaca ears: Characters who have animal ears based off of an alpaca.
wiki.snow leopard tail: A character with the tail of a snow leopard.
wiki.black scales: Scales that are black in color.
wiki.large ears: Ears that are notably larger than normal.
wiki.red feathers: Feathers that are red, don't use this tag if they are attached to wings.
wiki.purple tongue: A tongue that is colored purple. If a character has their mouth open and the rest of the mouth is also purple, that can count under this tag.
wiki.otter ears: Characters who have animal ears based off of an otter.
wiki.cable tail: A mechanical tail composed of an electrical cable, usually ending in an electric plug or some other connector, or sometimes in an attached tool or weapon.
wiki.bear tail: A small and stumpy tail originating from a bear.
wiki.double amputee: A character who, often due to injury or illness, has lost part or all of two limbs. These can be any of: • An armless amputee (both arms are missing) • A legless amputee (both legs are missing) • One amputated arm, and one amputated leg
wiki.inkling: A species of humanoid cephalopods in the Splatoon (series) series that can transform into squids and back to their humanoid form at will.
wiki.octoling: A species of humanoid cephalopods in the Splatoon (series) series that can transform into octopi and back to their humanoid form at will. The player can choose from an Octoling Boy or an Octoling Girl.
wiki.fish boy: Monster Boys that have fish characteristics. Differs from a merman or mermaid in that while they can be humanoid, they have more blatantly fishy characteristics than a fish tail, such as gills, multicolored skin, scales across the body, or different fish physiology like head protrusions.
wiki.groin: The linear depressions at the bottom of the stomach, where the abdomen meets the thighs. Often shown exposed above the waistband of a lowleg garment, below the leg holes of a highleg garment, or through a pelvic curtain.
wiki.anus: The external opening of the rectum.

wiki.blonde pubic hair: Pubic hair that is colored blonde.
wiki.light areolae: Areolae that are lighter in color than the surrounding skin. Typically seen on characters with dark skin.

wiki.pussy juice drip through clothes: Pussy juice seeping through worn clothing.
wiki.dog penis: The penis of a dog. Typically knotted.
wiki.anal fluid: Liquid secreting from the anus. Not cum, but its own liquid originating from the anus itself.
wiki.pubic stubble: The stubble left behind after shaving one's pubic hair.
wiki.joints: A character with artificial arm or leg joints.
wiki.material growth: A character displaying foreign material growth on their skin, such as crystal, stone, bone, wood, etc.
wiki.bandaged hand: When a character has at least one hand wrapped in bandages.
wiki.suction cups: A suction cup like the ones found on the tentacles of cephalopods such as octopuses.
wiki.cuts: Cuts or tears to the skin caused by something sharp. A type of injury. When healed, often turns into a scar.
wiki.crossed bandaids: Two bandaids that overlap to form a cross, plus, or X. Typically used for comedic purposes.
wiki.bandaged neck: Some bandages are wrapped around a person's neck.
wiki.stitched face: When a character has stitches running across a significant portion of their face.
wiki.thick lips: Lips that are especially large or prominent, more so than ordinary lips.
wiki.red hands: Hands that are colored red, differently than the rest of the character's skin.
wiki.gauze: A piece of fabric used to cover wounds, generally on an injury too large for a bandaid.
wiki.mole under each eye: A mole under each eye. Same as mole under eye, but on both sides.
wiki.bandaid on forehead: A bandaid on a person's forehead.
wiki.cheekbones: The bone below the eyes that form the protruding part of the cheeks.
wiki.dirty feet: When the feet or soles are dirty, usually from going barefoot.
wiki.no mole: When a character that usually has a mole is depicted without one. Often (but not always) an artistic error.
wiki.ear birthmark: A birthmark located on the ear.
wiki.dirt: An earthy substance commonly found on the surface of the Earth, formed from the weathering of rocks and organic matter, that leaves things dirty upon contact.
wiki.food in mouth: Food held or hanging from the mouth, generally without using the hands to hold it.
wiki.food on face: Having particles of food on one's face. Generally a result of messy eating.
wiki.same-sex bathing: Two or more characters of the same gender sharing a bath or shower (place). Mutually exclusive with mixed-sex bathing.
wiki.biting: Using one's teeth to pierce or hold an object.
wiki.clothes in mouth: A piece of clothing being held in the mouth. Usually a type of clothes lift where the clothing is lifted by the wearer and held in their mouth.
wiki.hair tie in mouth: A person holding a hair tie (including scrunchies) in their mouth, usually while tying their hair.
wiki.food on head: Food on someone's head. If it's fruit, use fruit on head as well.
wiki.duel: A one-on-one fight between two people, as opposed to a single person fighting a large force, or two large forces clashing (as in a battle).
wiki.popsicle in mouth: A popsicle held in the mouth.
wiki.twitching: Sudden, involuntary, sharp movements in response to agitation or stimulation. Usually denoted by jagged motion lines or the moving body part having a jagged outline. May be animated without these techniques.
wiki.attack: A maneuver made with intent to inflict damage on a person, creature, or object. Can see the attack move is hitting a target, or the attack is blocked or dodged by the target.
wiki.digging your own grave: When a character does something stupid or offensive with a lack of foresight and is about to be punished for it.
wiki.attacking viewer: A character ready to attack the viewer.
wiki.incoming attack: A character ready to attack the viewer.
wiki.hairdressing: Caring for one's (or others) hair by styling, cutting, braiding, or washing.
wiki.drinking straw in mouth: Someone having a drinking straw in their mouth, usually because they're drinking from a cup.
wiki.carrying under arm: Carrying something or someone under the arm, next to the torso.
wiki.hair in own mouth: When a character is holding a lock or single strand of their own hair in their own mouth. Often used as a visual shorthand for derangement, e.g., on yandere characters, but also sometimes just used as a sign of general dishevelment.
wiki.in the face: Getting hit in the face with something: a pie in the face, a face punch, a slap, or anything else. If it's cum, use facial instead.
wiki.stab: A piercing wound caused by something sharp, such as a knife or a sword.
wiki.feral instincts: An animal-like character (such as a monster girl, furry or kemonomimi) exhibiting behavior from the animal they're based on. For example, a cat girl grooming themselves or playing with cat toys, or a dog girl playing fetch.
wiki.ribbon in mouth: When a character is holding a ribbon in their mouth.
wiki.shirt in mouth: A character holding up the shirt they're wearing with their mouth. Usually this is the bottom hem of the shirt to expose the chest and abdominal areas.
wiki.utensil in mouth: Holding a fork or spoon in one's mouth, usually while eating.
wiki.multiple riders: More than one person riding on the same object or animal.
wiki.blowing bubbles: • Blowing a soap bubble through a bubble pipe, bubble wand or similar tool. • Exhaling air while underwater to create bubbles.
wiki.bubble blowing: • Blowing a soap bubble through a bubble pipe, bubble wand or similar tool. • Exhaling air while underwater to create bubbles.
wiki.cutting hair: When one's hair gets cut off, regardless of who does the cutting or how it gets cut.
wiki.theft: Stealing or otherwise taking something from its rightful owner without permission.
wiki.slashing: The act of swinging a bladed weapon in the air, either at an opponent or to prepare for battle. This is often portrayed with an attack trail left behind in the air by the swung weapon.
wiki.shaking: Somone shaking another person or object back and forth.
wiki.spit take: A situation wherein a character spits out what they have just consumed for any reason, particularly as a reaction to what someone has said or done, usually from surprise.
wiki.flying kick: An execution of a kick while one is in midair.
wiki.stalk in mouth: When a character is chewing on a stalk of wheat, or other similar plants.
