wiki.logo parody: A modified copyright logo used to better fit the theme of the overall image or to avoid copyright infringement. A common parody is Wcdonald's with a W, compared to Mcdonald's which uses an M.
wiki.dithering: A method to create the illusion of color shading/blending through varied spacing of different-colored pixels from a limited palette.
wiki.araki hirohiko (style): Araki Hirohiko's style of drawing. Known for its serious, heavily-detailed, and glamorous look in JoJo no Kimyou na Bouken.
wiki.through medium: Someone going through or coming out of the medium they are presented in, such a coming out of a page or screen. This typically implies crossing over from a fictional world to reality.
wiki.western comics (style): Images in the style of traditional American/western comic books. (Not simply images featuring comic book characters.)
wiki.riyo (lyomsnpmp) (style): A style parody of Fate/Grand Order artist Riyo (lyomsnpmp). Chibis with big round eyes, usually completely open.
wiki.k-pop: A form of popular music originating in South Korea. K-pop commonly refers to idol groups or artists, including references to lyrics, dances, and outfits from K-pop songs and music videos.
wiki.1970s (style): Anime or manga drawn in a style that was popular in the 1970's.
wiki.ligne claire: Ligne claire (French for "clear line") is an art style characterized by strong black outlines, flat colors, and detailed backgrounds with little contrast between the subject and the background.
wiki.visual novel: A style of game that mainly consists of text (both dialogues and narrative) over a background image. Many games have the player make options that affect the outcome of the story.
wiki.crosshatching: A shading technique that uses intersecting lines of varying densities to simulate varying levels of darkness. A lightly colored object will have few lines, whereas a very dark object may have so many lines as to be solid black.
wiki.inktober: A drawing challenge, started by illustrator Jake Parker in 2009, that's held every October where artists draw one ink drawing per day of the month and post it.
wiki.black outline: An outline around a character or object that is colored black.
wiki.pink outline: An outline around a character or object that is colored pink.
wiki.bkub (style): Images that are in the style of bkub, whether it be his original style or its adapted form as seen in the Pop Team Epic anime (easily identifiable due to its pseudo-3D-like appearance).
wiki.takeuchi takashi (style): Artwork drawn in the style of Takeuchi Takashi, best known for illustrating the Fate series since its inception with Fate/Stay Night.
wiki.toriyama akira (style): Artwork done in the style of the late Toriyama Akira, a popular and legendary artist well-known for series such as Dragon Ball, Dragon Quest, Chrono Trigger, and Dr. Slump to name a few.
wiki.pinup (style): A genre of art emulating, replicating or referencing classic 1940s or 1950s style pinup posters.
wiki.yellow outline: An outline around a character or object that is colored yellow.
wiki.ishikei (style): Art style of the prolific ero artist Ishikei. Seems to be frequently copied by various other ero artists due to its popular appeal.
wiki.what: An image that is bizarre, horrific, surreal, disturbing, or that otherwise makes you say "What."
wiki.pursed lips: To bring the lips tightly together, usually as an expression of disapproval.
wiki.affectionate: Characters demonstrating mutual fond or loving feelings for each other in a context which is not romantic or sexual, primarily between family members or animals.
wiki.misunderstanding: A common device for comedy. One character incorrectly interprets the words or actions of another character. The classic example is someone walking into the room when two characters are in a compromising position.
wiki.gao: Japanese sound effect for a roar.
wiki.fingersmile: Pushing up one or both sides of one's own mouth with fingers to form a smile. Frequently associated with Yin (darker than black) from Darker Than Black and Marnie (pokemon) from Pokemon.
wiki.nyan: A sound effect used for imitating a cat's cry. The Japanese equivalent of "meow".
wiki.flying teardrops: For when teardrops appear to be flying off a person's eyes, physics be damned.
wiki.igote: A garment covering one arm (usually the left) as well as the shoulder. Traditionally used by practitioners of kyuudou to protect the arm from the bowstring.
wiki.depressed: Refers to both the mood and the mental illness.
wiki.homu: A sound effect associated with Akemi Homura from Mahou Shoujo Madoka Magica. A play off her name in a similar manner to Pokémon. Homura's nickname among Japanese fans is Homuhomu. This phrase was never used in the drama, though.
wiki.cross-eyed: When both eyes point inward, whether voluntary or involuntary. The opposite is wall-eyed.
wiki.remembering: When a character recalls a past event, typically from their own perspective. If the recollection is involuntary, use flashback.
wiki.;(: A closed mouth frown with one eye closed.
wiki.unhappy: For when a character is expressing his depression towards something.
wiki.mukyuu: A nonsensical catch-phrase attributed to Patchouli Knowledge of Touhou. It is the onomatopoeia of a groan combined with a sigh.
wiki.tantrum: An emotional episode fueled by feelings of anger, distress or refusal. Often involves screaming, crying, lying or rolling on the floor, flailing of arms, or throwing objects. There are two kinds of tantrums; the sort done by children in order to get their way, and the sort done by adults who are at their boiling point.
wiki.curious: Just interest because of desire to know or strangeness.
wiki.charisma break: When a character's normally cool or charismatic demeanor is destroyed. No meta-knowledge about the character should be required to use this tag.
wiki.iei: An iei is a portrait (object) photo (object) of a deceased person. Commonly seen in scenes during, before, or after Japanese funerals, either on display or carried by a family member.
wiki.3others: An image depicting three characters of ambiguous, indeterminate, or non-binary gender. Dolls only count if animate. Depictions of characters on paintings etc don't count unless it plays a major role in the work. If the presence of a character is only implied, it doesn't count.
wiki.6+others: An image depicting six or more characters of ambiguous, indeterminate, or non-binary gender. Dolls only count if animate. Depictions of characters on paintings etc don't count unless it plays a major role in the work. If the presence of a character is only implied, it doesn't count.
wiki.marker (medium): Art done using markers, also known as felt-tip pens, most popularly Copic markers「コピック」, but also the more generic "magic markers"「マジック」.
wiki.millipen (medium): Written as「ミリペン」, this common abbreviation of "Millimetre Pen" refers to the instrument also known as a technical pen. It has a hard tip and is known for making solid, consistent lines. In this regard, it's easier to use than a nib pen, but there's a trade-off in terms of how much control you can have over your line.
wiki.nib pen (medium): A work of traditional media drawn with a nib pen, a pen that requires constant dipping in an ink reservoir to function.
wiki.ink (medium): A medium that consists of ink which has been applied to a surface, typically paper. The ink can be applied using different tools, such as a nib pen, ballpoint pen, technical pen, marker, or brush, or through the printmaking process.
wiki.ballpoint pen (medium): Art drawn using a ballpoint pen.
wiki.watercolor pencil (medium): Written「水彩色鉛筆」, water-soluble pigments packaged as a pencil, delivering the advantages of both colored pencil and watercolor in being able to draw fine details and also to blend them with water.
wiki.calligraphy brush (medium): A piece of traditional media or faux traditional media created using a calligraphy brush and ink.
wiki.pastel (medium): Pastel is an art medium in the form of a stick consisting of pure powdered pigment and a binder.
wiki.oil painting (medium): For when the image itself is an oil on canvas painting. Not to be confused with an oil painting in the image.
wiki.acrylic paint (medium): Works that were created using acrylic paint.
wiki.mixed media: Artwork in which more than one medium or material has been employed, such as a combination of traditional media and digital (computer-based) media.
wiki.border: When a picture has a border along its sides. Most often, this is a simple solid color border on all four sides. See ornate border for more complex borders.
wiki.grey border: An image that has a grey-colored border around its edges.
wiki.pink border: An image that has a pink-colored border surrounding its edges.
wiki.red border: A post with a red border around the image.
wiki.blue border: When the outer borders of an image are colored blue.
wiki.yellow border: An image that has a yellow-colored border around its edges.
wiki.brown border: An image that has a brown-colored border around its edges.
wiki.green border: An image that has a green-colored border around its edges.
wiki.purple border: An image that has a purple-colored border around its edges.
wiki.ornate border: A border with intricate details: whether it be ornamentation along its length, geometric designs, or simply added shapes/figures. Often paired with, but not mutually inclusive to, inset border.
wiki.lace border: The outer edge of the image is bordered with lace.
wiki.inset border: A type of border that is inset in the image, noticeably separated from the edge or an additional border. Typically consists of one to two lines in a solid color; if more complex consider adding ornate border.
wiki.4koma: A continuous four-panel comic strip in a vertical, horizontal, or square format. An example is Azumanga Daioh.
wiki.1koma: A self-contained comic consisting of a single panel. A Western example is Heathcliff, or The Far Side.
wiki.5koma: A five-panel comic strip lain in a continuous vertical or horizontal format.
wiki.multiple 4koma: Two or more sets of 4koma in one image. Extra details besides the 4koma (such as a character standing beside the panels) don't count.
wiki.square 4koma: A 4koma with a 2×2 format (2 rows and 2 columns).
wiki.right-to-left comic: A non-Japanese comic that is written right-to-left (frame and balloon order, text orientation) instead of the usual left-to-right.
wiki.sequential: An image with a series of events that happen in sequential order. Unlike a normal comic, there is no clear separation of scenes into distinct panels.
wiki.inset: Pictures having other pictures (predominantly photos/portraits of characters) set into the main image.
wiki.photo inset: When a photo is embedded into the image, either as a reference or as a component of the overall image itself.
wiki.projected inset: When there is a projection of someone or something in the background of an image.
wiki.film strip: A strip of still images that can be played back on a projector to depict a moving image. Perforations in the sides of the strip allow it to be moved by a projector's mechanism. Film strips can also depict photos taken by a non-video camera.
wiki.character profile: An image that contains information about a pictured character such as their name, personality traits, likes and dislikes, etc.
wiki.expressions: Several variations of the same character doing different facial expressions and emotions. This is often in the form of an expression chart, or in a series of small portraits in a character profile showing a character's different expressions.
wiki.expression chart: A grid-like chart of multiple expressions.
wiki.variations: A character being shown in multiple variations, usually different outfits or appearances.
wiki.color guide: A palette of colors of an image shown within itself. In the context of printing, these are known as color bars and are used to measure print quality.
wiki.diagram: A type of graph that uses symbols and brief words to represent a flow of information or steps (e.g. a relationship graph).
wiki.chart: Artwork that contains organized information for easy reading, identification, and comparison. On Danbooru this usually takes the form of a tabular set of panels (e.g. expression chart), or a lineup of subjects to be compared visually (e.g. height chart)
wiki.how to: A post that gives step by step instructions on how to perform a certain action depicted in the picture. Typically, this is a drawing tutorial, but it can be any subject.
wiki.noose: A loop-shaped rope knot used to perform hanging executions or suicides.
wiki.self-harm: The act of inflicting injury on oneself, or evidence of very recent self-injury. Usually associated with depression or suicidal tendencies though not always (ex: a blood sacrifice).
wiki.seishou elementary school uniform: The school uniform worn by students of the Private Seishou University-affiliated Elementary School in the Lyrical Nanoha series.
wiki.nami junior high school uniform: Refers to the school uniforms worn by the underwater-based characters of Nagi no Asukara. They are basically serafuku in some sense for both genders.
wiki.kindergarten: Youchien (幼稚園) or Japanese Kindergarten is a form of preschool for children ages 3-6. There are both public and private kindergartens. They're all supervised by the Japanese Ministry of Education, but are not a part of the official education system.
wiki.if they mated: A non-canon child of two known characters. The child is often either a fusion of their parents or resembles an aged down but otherwise identical clone of the mother. See science babies for the children of a same-sex couple.
wiki.age regression: When a character becomes younger in-universe for whatever reason. The post should have indicators that it isn't simply a time paradox or a depiction of a character when they were younger.
wiki.lolidom: A sexual situation in which the dominant partner is the loli. The masculine equivalent would be shotadom.
wiki.mesugaki: Literally, "bitch brat". A young/small girl, usually a loli, petite, or oppai loli, who acts sassy and provocative towards people older or bigger than her (especially adults) in a sexually charged manner. The male equivalent is called "osugaki".
wiki.onee-loli: A genre consisting of pairing a younger girl with an older girl/woman in a risque, sexual or romantic fashion. The term is a portmanteau of 'onee-san' (elder sister/older woman) and 'loli' (young girl).
wiki.onii-shota: A genre consisting of pairing a younger boy with an older male in a risque, sexual or romantic fashion. A portmanteau of 'onii-san' (elder brother/older man) and 'shota' (young boy).
wiki.wheelbarrow pose: A pose taken from the wheelbarrow race, in which teams of two try to move as quickly as possible while assuming a pose reminiscent of pushing a wheelbarrow. One participant (the wheelbarrow) has their hands on the ground, while the other holds their legs up off the ground like handles.
wiki.child on child: Romantic or sexual interaction between prepubescent children. From the Japanese phrase 子供同士, translating to “children together” or “between children”.
wiki.perversion of games: A normally innocent game or sporting activity that is made sexual in some way.
wiki.hanging legs: Legs dangling limply off the ground while a character is lifted or suspended in midair.
wiki.competition: When two or more opposing sides attempt to outperform the others. Typically seen in the form an organized event, such as sports.
wiki.fighting over penis: Two characters fighting (even verbally) over control for another character's penis.
wiki.living fleshlight: When a person is used as a Fleshlight-type sex toy. This generally involves a size difference and the person being lifted in the air while they are used.
wiki.twister (game): A game of physical skill using human bodies as player pieces. The game is played on a plastic mat with blue, green, red, and yellow spots that the players must place their hands and feet upon while trying not to fall. A twister wheel is used to determine where the players must move to.
wiki.kissing another during penetration: A character kissing another while being penetrated.
wiki.kissing viewer: A character delivering a kiss to the viewer, or one appears to be forthcoming.
wiki.reverse netorare: A variant of netorare where a character steals a woman's love interest.
wiki.thigh straddling: A position where one character is straddling someone else's thigh. Often, but not always, a form of frottage.
wiki.hand wrapped around waist: A larger person holding a mini person or other smaller character with a single hand wrapped around their waist or body. A form of size difference.
wiki.unwanted creampie: Internal ejaculation that is not desired by its recipient, or someone clearly indicating that they do not wish to receive it.
wiki.forced kiss: A kiss that occurs due to physical force or coercion, either by the kisser or someone else.
wiki.hand between own legs: A character's hand(s) placed between their legs.
wiki.holding own legs back: A character holding their own legs back to their chest or beyond, folding themselves in half.
wiki.bound thighs: Both thighs are bound together with some sort of restraint.
wiki.figure four sitting: Sitting with one ankle or calf resting on the knee of the other leg.
wiki.legs bound apart: Both legs bound apart from one another by some sort of restraint, so that they can't be closed. The opposite of bound legs.
wiki.reverse squatting cowgirl position: A variation of reverse cowgirl position where the person on top rides their partner while squatting with their feet on the ground, rather than kneeling. Typically a more assertive or female-dominant position. Or a power bottom when referring to male characters.
wiki.over the knee: A position in which one person is sitting down and a second is either bent over or lying with their stomach on the first person's knees/thighs. Usually used for spanking.
wiki.footjob with footwear: Giving a footjob or female footjob while wearing shoes, boots, or sandals.
wiki.panties around thighs: Panties that have been pulled down and are hanging around the thighs.
wiki.sitting split: Performing a split while sitting or laying on the stomach. The legs may be spread to the sides, or to the front and back.
wiki.v legs: Spread legs held straight out in a V-shape, with the knees unbent.
wiki.panties around ankles: Panties that have been pulled down and are hanging around the ankles.
wiki.frontal thigh sex: Thigh sex with both partners facing each other, chest-to-chest.
wiki.legs behind head: Referring to when a character's legs are behind their head. This pose is an example of frontbending, requiring a slightly higher amount of flexibility.
wiki.holding party popper: When a character is holding a party popper.
wiki.snowball fight: A play fight using snowballs as weapons.
wiki.birthday party: A party held to commemorate the date of one's birth.
wiki.water fight: A mock battle involving water that often takes place during the summer. Water guns and water balloons are commonly used.
wiki.pillow fight: A mock fight using pillows as weapons. Pillow fights often occur during sleepovers.
wiki.holding unworn clothes: Holding any type of removed clothing. Do not use if the clothing is still being worn.
wiki.mind break: When someone is under circumstances that change how they view sex. Usually portrayed as the subject of rape coming to enjoy it.
wiki.anal only: A situation where a character either has restricted use of their vagina (such as maebari, backless panties, chastity belt, etc.); or where a character voices or shows their displeasure for vaginal sex and/or their preference for anal sex (by speech bubble, body writing, etc.).
wiki.condom left inside: When a condom remains inside an entered orifice (vagina, anus, etc.) rather than on the object to which is was applied (penis, dildo, etc.), most often after being fully used.
wiki.imminent netorare: As netorare involves infidelity in which someone close to the protagonist (usually someone's lover, though the dilution of the word has meant that it has also been applied to friends, unrequited love interests, or even relatives) is usually unwillingly seduced and stolen away, imminent netorare involves images where th…
wiki.before netorare: A post part of a comic or segmented comic showing a character's interaction with a character that they won't be having sex with before netorare occurs, specially if it's a normal interaction and they aren't aware of what is going to happen.
wiki.multicolored clothes: Clothing that prominently features two or more distinct colors. For example, a red-and-blue dress. • White, black, and grey don't count. For example, blue-and-white striped thighhighs don't count. • Multiple shades of the same color don't count. For example, a light-blue-and-dark-blue shirt doesn't count.
wiki.military combat uniform: A military uniform designed for combat, adorned with various equipment to help engage the enemy. Pouches for extra storage, vision-enhancing goggles, and armor such as bulletproof vests are all a common sight, as is a set of military fatigues underneath.
wiki.single shoulder pad: Shoulder pads worn on only one side.
wiki.shirt under shirt: Wearing a shirt over another shirt. Often seen in baseball uniforms.
wiki.blue trim: An article of clothing that has a blue trim around at least one of its edges.
wiki.green visor: Ambiguous tag. Do not use. See visor for alternatives
wiki.animal ear hood: An animal hood with adornments resembling fake animal ears.
wiki.sideless dress: A dress that exposes a large area of a character's side skin.
wiki.black wrist cuffs: Wrist cuffs that are coloured black.
wiki.two-tone scarf: Scarf which has two basic colors.
wiki.gold ring: A ring made of, or coloured, gold.
wiki.red brooch: A clasp or pin that typically has a gem attached, often secured to a piece of garment.
wiki.black shrug: A shrug that is black in color.
wiki.mouth piercing: A piercing on the lips or around the mouth.
wiki.two-tone one-piece swimsuit: A one-piece swimsuit that is additionally two-tone.
wiki.untied footwear: Lace-up boots, shoes, or sneakers that have their shoelaces undone.
wiki.two-tone thighhighs: Thighhighs that have exactly two basic colours.
wiki.purple veil: A veil that is colored purple.
wiki.blue veil: A veil that is colored blue.
wiki.ring hair ornament: A hair ornament in the shape of a ring.
wiki.bandaid on thigh: A bandaid on a person's thigh.
wiki.two-tone sweater: A specific type of multicolored sweater that features two distinctly separated colors.
wiki.two-tone necktie: A multicolored necktie that has exactly two colors.
wiki.two-sided headwear: Headwear, such as a hat, made with two-sided fabric. The inner surface or liner is a different color and/or pattern than the outer one.
wiki.emo fashion: A fashion style that was popular amongst teenagers during the 2000s.
wiki.number print: Clothing or another object with a number design printed on it. Notably on the shirt that Cover Bikini Girl (Gta Vi) wears.
wiki.chihaya (clothing): A thin, white ceremonial overgarment sometimes worn by a miko.
wiki.multiple necklaces: More than one necklace on a character's neck.
wiki.han'eri: A decorative piece of cloth worn under the neckline of a kimono to add style or color to an outfit. Recognizable by the kimono's neckline contrasting in color or design with the rest of the kimono.
wiki.white hanfu: A hanfu that is colored white.
wiki.front-hook bra: A form of front-fastening bra that opens in with a hook between the breasts.
wiki.pink trim: An article of clothing that has a pink trim around at least one of its edges.
wiki.flak jacket: A type of body armor designed to protect from from explosive weaponry such as anti-aircraft artillery ("flak" is a German contraction for Fliegerabwehrkanone, "aircraft-defense gun") or grenade fragments.
wiki.red tabard: A tabard that is red in color.
wiki.bandana around neck: A bandana worn around the neck, often with the majority of it hanging in front. Some utilize it as a mask.
wiki.muzzle (mask): A device that is placed over the snout of an animal to keep them from biting or otherwise opening their mouth.
wiki.single bare foot: When a subject is wearing footwear or legwear on one foot but is entirely barefoot on the other foot.
wiki.blue visor: Ambiguous tag. Do not use. See visor for alternatives
wiki.qixiong ruqun: Qixiong ruqun is a style of traditional Chinese clothing hanfu, consisting of a long-sleeved blouse or jacket and a high-waisted skirt that reaches just below the armpits, covering the chest. It was most popular during the Tang Dynasty (618–907 CE) and is one of the best-known ruqun variations.
wiki.pinstripe pants: Any type of pants with a pinstripe pattern, commonly seen as part of a pinstripe suit.
wiki.character charm: A charm (object) designed after a character.
wiki.black leg warmers: Leg warmers that are colored black.
wiki.black arm warmers: Arm warmers that are colored black.
wiki.aqua sleeves: A pair of sleeves that are colored aqua. The sleeves have to either be detached, or differently colored from the rest of the garment the character is wearing (such as raglan sleeves).
wiki.rerebrace: A piece of medieval knight's armor worn to protect the upper arms.
wiki.coat partially removed: When a coat is pulled down and worn off shoulder (hanging low around the arms or elbows), rather than on top of the shoulders.
wiki.unworn footwear: Deprecated tag. Use one of the tags below instead. → unworn boots, unworn shoes, unworn sandals, unworn slippers
wiki.pinstripe dress: A dress with a pinstripe pattern.
wiki.fur shawl: A shawl made of animal fur, see fur (clothing).
wiki.orange halo: A halo that is colored orange.
wiki.brazilian flag print: Clothing or an object that has printings resembling the Brazilian flag.
wiki.lace sleeves: Sleeves made out of lace, not to be confused with lace-trimmed sleeves.
wiki.gold armlet: An armlet made out of gold.
wiki.detached hood: A type of hood that is not attached to any sort of upper body clothing such as a shirt or jacket.
wiki.qi lolita: A style very similar to Wa Lolita, but instead of being inspired by traditional Japanese clothes, it is influenced by traditional Chinese clothes (e.g. qipao or hanfu), culture and other things related to the styles and influences.
wiki.middle ring: A ring that is worn on the middle finger.
wiki.animal helmet: A helmet with fake animal ears, or in the shape of an animal head.
wiki.undersized breast cup: When the breast cup of a bra or leotard is noticeably too small for the breasts and doesn't properly cover the chest.
wiki.race bib: A race bib is commonly used by athletes in sporting competitions and have numbers and/or the competitor's names on them to differentiate between them all. Race bibs can be sorted into 2 categories: • An adult sized bib that has straps going over the shoulders and around the waist • A sticker or piece of paper that is s…
wiki.pendant collar: A collar with a pendant hanging from it.
wiki.yami kawaii: Yami Kawaii (meaning "sick cute") is an aesthetic that has been bubbling out of Tokyo's streets and manifests through accessories such as fake guns, syringes, gas masks, pills, bandages and bandaids.
wiki.cross-laced cutout: Clothing with a cutout opening (for example, a cleavage cutout, navel cutout, or heart cutout), which has criss-crossing laces, strings, or ribbons.
wiki.belt chain: A short or long chain with clasps on both ends so that a wallet can be secured or fixed to a belt. As a motorcyclist, a wallet chain is an indispensable accessory.
wiki.two-tone pants: Multicolored pants that consists of exactly two colors.
wiki.stirrup footwear: Socks that have a stirrup around the sole of the foot, leaving both the toes and heel uncovered. Footwear should not get past knees, otherwise use stirrup legwear.
wiki.purple tabard: A tabard that is purple in color.
wiki.letter hair ornament: A hair ornament in the shape of a (usually Latin alphabet) letter.
wiki.aqua trim: An article of clothing that has an aqua trim around at least one of its edges.
wiki.waist ribbon: A long and thin ribbon cinching the waist.
wiki.heart-shaped gem: A gem that has been crafted into the shape of a heart.
wiki.shirt partially tucked in: When a shirt is only partially tucked in a skirt, pants or other bottomwear.
wiki.blue wrist cuffs: Wrist cuffs that are coloured blue.
wiki.vertical-striped headwear: A hat or other type of headwear with a vertical-striped pattern.
wiki.poleyn: A form of medieval knight's armor that protected the knees.
wiki.single fishnet legwear: A fishnet legwear worn in just one leg. Can be fishnet thighhighs or fishnet socks.
wiki.high-visibility clothing: Clothing designed to be highly visible for safety purposes, typically bright colors with reflective strips. Often worn by construction workers, railroad workers, police, firefighters, traffic controllers, and other people working near road traffic or in hazardous conditions.
wiki.white tunic: A tunic that is colored white.
wiki.leaf hat ornament: A hat ornament shaped like a leaf.
wiki.empire waist: A style of clothing, usually a dress, with a fit directly below the bust, giving a high-waisted appearance. This emphasizes the bust and lengthens the body's appearance.
wiki.two-tone hat: A hat that has two basic colors.
wiki.green robe: A robe that is colored green.
wiki.black bandana: A bandana that is colored black.
wiki.print pants: Pants with a motif printed on them.
wiki.checkered hairband: A hairband that has a checkered pattern.
wiki.pink sweater vest: A sweater vest that is colored pink.
wiki.sabaton: An armored shoe. A sabaton or solleret is part of a medieval knight's armor that covers the foot.
wiki.waist sash: A sash worn wrapped around the waist.
wiki.orange gemstone: A gem with an orange color.
wiki.yellow capelet: A capelet that is colored yellow.
wiki.cross-laced bikini: A bikini top with criss-crossing laces, strings, or ribbons.
wiki.high-visibility vest: A brightly-colored (usually yellow) vest worn to make a person more noticeable, often for safety purposes such as visibility in traffic.
wiki.aristocratic clothes: Clothing that was either commonly found to be worn in the early modern period in Europe (ex. Victorian clothes), or inspired by it in works of fiction.
wiki.yellow headband: A headband that is colored yellow.
wiki.purple bag: A bag that is colored purple.
wiki.leggings under shorts: Leggings that are underneath shorts of any kind.
wiki.compression shirt: A type of skin tight shirt commonly used by athletes. The shirt is designed to put pressure against the body, supporting the muscles and absorbing sweat to prevent chafing.
wiki.camera around neck: A camera hanging from the neck by wearing a rope attached to it.
wiki.eye print: Clothing or a fabric item that has the printed design of an open eye.
wiki.rosary: A type of prayer beads with a cross attached to the bottom. It is used as the part of a meditation ritual where the user prays to Jesus Christ and the Virgin Mary.
wiki.military dress uniform: A type of formal military uniform designed for parade and ceremonial use. They usually have more distinctive designs, that show various insignias and other decorations or awards like medals or ribbon bars.
wiki.o-ring harness: A harness that features an o-ring as part of its design.
wiki.white arm warmers: Arm warmers that are colored white.
wiki.purple tank top: A tank top that is colored purple.
wiki.gem hair ornament: A hair ornament or hairclip shaped like a gem.
wiki.broken mask: A mask that is broken or cracked. Also tag half mask and half eye mask when applied.
wiki.grey camisole: A camisole that is colored grey.
wiki.grape hair ornament: A hair ornament that looks like either an individual grape or a bunch.
wiki.tooth earrings: Earrings that are a tooth, or at least designed to resemble one. Do not add tooth unless there is a clear focus on the earrings.
wiki.torn socks: Socks or kneehighs that are torn.
wiki.floating neckwear: Neckwear that is blowing in the wind, floating in midair, or otherwise not being held down by gravity.
wiki.bird hair ornament: A hair ornament or hairclip shaped like a bird.
wiki.ghost hair ornament: A hair ornament or hairclip shaped like a ghost.
wiki.multicolored necktie: A necktie that has two or more distinct colors present in its design. See multicolored clothes for guidelines on what is considered multicolored.
wiki.balaclava: A balaclava, also known as a balaclava helmet or ski mask, is a form of headgear that covers the whole head, exposing only part of the face. Often only the eyes or eyes and mouth are left exposed. Typically worn by criminals, SWAT operators or conventional soldiers.
wiki.green brooch: A clasp or pin that typically has a gem attached, often secured to a piece of garment.
wiki.xiao guan (headdress): Xiao guan (lit. small guan) is an informal guan (Chinese headwear for men) which covers the topknot of hair and secured with either hair stick or chinstrap. It come in various shapes, as long as it is the size fitting to that of a topknot.
wiki.wide brim: A hat with a wider brim than an ordinary brimmed hat.
wiki.brown robe: A robe that is colored brown.
wiki.heart belt: A buckle in the shape of a heart.
wiki.purple headband: A headband that is colored purple.
wiki.character hood: When someone is wearing a hood designed to resemble another character. Also tag the character being imitated by the hood.
wiki.chest guard: A piece of armor or other protective covering that covers only the upper chest.
wiki.xiangyun: The traditional Chinese way of drawing (auspicious) clouds. Also known as yunwen or lucky clouds.
wiki.animal hair ornament: A hair ornament that takes the form of an animal.
wiki.glass slipper: A pair of shoes made out of glass, based off of the Cinderella (fairy tale) fairy tale where the heroine wears a pair of glass shoes to the royal ball, but must flee at midnight and accidentally leaves one behind. The prince uses the remaining shoe to identify Cinderella, since it can only fit her feet.
wiki.single knee boot: Wearing a knee boot on one leg, while the other leg is wearing either no footwear or footwear of a different length.
wiki.butterfly earrings: Earrings shaped to resemble a butterfly.
wiki.fur bikini: A bikini made of fur or faux fur. For a bikini with only fur outlining the edges, see fur-trimmed bikini.
wiki.shirt under dress: Ambiguous tag. Use pinafore dress or skirt set & vest instead.
wiki.gradient skirt: A skirt that has a noticeable gradient to it.
wiki.arm pouch: A small pouch worn on the arm.
wiki.red corset: A corset that is colored red.
wiki.see-through one-piece swimsuit: A one-piece swimsuit that is see-through because it is wet or transparent.
wiki.latex thighhighs: Thighhighs that are made of, or at least look like latex because of their shininess
wiki.bikini under shorts: A bikini bottom worn under shorts.
wiki.black bustier: A bustier that is colored black.
wiki.heart-shaped ornament: Any ornament bearing the shape of a heart that doesn't have a more specific tag for it.
wiki.black nightgown: A nightgown that is colored black.
wiki.aqua pants: Pants that have aqua (greenish blue) or turqouoise color.
wiki.lace-trimmed headwear: A hat or any other piece of headwear with lace trim.
wiki.aqua vest: A vest that is colored aqua
wiki.white hakama: A hakama that is colored white.
wiki.two-tone shorts: Multicolored shorts that have exactly two colors.
wiki.red tube top: A tube top that is red in color.
wiki.mortarboard: A square-shaped hat with a small tassel, worn during graduation ceremonies.
wiki.spider print: Clothing or an object with a spider printed on it.
wiki.wrist flower: One or more flowers worn on the wrist as an ornament.
wiki.fox hair ornament: A hair ornament shaped to resemble a fox, whether it’s just the face or a miniature replica of the entire animal.
wiki.bead choker: A choker comprised of beads strung together by a string.
wiki.crown hair ornament: A hair ornament or hairclip shaped like a crown.
wiki.zipper skirt: A skirt with a zipper, to make it easier to put on and take off the skirt.
wiki.orange tank top: A tank top that is colored orange.

wiki.horned hat: A hat with horns in its design.

wiki.horned mask: A mask that has fake horns attached.
wiki.multicolored halo: A halo with more 2 or more colors.

wiki.two-tone veil: A veil that is two-toned (two colours).
wiki.asymmetrical pants: Pants that have inequal leg length by design.
wiki.cuisses: A piece of medieval knight's armor worn to protect the thigh.
wiki.brown suit: A suit that is colored brown.
wiki.green trim: A green trim is present on clothing.
wiki.gold belt: A belt that is colored gold.
wiki.white armband: An armband that is white in color.
wiki.criss-cross straps: At least two straps on either an article of a character's clothing or on their own (such as wrappings on a character's arms or legs) crossing over with each other to make an X formation.
wiki.oxygen mask: A mask used to transfer oxygen or anesthesia gas from a storage tank to the lungs.
wiki.studded gloves: Gloves with metal studs, usually on the knuckles or the back of the hand.
wiki.vertical-striped vest: A vest that has vertical stripes.
wiki.two-tone vest: A multicolored vest that consists of exactly two colors.
wiki.colored eyepatch: An eyepatch that is not black or white.

wiki.two-tone panties: Multicolored panties that have exactly two colors.
wiki.pants under dress: Pants being worn under a dress.
wiki.cloud hair ornament: A hair ornament or hairclip shaped like a cloud.
wiki.lipstick ring: A ring of lipstick left around a penis by fellatio.
wiki.white slingshot swimsuit: A slingshot swimsuit that is colored white.
wiki.striped belt: A belt with a striped pattern.
wiki.spiked footwear: Deprecated tag. Use one of the tags below instead. → spiked boots, spiked shoes, spiked sandals
wiki.piano print: A cloth pattern mimicking the 12-step pattern of a piano keyboard.
wiki.pleated shirt: A shirt with multiple pleats. Do not use this tag for shirt darts, or simple back pleats near the shoulders.
wiki.red wrist cuffs: Wrist cuffs that are colored red.
wiki.baseball helmet: A helmet worn by batters on a baseball (sport) team to protect them from the hard impact of a baseball (object).
wiki.purple trim: An article of clothing with a purple-colored trim around at least one of its edges.
wiki.swimsuit skirt: A type of one-piece swimsuit design that incorporates a skirt.
wiki.green camisole: A camisole that is mainly in green color
wiki.black pouch: Broad term for various small containers usually made from leather, textiles, or plastic. Objects called pouches include: • A small non-rigid bag usually with a drawstring for holding or carrying things. • A small semi-rigid container closed with a zipper.
wiki.just shoes: A nude person wearing only their shoes and socks.
wiki.collared leotard: A leotard with a folded collar.
wiki.captive bead ring: A ring piercing with a bead that fits into a small opening in the circle of the ring.
wiki.classic lolita: A style of Lolita fashion heavily based on historical fashion. It tends to have a "mature/elegant" Victorian look to it.
wiki.carrot print: Clothing or an object with at least one carrot printed on it.
wiki.gradient kimono: A specific type of kimono that gradually changes from one color to one or more other colors.
wiki.motoyui: A type of traditional Japanese ponytail holder or hair tie; may be a hair tube if notably elongated.
wiki.plaid apron: An apron featuring a plaid pattern.
wiki.o-ring panties: A pair of panties that have an o-ring keeping them together, typically at the sides.
wiki.knit hat: A warm hat made of wool or synthetic fibers intended to provide warmth in cold weather. Typically, knitted caps have simple, tapered structures, but there are many variants.
wiki.grey robe: A robe that is colored grey.
wiki.print hairband: A hairband that has any type of printed patterns on it.
wiki.polka dot bowtie: A bowtie with a polka dot pattern.
wiki.yellow cloak: A cloak that is colored yellow.
wiki.metal gloves: A glove made of metal that cannot be classified as gauntlets, studded gloves, mechanical hands, or any other known armor type.
wiki.yellow jumpsuit: A jumpsuit that is colored yellow.
wiki.bandaid on shoulder: A bandaid on a person's shoulder.
wiki.lemon print: Clothing or objects that have lemon printed on them.
wiki.pinstripe vest: A vest with a pinstripe pattern.
wiki.blue corset: A corset that is colored blue.
wiki.character mask: A mask that is designed to look like a specific character.
wiki.hockey mask: A mask used by ice hockey goalkeepers to protect their face from stray pucks. The original design has fallen out of favor for caged helmets worn nowadays, but it lives on in fiction and artwork, notably as Jason Voorhees' signature item.
wiki.armored skirt: A skirt plated with some armor, or is entirely made out of metal.
wiki.wool: The fine soft curly or wavy hair forming the coat of a sheep, goat, or similar animal, especially when shorn and prepared for use in making cloth or yarn.
wiki.crown of thorns: A crown made of thorns, most associated with the crucifixion of Jesus.
wiki.long hoodie: A hoodie that goes lower than the waist and is sometimes worn as a dress, with no lower garment.
wiki.paw print soles: Socks, shoes, or thighhighs with a paw print design on the soles.
wiki.skull hat ornament: A hat ornament shaped like a skull or skull and crossbones.
wiki.mascot costume: A costume that covers the wearer's face, depicting a mascot. Often designed with bright colors and cute features to appeal to children, and can be found at amusement parks, sports games, concerts, and conventions.
wiki.green suit: A suit that is colored green.
wiki.purple arm warmers: Arm warmers that are colored purple.
wiki.sleeping bag: An insulated covering for a person that can be closed with a zipper or similar means to form a tube, which functions as a portable bedding in situations where a person is sleeping outdoors, like camping.
wiki.waraji: Sandals made from straw rope that in the past were the standard footwear of the common people in Japan. Now they are mostly worn by traditional Buddhist monks. Unlike zouri, the treads are tied up to ankles with straw ropes.
wiki.print pajamas: A set of pajamas that have any type of printings on them.
wiki.spiked belt: A belt with spikes on it.
wiki.dolphin hair ornament: A hair ornament or hairclip shaped like a dolphin.
wiki.wrist belt: A belt worn on the wrist as a bracelet.
wiki.padded jacket: A jacket filled with material without distinct separation of cells. Horizontal rectangular cells should instead be tagged down jacket and square cells quilted jacket.
wiki.brown hakama: A hakama that is colored brown.
wiki.pink sarong: A sarong that is colored pink. A signature element of Nico Robin's post-timeskip design.
wiki.hip armor: Armor on the hips. For more proper terms see List of armor.
wiki.liquid halo: A halo that is made of a liquid, such as blood or water.
wiki.single elbow pad: When a character is wearing elbow pads on only one elbow.
wiki.spurs: A metal tool worn on the heels of cowboy boots or riding boots to help get the horse moving. They usually take the form of round metal wheels with dull spikes.
wiki.onigiri print: Clothing or an object that has one or more onigiri printed on it.
wiki.aqua scrunchie: A scrunchie that is colored aqua.
wiki.ribbon-trimmed shirt: A shirt with ribbon trim around the edges. Usually recognizable as a dotted line along the edge of the shirt.
wiki.black sarong: A sarong that is colored black.
wiki.wireless earphones: Earphones, often earbuds, that use Bluetooth (or another radio communication system) to function without wires. Some wireless earphones include small integrated microphones so they can be used for communications in much the same way as a headset.
wiki.brown bodysuit: A bodysuit that is colored brown.
wiki.spiked anklet: An anklet with one or more spikes atatched.
wiki.print apron: An apron that has any kind of printed design on it.
wiki.green sports bra: A sports bra that is green.
wiki.dinosaur costume: A costume based off a dinosaur. Also applies to character dolls depicting characters wearing such costumes.
wiki.flower hairpin: A hairclip with a flower as its primary design.
wiki.furisode sleeves: Dangling sleeves similar to those on a furisode, but attached to a garment that is not a furisode. Do not use this tag with actual furisode kimonos, although it can be used with short kimonos or kimono tops worn with hakama.
wiki.spiked helmet: A character's helmet that has spikes on it. Can be historical helmets such as the German pickelhaube, or fantasy helmets with spikes on them.
wiki.floating hair ornament: A piece of headgear (an assorted head accessory) that floats near the head of a character. Sometimes similar to a hair ornament, but not actually part of the hair.
wiki.underworld (ornament): This tag refers to the red orb that Hecatia Lapislazuli has on her hat in her default form.
wiki.multicolored pants: A pair of pants that have at least two or more colors present. See multicolored clothes for guidelines on what is considered multicolored.
wiki.barding: Armour for horses and other mounts. Use this tag for any armour on an animal meant for riding, including just a simple face or chest guard. Some of them are decorated.
wiki.layered gloves: Multiple gloves worn on top of each other.
wiki.undone bra: A bra that has been opened from the front or the back, usually via a clasp, hook, or tie between the cups.
wiki.unworn crown: A crown is present in the image, but is not being worn. This is different from floating crown because it's implied that it's being worn there, whereas it isn't here.
wiki.side-tie dress: Either: • A sideless dress that is held together with laces, strings, or ties along the sides. It may be cross-laced or straight-laced. • A dress that has laces on the sides tied into bows.
wiki.hannya: A Noh mask from traditional Japanese theater, representing women who have been consumed by jealousy or obsession.
wiki.gradient jacket: A jacket with a gradient on it.
wiki.underwear writing: Underwear with text written along the elasticated bands. Most commonly seen on sports bras, sports panties, and male underwear imitating the Calvin Klein-brand.
wiki.pankou: The frog button toggles used to fasten traditional Chinese outfits like the tangzhuang and qipao.
wiki.grey hakama: A hakama that is colored grey.
wiki.victorian maid: A maid from the Victorian era, the period of Queen Victoria's reign from 1837 to 1901. Victorian maids are characterized by a long apron and long dress, accompanied with a mob cap. A classic example is Emma (victorian romance emma) from Victorian Romance Emma.
wiki.bone print: An article of clothing or anything made out of fabric that has the printed motif of bones.
wiki.arm out of sleeve: A sleeved top, such as a shirt or jacket, worn with one arm outside of the sleeves.
wiki.purple camisole: A camisole that is mainly in purple color
wiki.brown-tinted eyewear: Tinted eyewear with a brown tint.
wiki.sleeveless duster: A duster (not to be confused with duster, the cleaning tool), is a "loose-fitting long coat".
wiki.dou: The breastplate in traditional Japanese armor worn by samurai. It's made up of iron and/or leather plates (kusazuri) of varied sizes and shapes hanging both on its front and back.
wiki.naked paint: Wearing only bodypaint while otherwise nude. See painted clothes for bodypaint made to look like clothing.
wiki.purple corset: A corset that is colored purple.
wiki.anna miller: A chain of restaurants in Hawaii and Japan. The first branch opened in 1973 in Hawaii, then expanded to 25 locations in Japan later that year.
wiki.hooded shirt: A shirt with an attached hood. Not to be confused with a hoodie, which for Danbooru tagging purposes is a hooded sweatshirt or sweater.
wiki.purple armband: An armband that is purple in color.
wiki.undone neckerchief: A neckerchief that has been untied and is hanging around the wearer's neck.
wiki.clothes in front: Holding a piece of clothing in front of one's body to see how it would look without actually wearing it.
wiki.unworn slippers: Slippers that currently aren't being worn.
wiki.cycling uniform: A type of sportswear worn when riding a bicycle, especially when racing. Uniforms consist of a bike jersey, short bike shorts, gloves, a bicycle helmet, and sneakers.
wiki.red blindfold: A blindfold that is not black or white. Use this tag for unusual blindfold colors.
wiki.naked chocolate: A nude character that's covered in liquid chocolate.
wiki.battle damage: A visible sign of damage on the vehicle, mechas, or object done in the course of fighting.
wiki.bell-bottoms: Pants, most commonly jeans, that widen at the bottom, typically starting at the knees. Also known as flares. When they widen from the ankles only, it may also be called a boot-cut.
wiki.whale hat: An animal hat based on a whale, often worn by Okunoda Miyoi.
wiki.breast zipper: A zipper which lies directly above the breasts, over the nipples. Usually found on an outfit also including a crotch zipper.
wiki.monocle chain: A chain, string, or wire connected to a monocle intended to be connected to the wearer's clothing to prevent the monocle from being able to fall to the ground and damaging it. Despite its intended purpose to protect the monocle, they're commonly depicted dangling with a hanging ornament on the end instead.
wiki.earphones removed: A pair of earphones in the image is not being worn by anyone. If one side is being worn but not the other, use single earphone removed instead.
wiki.detached pants: Like detached sleeves, but on the legs.
wiki.whale tail (clothing): When the top of one's thong can be seen over the rear waistline of the pants, forming what looks like a whale's tail.
wiki.yellow armor: Armor that is colored yellow or gold.
wiki.tote bag: A distinctly large bag used for carrying a number of items.
wiki.frilled sash: Sash which has frills on it.
wiki.paw hair ornament: A hair ornament in the shape of a paw.
wiki.sleeve rolled up: The singular version of sleeves rolled up, used when only one sleeve is rolled up/is visible.
wiki.ghost print: Clothing or an object with the printed motif of ghosts.
wiki.pleated sleeves: Sleeves with vertical folds of fabric, like a pleated skirt but on the arms.
wiki.food on clothes: Food on someone's clothes, often due to spilling or dropping food or being a messy eater.
wiki.headwear with attached mittens: Hat or hood with attached mittens or gloves.
wiki.see-through shawl: A shawl that is made of transparent material.
wiki.unworn cape: A cape that a character normally wears is present in the image but not being worn.
wiki.undone sarashi: When the bandages (or any other wrappings) of a sarashi is untied or loosened up.
wiki.single earphone removed: Someone is wearing one side of a pair of earphones, but not the other; either to increase audibility of their surroundings, or to offer that side to someone else.
wiki.purple suit: A suit that is colored purple.
wiki.orange bandana: A bandana that is colored orange.
wiki.cat choker: A choker bearing some kind of cat motif in its design. This may include a cat o-ring or some cat-shaped attachment.
wiki.dress ribbon: Ribbon tied to a dress. Can be a long ribbon that goes fully around the dress, that when tied right under the breasts counts as underbust.
wiki.ribbon-trimmed bra: A bra with ribbon trim around the edges. Usually recognizable as a dotted line along the edge of the bra.
wiki.skull belt: A belt with a skull design, either on the buckle or on the belt itself.
wiki.multicolored shorts: A pair of shorts that have at least two different colors present on their design. See multicolored clothes for detailed guidelines on what is considered multicolored.
wiki.collared shrug: A shrug_(clothing) with an attached collar; think of a detached collar that spans the shoulders at minimum, and covers a majority of the arms at maximum.
wiki.socks over pantyhose: Any kind of socks worn over pantyhose.
wiki.leg cutout: Term used for describing clothing for the leg that has openings as part of the design to expose bare skin.
wiki.gradient sleeves: Shirt sleeves that have a noticeable gradient to it.
wiki.shibari under clothes: Wearing shibari-style bondage under the clothes.
wiki.purple sweater vest: A sweater vest that is colored purple.
wiki.naked necktie: Where the character is nude but wearing a long necktie that runs down the front torso. Often employed as convenient censoring for males.
wiki.wolf cut: A hairstyle that has more hair volume on top, and thinned-out hair starting at the base of the neck. It is typically cut more wildly, resembling a wolf's mane.
wiki.hair extensions: Pieces of (often synthetic) hair that are clipped or sewn in to add fullness or length to one's existing hair.
wiki.ring hair extensions: Hair extensions that fasten to the hair through a ring hair ornament or short chain. Serves as both a hair accessory and hair extensions.
wiki.sidelocks tied back: Long sidelocks that are tied back to join a (possibly unseen) hair bun or ponytail at the back of the head. If pulled straight back and taut they don't qualify as being sidelocks, so some amount of slack is required, such that they drape in a U-shape on either side of the head.
wiki.fluffy hair: Hair that is fluffy. As a general rule, if the hair has a lot of volume and looks as though it would be very soft to the touch, then it's likely fluffy hair.
wiki.hair vines: Vines worn on the hair as a decorative element.
wiki.fanged bangs: Bangs with long tendrils on the sides, giving the appearance of hair "fangs" framing the face. The "fangs" are basically extensions of the outer edges of the bangs.
wiki.bun with braided base: A hair bun with a braid wrapped around the base.
wiki.shuangyaji: A Chinese women's hairstyle which consists of two hair buns or hair rings, sometimes braided. It resembles two small coils on the top of the head or beside the forehead; sometimes resembling bow-shaped hair. During the Song Dynasty in China, it was common for maids and young girls to wear such hairstyle.
wiki.plant hair: Hair that is composed of plant matter, typically leaves.
wiki.quad braids: A hairstyle that consists of four braided lengths of hair.
wiki.beehive hairdo: A hairstyle in which long hair is piled up in a conical shape on the top of the head and slightly backwards pointing, giving some resemblance to the shape of a traditional beehive.
wiki.tall hair: Hair that extends a considerable distance above the character's head.
wiki.balding: When a character isn't quite bald but retains little enough hair around their cranium to qualify as balding.
wiki.nihongami: Historical Japanese hairstyles that traditionally denoted an aspect of the wearer's identity, such as their age, societal status or marital status.
wiki.single drill: Like twin drills, but just a singular ponytail or side ponytail made out of drill hair.
wiki.translucent hair: Hair which allows light to pass through its otherwise solid areas.
wiki.butterfly-shaped pupils: When a character's pupils are shaped like butterflies.
wiki.official alternate eye color: Alternate eye colors of official origin.
wiki.lazy eye: When one eye is looking in the wrong direction. This may be an artistic error, a medical condition (which is usually strabismus) or a sign of the character's craziness.
wiki.orange pupils: A character has orange pupils in their eyes instead of the standard black.
wiki.white mouth: When the inside of a character's open mouth is plain white. A notable feature of Yua Serufu.
wiki.pink sclera: Where the sclera - the white part of the eye - is colored pink.
wiki.missing eye: A character with a single missing eye, made visible by an empty eye socket.
wiki.glowing mouth: When the inside of the mouth is glowing. Often seen on demonic and mechanical characters, and characters breathing fire or charging /firing an energy beam from their mouth (post #1010988).
wiki.purple sclera: When the normally white part of the eye is colored purple.
wiki.grey sclera: When the normally white part of the eye is colored grey.
wiki.smeared lipstick: Lipstick that is smudged across its wearer's face. A common consequence of passionate kissing or fellatio, but it can also be due to nonsexual activities like eating, wiping mouth or a making a mistake applying lipstick.
wiki.triangle-shaped pupils: When a character's pupils are shaped like a triangle.
wiki.aqua lips: A character or person depicted has aqua colored lips.
wiki.green tongue: A tongue that is colored green. If a character has their mouth open and the rest of the mouth is also green, that can count under this tag.
wiki.single blush sticker: When a character has only one blush sticker visible.
wiki.gradient nails: Fingernails and/or toenails that feature a color gradient.
wiki.yellow lips: When a character's lips are colored yellow from lipstick.
wiki.aqua pupils: A character has aqua pupils in their eyes instead of the standard black. Due to the subjective nature of color judgment and other factors (such as the lighting on the characters) there is an overlap between this tag, the blue pupils, and the green pupils tags.
wiki.yellow teeth: Teeth with a yellow hue. May or may not be due to poor dental hygiene.
wiki.sweaty armpits: Armpits that are covered in sweat, typically due to heat, physical activity and/or nervousness.
wiki.gauze on cheek: A gauze on a character's cheek(s).
wiki.thick chest hair: Thick patches of chest hair covering most of the characters chest. In stylized depictions it may have the same consistency as fur or head hair.
wiki.outie navel: A navel that outwardly protrudes from the stomach. The opposite of a normal "innie" navel, which is sunken into the stomach.
wiki.mark under both eyes: A facial mark that appears under both of a character's eyelids, or in some cases, directly on the bottom eyelids.
wiki.winged heart tattoo: A tattoo in the shape of a winged heart.
wiki.medium sideburns: Sideburns that go pass the mid section of the ear, but do not reach the jaw bone like long sideburns.
wiki.alternate body size: Ambiguous tag. Use one of the following: → taller than canon, shorter than canon, fatter than canon, more muscular than canon, thinner than canon, alternate breast size (larger), alternate breast size (smaller), alternate ass size (larger)
wiki.black hands: Hands that are colored black, differently than the rest of the character's skin.
wiki.thick arm hair: Arm Hair that is thick or dense in volume.
wiki.blood on chest: Blood that is on somebody's chest.
wiki.disembodied eye: One or more eyes that are not physically attached to a character's body. Typically associated with supernatural beings like youkai, demons, eldritch abominations, etc.
wiki.scar on back: A scar located on a character's back.
wiki.sparse navel hair: Light patches of hair found in the stomach region.
wiki.circle facial mark: A facial mark in the shape of a circle.
wiki.asymmetrical arms: When a character's arms are physically asymmetrical. Often used to comedically imply a character masturbates a lot by giving them a single exaggeratedly muscular arm.
wiki.sparse arm hair: Arm hair that is thin or sparse in density.
wiki.scar on shoulder: A scar located on a person's shoulder.
wiki.scars all over: A character with scars all over their body. Don't use when only a small part of the skin is visible.
wiki.aroused nosebleed: When a character has a nosebleed because they are comically aroused, often exaggerated to an absurd degree and almost always played for laughs.
wiki.organs: Internal viscera that are exposed for the viewer to see.
wiki.sparse leg hair: Leg hair that isn't concentrated and is lacking in volume. Might be depicted as sparse lines. (post #7696578).
wiki.very hairy: Body hair that is thick, fur-like, and/or covers most of the body.
wiki.arrow in body: When an arrow is embedded inside someone's body, often in the chest or in the back.
wiki.triangle facial mark: A facial mark shaped like a triangle ( ▲ ▼ ► ◄ ◤ ◢ ).
wiki.alternate facial hair: Characters who are drawn with a facial hair style different from their default one. A common example of this is Ryu (street fighter) from Street fighter.
wiki.long fingers: A distinct emphasis on the length of a person's fingers. This could be intentional or an artist error in drawing the hands.
wiki.hole in chest: A literal hole in the character's chest. Often associated with heart out of chest. Not to be confused with a cleavage cutout.
wiki.paint on body: Paint spattered or smeared on the bare skin of a person's body.
wiki.long arms: A character’s arms are longer than normal human proportions by design.
wiki.bruised eye: Bruising around the eye. Often includes swelling that makes it hard to keep the eye fully open.
wiki.v-taper: A muscular physique featuring a broad upper back and shoulders with a narrow waist, creating a V-shaped body.
wiki.skeletal hand: A hand that consists exclusively of bone, while other parts of the body consist of flesh or even mechabare.
wiki.bite mark on neck: A bite mark on someone's neck.
wiki.bursting pectorals: A male-specific wardrobe malfunction caused by an outfit ill-fitted to a boy's larger pectorals. Situations can include the boy's outfit stretching very tightly around his chest, pectoral overhang on a top, or buttons or another fastening accessory flying off his outfit as the fabric tears.
wiki.deep wound: A particularly deep and/or wide injury that starts to reveal features beneath the surface of the skin.
wiki.big head: When the character's head is propotionally large compared to the rest of the body. Typically seen on an extreme form of chibi art where the character's head were drawn larger in size than the entire body, usually to emphasize their expressions.
wiki.severed arm: An arm that has been severed from its body.
wiki.scar on tail: A scar located somewhere on a character's tail.
wiki.thick leg hair: Leg hair which is thick and covers most of the leg, in more stylized depictions it can look like patches of fur.
wiki.bleeding from forehead: Bleeding from the forehead, or from some unspecified place hidden by hair, so that the blood flows into the forehead region.
wiki.cleft chin: A chin where the bone splits down the middle in a distinctive cleft. Sometimes colloquially referred to as a "butt chin", it is stereotypically associated with strength and extreme masculinity.
wiki.alternate height: Ambiguous tag. Use either taller than canon or shorter than canon.
wiki.hand hair: Body hair grown on the hands.
wiki.single bare arm: When only one arm is bare, while the other is at least 3/4 covered.
wiki.finger tattoo: A tattoo located on the fingers.
wiki.ass hair: Body hair on the subject's ass.
wiki.long mustache: A lengthy or voluminous mustache. Must extend past the cheekbones if the mustache defies gravity; or must reach to or past the chin if it follows more realistic depictions. For mustaches that reach to the wearer's nipple line or longer, see very long mustache.
wiki.bursting ass: When the ass is too big and causes tight or undersized clothes to burst, or looks like it's about to burst or pop out at any moment.
wiki.personification: When a non-human entity, such as an inanimate object, animal, creature, vehicle, etc, is depicted as a human or humanoid.
wiki.mecha musume: The anthropomorphization of hardware of all kinds (mecha) as cute girls (musume). Popular for military hardware, but also cars, trains, game consoles, etc. Closely related to the OS-tan phenomenon.
wiki.multiple persona: Three or more different versions of the same character appearing together in the same scene. Like dual persona, but with more than two characters.
wiki.humanization: A humanoid character (android, furry, monster girl, humanoid mecha, elf, etc.) depicted as an ordinary human.
wiki.panther ears: Characters who have ears of a black panther (basically a leopard ears or a jaguar ears which are colored in black).
wiki.eastern dragon horns: A style of horns commonly seen on East Asian mythological creatures such as a eastern dragon or a qilin (mythology). They are categorized as horns but do not resemble traditional animal horns or western dragon horns. They branch like antlers but are thicker and straighter.
wiki.panther girl: A girl with black panther-like features, such as panther ears or a panther tail. Usually with black fur, especially with furry characters.
wiki.japan national police: Japan's national police force. Unlike the national police from various other countries, they do not have jurisdictions of their own. They are instead responsible for supervising every prefectural police department in the country.
wiki.yellow feathers: Feathers that are yellow, don't use this tag if they are attached to wings.
wiki.hyena ears: Animal ears resembling those of a hyena.
wiki.single ear down: When a character with animal ears that would normally point upwards has lowered one of their ears.
wiki.step-siblings: Siblings who are not related by blood but by the union of their parents.
wiki.panther tail: A character with a tail of a black panther.
wiki.eastern dragon tail: The tail of an eastern dragon. The back of the tail is usually covered in fur and there is a tuft of hair at the tip.
wiki.dragon ears: The ears of a dragon girl or dragon boy.
wiki.red scales: Scales that are red in color.
wiki.hedgehog girl: Girls with intrinsic hedgehog features, such as quills, hedgehog ears or a hedgehog tail.
wiki.chest tuft: A patch of protruding fur on chest. Usually associated with furry due to amount of body fur.
wiki.two-tone wings: Wings that feature two colors. Can also apply with sides on the wings having different colors.
wiki.halfling: A humanoid race found in a number of fantasy settings, most notably Dungeons & Dragons. They're physically similar to humans, except about half as tall and not as stocky as the similarly sized dwarves. They tend to be portrayed as stealthy and lucky, often classed as thieves or rogues.
wiki.fur-tipped tail: Normally furless (e.g., dragon) tails which have fur on the tips. Not to be used for tails which are completely furred.
wiki.green scales: Scales that are green in color.
wiki.large horns: Horns that are noticeably large relative to the character's head.
wiki.reptile boy: A boy with reptile traits, such as scales or a lizard tail.
wiki.drawn whiskers: Animal whiskers drawn on to a persons face as a virtual representation. Usually accompanied with drawn ears and commonly found through a face filter on phones.
wiki.brown feathers: Feathers that are brown, don't use this tag if they are attached to wings.
wiki.mimic: A type of fantasy monster that lures unsuspecting victims to their doom by taking another appearance, most often a treasure chest, but may take other forms as well.
wiki.komainu ears: Use a better tag such as dog ears or lion ears depending on what the ears actually look like.
wiki.chipmunk girl: A girl with real chipmunk characteristics, such as squirrel ears or a squirrel tail.
wiki.yuki onna: Yuki-onna (雪女, lit. snow woman) is a traditional youkai in Japanese mythology. She is often depicted as a tall, beautiful woman with long hair that appears during snowy nights, with inhumanly pale or even transparent skin that blends in with the snow and gives her a ghostly appearance.
wiki.jaguar girl: A girl with jaguar-like features, such as jaguar ears or a jaguar tail.
wiki.golem: In Jewish folklore, a golem is an artificial being made from inanimate matter, traditionally clay or mud, which is then animated by supernatural means. The resulting entity is physically robust and can be directed to perform work, but is usually not fully sapient; lacking both initiative and common sense.
wiki.red panda ears: Characters who have animal ears based off of a red panda.
wiki.hedgehog boy: A boy with real hedgehog features, such as quills, hedgehog ears or a hedgehog tail.
wiki.spines: Stiff, pointed appendages on an animal, as the quills of a porcupine, or the sharp, bony rays in the fin of a fish.
wiki.hook hand: A prosthetic hook replacing a lost hand. It may be a prop, or an actual replacement for the hand. Popularly associated with pirates due to Captain Hook, which Crocodile (one Piece) directly parodies.
wiki.pink feathers: Feathers that are pink, don't use this tag if they are attached to wings.
wiki.intertwined tails: Use when tails are intertwined around one another. → tails touching, heart tail, heart tail duo
wiki.screw in head: A screw or bolt (hardware) that goes through (or appears to go through) a character's head. Commonly seen on depictions of Frankenstein's monster.
wiki.huge horns: Horns that are much bigger than the head of the character they belong to.
wiki.mimic chest: A type of fantasy monster and the most commonly depicted form of mimic. It lures unsuspecting victims to their doom by taking the appearance of a treasure chest.
wiki.extra legs: A character with more legs than normal.
wiki.tiefling: A fictional humanoid race in the Dungeons & Dragons tabletop role-playing game. They are human-based 'planetouched', native outsiders that were infused with the touch of the fiendish planes (typically devils).
wiki.electric plug tail: A type of cable tail with an electric plug at the end.
wiki.train conductor: The leader of a train's crew, responsible for overseeing and managing the operation of the train.
wiki.chipmunk tail: Use this tag when a character has a tail of a squirrel. → tail, squirrel, squirrel ears
wiki.hyena boy: A boy with hyena traits such as hyena ears or a hyena tail.
wiki.blue scales: Scales that are blue in color.
wiki.prince: The son of a king and/or queen. The female equivalent is a princess.
wiki.orca girl: A girl with orca-like features such as black and white skin and an orca tail.
wiki.tendril: They aren't quite tentacles but they're not vines either.
wiki.tree horns: Horns or antlers that resemble branches and twigs. To further emphasize this, there can be leaves, flowers or fruit growing on them.
wiki.accidental pervert: When a person does a perverted action by accident. The (un)lucky victim will often come into contact with the person in an unlikely accident. The victim may or may not be an actual pervert.
wiki.food-themed creature: An animal or creature based on an item of food.
wiki.moth wings: Having wings like that of a moth.
wiki.giraffe ears: Characters who have animal ears based off of a giraffe.
wiki.drawn wings: Wings drawn behind or beside a character's body to give them the appearance of having wings.
wiki.dj: In context, this tag refers to characters doing the work of disc jockeys working in clubs or discos, rearranging, playing, and spinning vinyl records on turntables, as opposed to radio DJs who are voice announcers who play songs, not necessarily those recorded in vinyl.
wiki.fujoshi: A fujoshi (lit. rotten girl) is an overzealous female fan of yaoi. They are stereotypically portrayed as female perverts with coke-bottle glasses.
wiki.core: An opaque ball or other object that might be a control center, usually found in slimes or something else transparent/translucent.
wiki.mismatched wings: A single character with a mismatched pair of wings.
wiki.snow leopard girl: A girl with real snow leopard characteristics, such as snow leopard ears or a snow leopard tail.
wiki.two-tone horns: Horns that have two distinct colors.
wiki.jackal boy: A boy with jackal-like features, such as jackal ears and/or a jackal tail.
wiki.forward facing horns: Horns that face towards the front of the head.
wiki.imperial japanese navy: Posts containing references to the real life Imperial Japanese Navy, such as depictions of historical events, ships, or sailors with clear evidence of the colors or uniforms of Imperial Japan.
wiki.hand between legs: Ambiguous tag. → between legs, hand between own legs, arms between legs, arm between another's legs
wiki.4-finger heart hands: Heart hands made with only four fingers.
wiki.on rock: When a character is on a rock, boulder or any rock-like object, regardless if they're lying, sitting, squatting, standing, and such.
wiki.swinging: Deprecated. Use one of these instead: • An act of motion while suspended or on an axis. • swinging arm • swinging arms • swinging legs • swinging object • A rapid motion while holding an object. • swinging baseball bat • swinging golf club • swinging weapon • Swinging while on an axis-suspended object.
wiki.cropped head: A character that has been drawn so that only their head, neck, and potentially collarbone are visible. Do not use if the character is merely out of frame; the head should be visibly disconnected and floating on its own.
wiki.gun to head: See gun to own head or gun to another's head. → gun to own head, gun to another's head, at gunpoint
wiki.gyaru v: An upside-down V gesture, with the V pointing down and the palm facing out.
wiki.offering hand: A hand being offered to you, the viewer. Usually a prelude to holding hands, a handshake, being helped up off the ground, or a dance invitation. If both hands are offered, consider hugging viewer, carry me or outstretched arms instead.
wiki.helmet over eyes: A character's helmet is covering their eyes, but not the rest of their face.
wiki.powering up: When a character is readying an energy attack, casting a spell, or performing some other act that has a visual manifestation of their focusing energy, usually with the implication that this energy is going to be used offensively.
wiki.hands on another's waist: When both of a character's hands are on another character's waist, on the side of the stomach.
wiki.hands on own chin: When a character has both of their hands on their own chin, often as a form of head rest.
wiki.band (music): A group of people who gather together to produce music.
wiki.mask lift: When a mask is lifted up from its normal position.
wiki.hands on another's back: When both a character's hands are on another character's back.
wiki.flirting: The act of making romantic advances towards someone else.
wiki.heart hands failure: When two characters form a heart hands duo pose, but one responds with a different gesture, such as a thumbs up, a victory sign or even a middle finger instead.
wiki.sitting on branch: Sitting on a branch. Usually the branch is from a tree, but sometimes the branch is independent.
wiki.sway back: A character standing while leaning back without support.
wiki.catching: The act of grabbing someone or something before they can fall to the ground.
wiki.mugshot: A photo taken by police to keep records of arrested persons and criminals. The suspect is usually holding a sign in front of a wall with height marks.
wiki.bag over head: A bag pulled down all over the head.
wiki.hand on hand: Ambiguous tag. Use one of the following tags instead: • hand on another's hand • own hands together • holding hands
wiki.arms on knees: Resting both forearms on the knees.
wiki.henshin pose: The pose a character strikes before they transform, mostly associated with Kamen Riders and/or Precures.
wiki.waving arm: The motion of waving one's hand or arm as if saying "Hi!", "Bye!", or "Over here!".
wiki.book on lap: A book resting on a character's lap.
wiki.mask over one eye: A mask that only covers one eye. The covered eye might be completely obscured, or there can be a slit to allow the wearer to look through. Note that this should not be used for an eyepatch.
wiki.front-to-back: Two characters next to each other, with the front of one against the back of the other.
wiki.arms on table: Resting both forearms on top of a table.
wiki.pointing down: A character is pointing at least one finger downwards, indicating for the viewer to glance down.
wiki.toothbrush in mouth: When a character is holding a toothbrush in their mouth, usually whilst brushing their teeth.
wiki.reaching towards another: Reaching in the direction of someone else.
wiki.typing: The process of writing or inputting text by pressing keys on a typewriter, computer keyboard, cellphone, or similar device.
wiki.x arms: A gesture in which the arms are crossed in front of the chest to form an X shape.
wiki.adjusting footwear: A character is adjusting at least one of the footwear they're wearing.
wiki.object floating above hand: Something floating above a character's hand(s); can either be something intangible, such as an orb, heart or a star symbol, in which a character might be casting a spell - or it might be a physical object, in which it might occur due to telekinesis.
wiki.multiple hands: For posts with many disembodied hands, see surrounded by hands.
wiki.on water: A person is atop a body of water, usually by being partially submerged in a low pool, or being afloat on an innertube.
wiki.rubbing: To move two or more things back and forth upon each other using friction and pressure.
wiki.arm on table: Resting one forearm on a table. Often appears alongside elbow on table when the other elbow is also resting on the table.
wiki.cat's cradle: A game played with a loop of string resulting in a cat's cradle between the fingers of two (or more) people.
wiki.hiding behind another: One character is hiding behind another, possibly from fear or shyness. See human shield for an occasionally overlapping concept.
wiki.removing eyewear: Removing glasses or sunglasses from the character's face. The eyewear should be visibly held, close to the face.
wiki.riding animal: Riding on the back of an animal, other than a horse or horse-like creature (for that, see horseback riding).
wiki.hugging another's leg: Clinging to or hugging another person's leg.
wiki.chocolate on face: Melted chocolate spattered on a person's face.
wiki.hands on floor: Placing both hands on the ground or floor. This includes both indoors and outdoors, and when the floor is not drawn by the artist (an invisible floor).
wiki.sitting on animal: When someone sits on top of an animal, not necessarily for travel.
wiki.racing: A competition in which people compete to go around a racetrack in the fastest time. This includes running, swimming, horse racing, car racing, etc.
wiki.head on table: Someone is resting their head atop a table.
wiki.on crescent: Standing, sitting, lying, kneeling, squatting, or similar on a crescent shape item or a fantasy crescent moon.
wiki.fake video: A fake screenshot of a video, or of a video hosting website, such as Youtube or Niconico.
wiki.nuzzle: Pressing or rubbing one's face against another person as a sign of affection. Cats are known to do this.
wiki.collar grab: Grabbing someone by the collar of their shirt, whether in anger to attack them or in passion to kiss them.
wiki.apologizing: When a character offers an apology to be forgiven (sometimes with a dogeza).
wiki.smelling flower: The act of smelling a flower by bringing them near one’s nose.
wiki.cracking knuckles: Manipulating the knuckles to produce a sharp cracking sound. Cracked knuckles on the hands are common, but other joints can be cracked such as the wrists, feet, elbows, and knees.
wiki.hands on another's stomach: When one character has both of their hands on someone else's abdominal region.
wiki.arms around back: Both arms wrapped around someone's back.
wiki.peeling: Can imply one of two things:
wiki.w over eye: When the character makes a w symbol over their own eye or face.
wiki.sliding: The act of slipping across a surface either due to friction or the surface is at an angle.
wiki.carrying overhead: Carrying an object or person above one's head.
